articles.title: Getting Started, Platform Basics and Integrations
articles.module: Getting Started, Platform Basics and Integrations

blocks.x: Adit is an all-in-one practice platform for dental, orthodontic, optometry and chiropractic practices. It connects to the practice's EHR or practice management system (PMS) and syncs patients, appointments and related data so that Adit's modules can read from and write back to the practice's system.

On-premise EHRs connect through the Adit server application (Pozative.exe) installed on the office server, which uses a dedicated database user and admin-level credentials. Cloud EHRs connect through the Adit for Chrome browser extension, with a separate extension for each supported cloud EHR. This module covers that integration, how often Adit syncs, how to tell when the connection is down and how to reconnect, plus the everyday platform basics: navigation layout, global search, keyboard shortcuts, tables, the Create Request button, practice information, outgoing number, logs, system requirements, the Partner Dashboard and Adit Academy.

Articles in this module (23): Guide to Adit's Integration with Cloud-based EHRs; Guide to Adit's Partner Dashboard; Chrome Extensions for Cloud EHRs; Global Search Improvements; Guide to Adit Academy; Understanding Adit’s New Navigation Layout; What are Adit's minimum system requirements?; How to Edit Your Practice Information; How to Enable Adit as a Third-Party Integration in Crystal PM; Find your server app version; How to Find “Getting Started” Steps; How often does Adit Sync with my PMS and how do I manage this?; How To: Install the Adit browser extension for Chrome; Navigating and Customizing Tables in Adit; How to Set your Outgoing Number; How to Use the Create Request Button in Adit; Using Keyboard Shortcuts in Adit; How to view your logs within Adit; Why Adit needs login credentials and administrator-level access to your system; What does my Adit for Chrome extension's status mean?; Why does Adit create a user within my EHR (Patient Management System)?; How do I know if Adit is disconnected from my Practice Management Software (PMS/EHR); Troubleshooting: Reconnect your Adit for Chrome browser extension.

articles.title: Guide to Adit's Integration with Cloud-based EHRs
articles.module: Getting Started, Platform Basics and Integrations

blocks.x: Adit’s integration with cloud EHRs uses a browser extension for Google Chrome. This extension allows us to sync your patient and appointment information into the Adit platform, where you can then use our all-in-one solution to manage your practice, communicate with patients, and more!

In order for the integration to pick up your actions in your EHR and sync them to Adit, everyone in your practice must only use your EHR in the Chrome browser and must have the Adit for Chrome browser extension installed and running at all times.
The integration works using three distinct data syncs:
an initial database sync, which pulls all of your patient and appointment data into Adit,
an ongoing, real-time sync, which pulls any changes that you make to your patient or appointment data into Adit as they are made.
an ongoing, hourly backup sync, which pulls any changes that were missed by the real-time sync.
Initial Integration Setup

When you set up your integration, you will install the browser extension on one workstation and start the initial data sync. This sync may take 5-7 days to complete. You will also immediately install the browser extension on the rest of your workstations to ensure that changes made on those workstations can be synced to Adit in real time, even while the initial sync is processing in the background.
Before starting the initial sync, please keep the following important points in mind:
A user with admin-level permissions must be logged in to your EHR before installing the Adit browser extension and starting the initial sync.
The initial data sync will take 5-7 days to complete. During this time:
The EHR window can be minimized, but cannot be closed.
The computer must remain powered on and active. It cannot go to sleep, have the screen locked, or be logged off.
Your internet connection must remain stable for the entire duration.

The user who logged in to your EHR and started the sync cannot log in to any other workstation with the same user account. Ascend does not allow the same user to be logged in to multiple devices at the same time. If this is a problem for your team, we recommend creating a new user in your EHR and logging in with that account to start the initial sync.
You can continue to use your EHR and the workstation normally while the initial sync is running in the background.
Your EHR may normally timeout after 10 minutes of user inactivity; our sync will intentionally stop this from happening to preserve the integrity of your data.
Any failure to comply with the above points will cause the sync to fail and require you to re-start it again from the beginning.
For detailed instructions on how to install the Adit for Chrome extension on your workstations, please see How To: Install the Adit browser extension for Chrome.

We strongly recommend installing the Adit for Chrome extension on all of the workstations in your office to ensure there are no data discrepancies. The real-time sync only works when the Adit for Chrome extension is installed and running on the workstation, so that it can pick up changes made on that workstation in real time.

If you do not install the Adit for Chrome extension on all of your workstations, any changes made on a workstation without the extension will take an hour or more to sync, causing delays, data discrepancies, and interruptions to your automations (such as appointment reminders, patient forms, online scheduling, and more). In addition, there are currently two specific actions that will not sync at all if done on a workstation without the extension installed:
Deleting an appointment
Creating a new patient with a common name
Both of these actions will sync to Adit properly when done from a workstation that has the Adit for Chrome extension installed and logged in.

Once you have installed the Adit for Chrome extension on all of your workstations, you can work as normal while the initial sync continues in the background. Any changes made in your EHR on a workstation with the Adit for Chrome extension installed will be synced to Adit in real time.
Normal Daily Operation

Once the initial sync is complete, daily operation of the integration is very simple. As your team works in your EHR, the Adit for Chrome extension will pick up any changes they make and sync those to Adit.

Any workstations that have the Adit for Chrome extension installed and properly logged in will sync any changes they make in your EHR to Adit in real time. Workstations that do not have the Adit for Chrome installed or properly logged in will still have their changes picked up and synced, but there will be a delay before that data is visible in Adit as this backup sync is only done once per hour.

articles.title: Guide to Adit's Partner Dashboard
articles.module: Getting Started, Platform Basics and Integrations

blocks.x: Adit’s partner platform allows you to manage all your clients who use Adit from one singular access point.
How to Get Started

In order to get access to our partner platform, a representative from Adit’s team will send you an invitation via email. By accepting the invitation you will be redirected to https://partners.adit.com/ to create your account.
Once your account is created, you can add your first practice by selecting Request Access

In the pop up, add the Account ID of the practice you want to request access from. If you do not know the Practice’s Account ID, please contact the practice and direct them to this article here to locate their ID.
Next, select the users that will be able to access this practice’s Adit account, then select request access.
To learn more about how to add users to your partner account, click here.
The practice will then receive a request in their Adit account and can approve it accordingly. Once approved, you will get an email notification.
Managing Your Client Dashboard
Once a practice provides access to their Adit account, their information will be displayed in the Client dashboard.
The first column is Organization Name, which is the name of the Practice.
The second column is the Location of the practice. If there are multiple locations for a practice, they will show up in each row.
For Example:
ABC Dentistry (Houston)
ABC Dentistry (Austin)
ABC Dentistry (Dallas)
Clicking on the “eye” icon will open up that account
Adding Users To Your Account
You can add additional users to your partner account by clicking on the users tab in the top navigation bar.
Select Add User
In the pop up, enter in the following:
First Name
Last Name
Email
Password
Role :
Admin
Admin users will have the ability to invite, delete, and edit the settings of other user accounts in your partner account
Staff
Staff users will only be able to open up your client accounts that they have access to, also request access to other client accounts if they have the practice ID.
Managing Your Users
You can manage your existing users using the following Actions:
Edit
You can edit the Name, Email, Password, and Role of the user
Disable/Enable
This will disable/enable the user credentials accordingly
Delete
This will permanently delete the user from your partner account

articles.title: Global Search Improvements
articles.module: Getting Started, Platform Basics and Integrations

blocks.x: Global Search now finds messages, internal messages, tasks and settings, not just patients. You can also call or message a patient straight from the results.
Search and choose where to look
Type a name or keyword in the Search Patient box at the top of any page. Results are grouped by area, and View All opens the full list for that area.
Use the Searching dropdown to choose which areas to search. All areas are ticked by default, so untick the ones you do not need.
Filter the results
Select the filter icon at the end of the search box, choose your filters and select Apply.

rows: Due This Week or Due Next Week
Last 90 Days, or Between for your own date range

blocks.x: Call or message a patient
Each patient result has a Call icon and a Message icon. If the Call icon is greyed out, calling is not available for that patient. Hover over it to see why.
Search messages
Search by a patient's name or by words in a message. A name match opens the conversation in Engage. A word match opens it at that message, highlighted.
How far back

Search covers the last 90 days of text messages and 180 days of internal messages. For older text messages, set Message Date to Between in the filters. AI Web Chat is searched by the person's name only.
Open a settings page
Type a keyword such as appointment and a Settings section lists the matching settings pages. Select one to open it.
FAQs
Can I search only patients?
Yes. Open the Searching dropdown and untick everything except Patients.

articles.title: Guide to Adit Academy
articles.module: Getting Started, Platform Basics and Integrations

blocks.x: Welcome to Adit Academy!

Adit Academy is a free online training program that offers courses designed by product experts to help you expand your understanding and use of the Adit platform. Our courses feature expert training videos and articles with quizzes to test your knowledge and track your progress. Adit Academy is perfect to introduce new users within your practice to our software, or as a refresher for experienced users!
Sign Up for Adit Academy

Registering for Adit Academy is easy!
Once logged into your Adit dashboard, click on the "Question Mark" iconat the top right of the Adit page.
From the dropdown click on "Help Center". This will open the Help widget.
From the Help widget overlay box that appears, click the "Adit Academy" option.
This will create your account using the same username and password you already use to log into the Adit platform.
Log In to Adit Academy
You can log in to Adit Academy through the Help widget within your Adit dashboard (the same way you signed up, above), or you can navigate to https://academy.adit.com/ and log in manually.
Adit Academy Courses
Once you have logged in to Adit Academy, you will see three sections of courses:
000: Introduction: a quick guide on how to navigate through Adit Academy.
100: Platform Basics: a basic overview of the top features of each Adit platform module.

200: Beyond the Basics: contains sub-sections that are broken down by Adit platform module. Each module sub-section will have courses covering specific features and functions within that module. Each course will generally start with a link to a Knowledge Base article that goes over the feature or function, followed by a video that shows you how to interact with the module and a quiz to test your knowledge about what you just learned.
We recommend that new users go through the courses in sequential order, but you can click on any available course in whatever order you prefer.

articles.title: Understanding Adit’s New Navigation Layout
articles.module: Getting Started, Platform Basics and Integrations

blocks.x: Adit’s latest update introduces a redesigned interface that improves navigation, multitasking, and access to key features. This article explains the new UI/UX elements, their purpose, and how you can use them effectively.
1. New Menu Structure (Left Sidebar)
What’s New:
The main navigation is now on the left-hand side for faster access to frequently used features.
Hovering over a menu category instantly reveals its sub-menus, reducing the number of clicks to reach a page.

Switch Locations - If your practice has multiple locations, you can switch between them directly while setting up the booking link. This ensures the correct address, map, and provider availability are tied to the link.
Example:
Previously, to access Quick Text, you had to go: Engage - Preferences - Quick Text.
Now, hover over Preferences in the left menu to access Quick Text directly.
Why it Matters:
Reduces navigation time.
Keeps all core features in a consistent location.
2. New Third Panel
What’s New:
When viewing records like forms or patients, a third panel opens without leaving the main list view.
You can click through multiple records without navigating back and forth.
Why it Matters:
Enables faster review of records.
Reduces clicks and page reloads
3. Multitasking with the Patient Card
What’s New:
The Patient Card now opens as a persistent panel.
You can continue working in other modules without closing the card.
Why it Matters:
Saves time for staff reviewing multiple patients.
Allows quick appointment creation or task assignment without interrupting your workflow.
4. Tooltips: Moved to the Bottom Left
What’s New:
Tooltips now appear in the bottom left corner of the screen.
Clicking a tooltip opens the relevant help article.
Why it Matters:
Keeps help resources visible without blocking main content.
One-click access to step-by-step guides.
5. Homepage: Notifications Moved to Left Side
What’s New:
Practice Notifications and My Notifications are now in a left-side panel.
Why it Matters:
Creates more space for the Scheduler and other widgets on the right.
Keeps all alerts in a single, easy-to-scan column.
6. Homepage: New "Updates" Tab
What’s New:
A dedicated Updates tab is now on the homepage to see all platform changes without going to your profile menu.
Why it Matters:
Staff can stay informed on new releases without extra clicks.
7. Homepage: Scheduler Overview
What’s New:
The homepage includes a live Scheduler view.
You can quickly see appointments, open slots, and block-offs.
Learn More:
See Manage Your Schedule in Adit for detailed steps.
8. Ability to Collapse Notifications to Expand Scheduler
What’s New:
The left notification panel can be collapsed to show more of the scheduler.
Why it Matters:
Ideal for practices with heavy scheduling activity.
Gives a cleaner, full-width calendar view.
9. Homepage: "My Tasks" Tab
What’s New:
A My Tasks tab provides a quick view of assigned tasks and due dates.
Learn More:
See Task Management in Adit for step-by-step task creation and assignment.
10. Quick Text Button Renamed to "Create Request"
What’s New:
The old Quick Text button is now the Create Request blue button.
Why it Matters:
Supports a wider range of requests beyond quick messages.

articles.title: What are Adit's minimum system requirements?
articles.module: Getting Started, Platform Basics and Integrations

blocks.x: Adit’s integrated software platform and voice-over-IP (VoIP) phone system have relatively low requirements for storage, memory, and speed. Your practice must be able to meet the requirements listed below in order to use our products.
Server Application
Our server application integrates Adit's features with your EHR/PMS software. The Adit application is small, and it must be installed on the same computer as your EHR/PMS software database.
Operating System: Windows Server 2008 R2 SP1 or higher
Memory: 8 GB RAM or higher
CPU: 4 cores at 2.4 GHz or higher
Drive Space: 1 GB (must reside on the same drive as your EHR/PMS software)
Internet Speed: 10 Mbps download, 3 Mbps upload
Adit Voice Phones
In addition to the server application requirements listed above, your practice must also meet the following requirements for each phone.
Internet Speed: 2 Mbps download, 1 Mbps upload per phone
Adit Desktop App
Operating System: Windows 10 or higher (64-bit), or all versions of MAC OS
Memory: 4 GB RAM or higher (16 GB preferred)
CPU: minimum dual core processor
Drive Space: 1-2 GB of available space
Screen Resolution of 1366x768 or higher

articles.title: How to Edit Your Practice Information
articles.module: Getting Started, Platform Basics and Integrations

blocks.x: You can edit your practice information through your settings within the Adit App. This is useful to keep information and access on the account up to date.
These settings can only be edited by a user with Manager or Owner level access.
1. Go to Settings from the top right corner of the Adit App.
2. Select the specific location you'd like to edit the information for.
The following information can be edited within the Location settings:
- General Information: General information about the practice such as Area Name (Nickname), Address, Time Zone, and Contact information for the Practice.
- Google Business Hours: If connected to your Google Business Page, your practice hours will show here. This is the hours that will be provided for automated missed call texts if enabled.

- Business Hours (Online Scheduling): Here, you can edit the hours in which patients can schedule appointment through the Online Scheduling module. These can be different from the regular full practice hours if desired.
- User Access: This section shows users on the account and allows you to toggle which users have access to the specific location.
If there is only one location and you remove access for a user but do not remove them completely as a user, they would only see a blank screen upon login.
- App Access: This section allows you to show or hide app access to all users within the location.
Toggling off an application here removes access for all users at this location. Please navigate to the users settings if you wish to remove app access for specific users on the account.

articles.title: How To: Install the Adit browser extension for Chrome
articles.module: Getting Started, Platform Basics and Integrations

blocks.x: This article walks you through installing the Adit browser extension for the first time. If you already have the extension installed and need to troubleshoot it, please see Troubleshooting: Reconnect the Adit browser extension for Chrome.

Adit’s integration with cloud-based EHRs uses a browser extension for Google Chrome. This extension allows us to sync your patient and appointment information into the Adit platform, where you can then use our all-in-one solution to manage your practice, communicate with patients, and more!
The integration works using three distinct data syncs:
an initial database sync, which pulls all of your patient and appointment data into Adit,
an ongoing, real-time sync, which pulls any changes that you make to your patient or appointment data into Adit as they are made.
an ongoing, hourly backup sync, which pulls any changes that were missed by the real-time sync.
When you set up your integration, you will install the browser extension on one workstation and start the initial data sync.
Requirements for Initial Data Sync
Before starting the initial sync, please keep the following important points in mind:
A user with admin-level permissions must be logged in to your EHR before installing the Adit browser extension and starting the initial sync.
The initial data sync will take 5-7 days to complete. During this time:
Your EHR window can be minimized, but cannot be closed.
The computer must remain powered on and active. It cannot go to sleep, have the screen locked, or be logged off.
Your internet connection must remain stable for the entire duration.

The user who logged in to your EHR and started the sync cannot log in to any other workstation with the same user account. Your EHR likely does not allow the same user to be logged in to multiple devices at the same time. If this is a problem for your team, we recommend creating a new user in your EHR and logging in with that account to start the initial sync.
You can continue to use your EHR and the workstation normally while the initial sync is running in the background.
Your EHR may normally timeout after 10 minutes of user inactivity; our sync will intentionally stop this from happening to preserve the integrity of your data.

Any failure to comply with the above points will cause the sync to fail and require you to re-start it again from the beginning. Failure to do so will result in your Adit platform and Adit browser extension not working properly.
Initial Integration Setup
Install the Adit Browser Extension
To install the Adit browser extension the first time:
Open Google Chrome on one computer in your office.
Open your EHR in that Chrome window and log in with admin-level permissions.
Copy and paste the Chrome Extension link that our support team provided
In the next window, click Add Extension.
You will see a progress update in the top right corner of your Chrome window, and a notification when the extension has finished installing.
In the top right corner of your Chrome browser, click the Extensions icon.
Locate the Adit App extension in the list of installed extensions. Click the pin icon to add it to your toolbar for easy access.
Next, you’ll configure the Adit browser extension for your office.
Configure the Adit Browser Extension
To configure the Adit browser extension:
Click on the Adit icon in the toolbar at the top right corner of your Chrome window to launch the extension.
Log in with your Adit account credentials. You can log in with any user's Adit credentials, but we recommend using the same user account that will work on this workstation the most often.
Select your Adit account location from the dropdown, then click Save.
Give this workstation a nickname, so you can easily tell it apart from your other workstations. Click the Add Name button at the bottom of the window, type in your name, and click
Save.
You can now close or minimize the extension, but don't log out.
Configure Adit Integration Settings

Finally, you'll finish the configuration process within the EHR Settings section in the Adit platform.
If you are new to Adit, you can go back to the Get Started page, scroll down to Connect Your EHR, and click Set up.
If you have been an Adit client for a while and are just setting up the integration with your EHR for the first time, you'll go to Settings > Location > EHR, scroll down to Enable EHR Sync? and click Edit Settings.
Click Next through the first one or two pages, until you reach the page that looks like this:
Click Next to continue.

This page will ask you to map your EHR locations on the left to your Adit locations in the drop-down. You can only sync one EHR location to each Adit location, and each Adit location can only sync with one EHR location. Please choose your mapping carefully, then click Next.

The next screen will ask you how many workstations you have at each of the locations you mapped on the previous screen. Enter in the number of computers at each location where staff members will log into and use your EHR, then click Next.

You will now need to install the Adit browser extension on all of the workstations at each location. Follow the steps in the section below titled "Install the Adit browser extension on an additional workstation" on every workstation.

This page of the configuration flow will show you your progress of installing the extension on all of your workstations; click Refresh to see an updated number. When all of your workstations show they have connected, click Next.

The next page explains crucial information that you need to know before you start the initial data sync. Please read this page, make sure you understand it, and confirm your understanding by checking the box at the bottom. Then, click Next.

On the next page, you will select one workstation at each location to serve as the Primary workstation. This is the workstation that will perform the initial data sync for that location, and must abide by the requirements listed on the previous page. Once you have selected a primary workstation for each location, click Sync.
You can now close this configuration / setup flow by clicking the x in the top right corner.

The initial sync will now run in the background on each of the primary workstations. The real-time sync will begin working immediately on all workstations that have the extension installed, and the backup sync will run hourly.

You can use your workstations and your EHR normally while the initial sync processes in the background, but remember the requirements for that initial data sync to be successful as outlined at the beginning of this article!

If you would like to check on the status of your initial sync, you can return to the same location where you did the configuration (Get Started or Settings > Location > EHR) to see a progress and status bar on the last page.
Install the Adit Browser Extension on an Additional Workstation
To install the Adit browser extension on an additional workstation:
Open Google Chrome on one computer in your office.
Copy and paste the Chrome Extension link that our support team provided
Click the Add to Chrome button.
In the next window, click Add Extension.
You will see a progress update in the top right corner of your Chrome window, and a notification when the extension has finished installing.
In the top right corner of your Chrome browser, click the Extensions icon.
Locate the Adit App extension in the list of installed extensions. Click the pin icon to add it to your toolbar for easy access.
Click on the Adit icon in the toolbar at the top right corner of your Chrome window to launch the extension.
Log in with your Adit account credentials. You can log in with any user's Adit credentials, but we recommend using the same user account that will work on this workstation the most often.
Select your Adit account location from the dropdown, then click Save.
Give this workstation a nickname, so you can easily tell it apart from your other workstations. Click the Add Name button at the bottom of the window, type in your name, and click
Save.
You can now close or minimize the extension, but don't log out.

articles.title: Navigating and Customizing Tables in Adit
articles.module: Getting Started, Platform Basics and Integrations

blocks.x: Overview

The updated Adit platform introduces smarter, more customizable tables to enhance how you interact with data. Whether you are viewing patient lists, appointment data, or forms, the improved tables are designed to support multitasking and offer maximum control over what you see and how you work.
What’s New

articles.title: Why Adit needs login credentials and administrator-level access to your system
articles.module: Getting Started, Platform Basics and Integrations

blocks.x: Welcome to Adit! In order to ensure smooth and uninterrupted operation, it is crucial for users to provide their Admin username and password during the setup process. This allows us to implement and maintain essential features such as task scheduling and service monitoring to ensure that your app is running and updating at all times.
1. Task Scheduler

The task scheduler is a critical component of our system. It enables automated checks to determine if the Adit server app is running at specific intervals. If the app is not running, the scheduler will take the necessary steps to initiate it.
Functionality:
Checks the status of the Adit server app at regular intervals.
Automatically starts the app if it is not already running.
2. Service Montioring

The Pozativeappstatus service plays a vital role in ensuring the seamless operation of the sync module. It monitors the status of the sync process and takes corrective action in case of any synchronization issues, particularly with appointments.
Functionality:
Monitors sync status at specified intervals.
Restarts the server app if any synchronization issues, especially with appointments, are detected.
Why Admin User Credentials are Necessary:
Application Accessibility:
System users or local users may have restricted access to certain applications. Admin credentials grant us the necessary permissions to configure and run essential components.
Domain Setup Considerations:
In scenarios where a domain setup is in place, local users may have limited privileges. Admin credentials ensure unrestricted access to system resources.
Firewall and Security Settings:
Certain firewall and Windows Defender settings may prevent local users from using specific applications. Admin privileges bypass such restrictions, enabling uninterrupted operation.
Consequences of Sync Failure if Admin Credentials are not provided:
In the event of a sync failure, the following critical functionalities may be affected until the Server Application is manually restarted:
All Reminders:
Reminders for appointments and other things such as patient form reminder, payment requests, etc., may not function correctly.
Adit Pay:
The Adit Pay module may experience disruptions, affecting financial transactions.
Patient Forms and Online Scheduling:
The Patient Forms and Online Scheduling module may not operate as intended.
Deleted Appointments:
Deleted appointments may not sync with the Adit app, potentially leading to incorrect reminders.
Patient Details:
Updates to patient details may not be reflected in real-time.

articles.title: What does my Adit for Chrome extension's status mean?
articles.module: Getting Started, Platform Basics and Integrations

blocks.x: Your Adit for Chrome extension will show different statuses throughout the day, both in the extension itself and within your Adit platform.

Connected
The Adit for Chrome extension is logged in successfully and connected to both Adit and your EHR/PMS. Any actions you take in Adit or your EHR/PMS on this workstation will sync in real time.

EHR Idle
The Adit for Chrome extension is logged in successfully and connected to Adit, but not connected to your EHR/PMS. This does not necessarily mean something is wrong; your EHR/PMS could be idle, not in use, or logged out. If you see this status, you should check that the workstation is currently in use, and that the user is accessing your EHR/PMS through a Chrome browser window. Any actions you take in Adit or your EHR/PMS on this workstation will sync, but not in real time - they may be delayed by at least 1 hour.

Disconnected
The Adit for Chrome extension is not logged in or not connected to Adit. This could be because the computer is off or has no internet access, or the extension may need to be logged back in. If you see this status, check that the workstation is currently in use and has internet access. Then, check the Adit for Chrome extension to ensure it is logged in and has a location selected. Any actions you take in Adit or your EHR/PMS on this workstation will not sync. For instructions on how to reconnect your Adit for Chrome extension, please see How To: Reconnect your Adit for Chrome Extension.

blocks.x: At times, interruption may occur in the connection between your PMS server and Adit. The most common causes for this kind of interruption include:
a. The Adit server application (Pozative.exe) has been accidentally closed.
b. There was an interruption in your server's internet connection.
c. Your server computer was turned off.
d. The server login password has been changed.
Disconnections like this are fairly routine and will normally resolve on their own (for example, when internet access is restored or the server turned back on). However,
To check if your Adit account is disconnected from your PMS:

When you are logged into your Adit account, you will see a pink banner notification across the bottom of the screen.This means the connection between it and your PMS is broken, and information between the two are no longer syncing.
The message will say: Alert: Your EHR/PMS seems to be Disconnected. To continue using Adit, please turn on your server computer and make sure that the Adit application is running. Locations affected: view here
If you notice the pink "EHR Disconnected" banner at the bottom of your Adit screen persists after a few minutes, here are a few steps you can take:
1. Refresh the Adit desktop app or your browser window. If the banner goes away, that means we're re-connected an no further action is needed.
2. Check your server computer to make sure it is turned on, not in sleep mode, and connected to the internet.
3. Restart your server computer.
4. Ask your administrator if the system password (password to login to the server computer) has been changed. If so, please contact Adit to share the new password.
If none of the above resolve the issue (and the pink banner still persists), please send us an email to support@adit.com or call us at (832) 225-8865.

articles.title: Troubleshooting: Reconnect your Adit for Chrome browser extension
articles.module: Getting Started, Platform Basics and Integrations

blocks.x: Adit’s integration with many cloud EHRs uses a browser extension for Google Chrome. This extension allows us to sync your patient and appointment information into the Adit platform, where you can then use our all-in-one solution to manage your practice, communicate with patients, and more!
In order to use the integration, your staff must be using the Google Chrome browser to access your cloud EHR and have the Adit for Chrome extension installed and logged in to your Adit account.
The integration works using three distinct data syncs:
an initial database sync, which pulls all of your patient and appointment data into Adit,
an ongoing real-time sync, which pulls any changes that you make to your patient or appointment data into Adit as they are made.
an ongoing backup sync, which pulls any changes that were missed by the real-time sync.

Adit will let you know automatically if any workstation fails its real-time sync. Every 10 minutes, our application checks to see if each workstation has transmitted data in the last 10 minutes. If so, great! If not, we show you a notification bar at the bottom of your Adit dashboard to let you know that one or more workstations are idle. You can click through that notification for more details about exactly which workstations are affected and how to reconnect them.

Often, a workstation may stop syncing because no one is working in the cloud EHR on that computer in the last 10 minutes - for example, if there are no patients in an operatory at that time, or if a staff member logs off to go to lunch. In those cases, we will show those workstations as “Idle” until they start transmitting data again. Once the workstation starts syncing on its own again, we will automatically update its status back to "Syncing" and you will not need to take any action.

Sometimes, a workstation may have a hiccup where it does not start syncing on its own again. If you have been working in your cloud EHR on a workstation for more than 10 minutes and that workstation still shows a status of Idle, we encourage you to log out of the browser extension on that workstation and then log back in to reconnect it.
To reconnect the Adit browser extension:
In the top right corner of your Chrome browser, click on the Adit icon in the toolbar.
If you don't see the Adit icon, click the Extensions icon shaped like a puzzle piece and select Adit from the list.
Click the Logout button in the top right corner.
Log back in with your Adit credentials.
Select the correct location.
Make sure the Workstation Name is correct for this workstation.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, please contact Adit Support.

articles.title: Understanding SMS Billing & Mass Text Charges

blocks.x: Mass texting allows practices to instantly reach a large number of patients. However, SMS billing is not calculated only by the number of recipients.
Charges are determined by SMS segments, which depend on:
Number of recipients
Message length
Character encoding (GSM vs. Unicode)
Special characters, emojis, or formatting
How SMS Billing Works
When sending a mass text (for example, to 3,538 recipients), charges are calculated based on:
Number of recipients
Length of the message
Character encoding type
Special characters or emojis used
Each text sent may count as 1, 2, 3, or more SMS units per recipient.
Understanding SMS Character Limits
GSM Encoding (Standard Text)
Limit: 160 characters per SMS
If message exceeds 160 characters, it splits into multiple parts
Each part counts as 1 SMS unit
Segment Breakdown:
1-160 characters = 1 unit
161-306 characters = 2 units
307-459 characters = 3 units
Unicode Encoding (Emojis / Special Characters)
If the message contains:
Emojis ( )
Curly quotes (“ ”)
Special symbols
Certain punctuation
The message switches to Unicode encoding.
Limit: 70 characters per SMS
Segment Breakdown:
1-70 characters = 1 unit
71-134 characters = 2 units
135-201 characters = 3 units
Important: Even one emoji can reduce the limit from 160 to 70 characters.
Visual SMS Segment Calculation Example
Scenario:
You send a 180-character message with no emojis to 3,538 patients.

Step 1: Determine Encoding
No emojis → GSM encoding

Step 2: Determine Segments
180 characters → Falls under 161-306 range → 2 SMS units per recipient

Step 3: Calculate Total Units
3,538 recipients × 2 units = 7,076 SMS units

Step 4: Calculate Cost
7,076 × $0.01 = $70.76
Unicode Example:
Same 180-character message + 1 emoji
Switches to Unicode
180 characters → Falls under 135-201 range
3 SMS units per recipient
How Charges Are Calculated
Formula:
Number of Recipients × SMS Segments = Total SMS Units
Each SMS unit = $0.01
Frequently Asked Questions
Why is my SMS usage higher than my contact list?
SMS charges are based on message length, not just the number of recipients.
If your message exceeds character limits or contains emojis/special characters, it splits into multiple segments.
Each segment counts as a separate SMS per recipient.
Why did adding one emoji increase my bill?
Adding an emoji switches the message from GSM encoding (160 characters) to Unicode encoding (70 characters).
This significantly reduces the character limit per segment, causing the message to split into more units.
How can I reduce SMS costs?
Keep messages under 160 characters
Avoid emojis
Avoid special symbols
Use simple punctuation
Preview character count before sending
Key Takeaway
SMS overages typically occur due to message length and Unicode characters - not system errors.
Understanding character limits helps prevent unexpected charges and allows practices to optimize messaging costs effectively.

articles.title: What are the charges, overages, and surcharges on my invoice?

blocks.x: Adit Invoicing

Most Adit clients are billed for their Adit services with two separate invoices each month. The first is your recurring monthly subscription charge; some clients pay this annually instead of monthly. The second invoice is for your Adit application usage overages and surcharges.
Types of Charges
Your invoice will include three types of charges: service fees, overages, and surcharges.
Service Fees

A Service Fee is a set fee for a particular feature or module within the Adit platform. For most clients, the only feature we include separately on your invoice is Call Tracking. This feature has an additional charge because of the resource-intense nature of saving all call recordings and tracking records.
Overages

Your Adit subscription comes with a certain number of minutes, messages, and phone numbers included at no additional charge. If you go over these allotted limits, you will be charged a small fee for the additional minutes, messages, and phone numbers used. These are overage charges.
Please refer to Adit's Usage Policy for more information about what is included in your subscription.
You may be charged overages for:
Additional phone numbers
Call Tracking minutes
Text messages
Email messages
Video minutes
Mass/bulk text messages
Surcharges

Surcharges are additional fees passed on to you from a source outside of Adit, such as a mobile carrier or a regulatory agency. Adit passes these surchages on to you with no additional markup. These surcharges may include:

10DLC Registration Fee: a one-time fee charged to register your phone number for 10DLC regulatory compliance. May be charged an additional time if your registration has to be re-submitted due to incomplete information.
10DLC Maintenance Fee: a recurring monthly charge to maintain your 10DLC regulatory compliance.

FCC, CTRC, and Carrier Surcharges: a per-message fee charged by mobile carriers in the US and Canada, including T-Mobile, Bell, AT&T, Rogers, etc. These fees will vary based on the number of text messages you send per month, including 1:1 messages, automated messages, and mass/bulk messages.
How do I reduce my surcharges?

Carriers charge surcharges for every message sent and received. You can reduce the surcharges you are billed by using other Adit features in place of text messages. For example, reduce your mass texting surcharges by using Email Campaigns for marketing purposes; reduce your carrier surcharges by utilizing Adit's email and voice reminders in place of or in addition to text reminders. Striking a good balance between text messaging and other types of communication is how many of our clients reduced their monthly surcharges by 50-60%!
See our article on how to Edit an appointment reminder to learn how to set up reminders by email and voice.
To find out more about surcharges and overages, please see Adit's Usage Policy and Adit Terms.

articles.title: 10DLC: FAQ

blocks.x: To ensure compliance with Federal Communications Commission regulations and to avoid federal fines and charges for violating these regulations, we recommend that you register your business brand for 10-Digit Long Code (10DLC). This applies to all companies in North American who may send text messages to a US-based phone number.

Because a large volume of unsolicited text messages are often sent using messaging software (called "application-to-peer" or "A2P"), phone carriers in North American now partner with The Campaign Registry (TCR) to authenticate legitimate business phone numbers. By registering with TCR, businesses ensure the credibility of their messages, protecting consumers from unwanted texts, maintaining communication standards, and ensuring message delivery.

Failure to register your practice may incur additional fees and penalties from carriers and their partners. These fees will be added to your service charges. You may also encounter problems sending future text messages to patients if carriers mark your messages as spam due to a lack of 10DLC registration.
What is 10DLC?

10DLC (10-digit long code) is the newest service for business text messaging using SMS and MMS. 10DLC explicitly allows application-to-peer (A2P) SMS traffic over long code phone numbers for things like alerts, appointment reminders, notifications, and marketing messages. 10DLC is required by carriers to improve reliability and integrity of A2P communications.
How do I register my practice for 10DLC?
To register your outgoing number for 10DLC, navigate to Settings, then Locations, choose your location from the left navigation menu, then select Communications.

From here, you can fill in the required information and select whether you will register for Low-Volume or High-Volume messaging. Your choice should be based on your practice's daily combined text messaging needs, including individual texts, automated reminders, and mass texts. The following information is required:
Business Specific Information
Legal Company Name
Brand Name or Business Name
What type of legal form is the organization?
Country of Registration
Website
EIN/CCN Issuing Country
EIN/CCN
Business Address:
Street Address
City
State
Zip Code
Brand Contact Details:
Email Address
Phone Number
What are the costs and fees associated with 10DLC?
The costs associated with registering will differ depending on if you opt in to Low- or High-Volume Messaging.
These costs are directly passed from the carrier to you with no additional markup. These charges are subject to change. You can locate your charges by going to Settings > Admin Panel > Billing.
Low-Volume Messaging

blocks.x: Included In Your Subscription
Your Adit subscription includes:
2 phone numbers
Unlimited Adit Voice minutes
Unlimited 1:1 text messaging
500 call tracking minutes
100 video minutes
20,000 emails
These limits are per location per month. Some Adit subscription packages may include additional phone numbers or features.
Additional Charges and Overages
Some Adit features will incur additional charges for their use, while others will incur overages only if you surpass your allotted limit per location per month.
Additional phone numbers (over subscription allotment): $2 per number per month
Call tracking minutes (over subscription allotment): $0.03 per minute
Video minutes (over subscription allotment): $0.03 per minute
E-mails (over subscription allotment): $1.00 per 1,000 additional emails
Mass/bulk text messages: $0.01 per message, plus applicable carrier surcharges
Other Charges
Adit also passes on certain compliance surcharges and fee to you. We do not alter or markup these surcharges.
FCC and CRTC surcharges: charged directly by government regulatory bodies for text messaging
Carrier surcharges: charged by all major mobile carriers (AT&T, Bell, T-Mobile, Rogers, Sprint, etc) for text messages delivered to a recipient's mobile phone number
10DLC registration fee: minimum one-time fee of $22 charged to register your phone number for 10DLC regulatory compliance
10DLC maintenance fee: monthly fee of $2-11 for ongoing compliance maintenance
Why Does Mass Texting Cost More?

Mass and bulk text messages require additional security and compliance measures to ensure we are meeting government regulations and carrier requirements. There are various fees associated with this compliance, so we pass some of that cost on to you by charging a small amount ($0.01) per mass/bulk message sent.
More Information About Minutes
Adit Voice Minutes vs Tracking Minutes

Adit tracks Adit Voice call minutes and Tracking minutes separately based on the type of phone number the call was made to or from. Our phone carrier designates these calls differently because they are routed differently - landline calls typically ring directly on an extension in your office, while tracking numbers route the call from one phone number to another phone number before an extension rings.
If you made a call from or received a call on your Adit Voice landline, those are Adit Voice minutes. Typically, your landline number will route to various extensions within your office.
If you received a call on a Tracking phone number, those are Tracking minutes.
If you forward landline calls to a Tracking number in your call flow, any calls forwarded to that Tracking number will use Tracking minutes.

articles.title: Guide to the Patient Card

blocks.x: Adit’s Patient Card is a one-stop place to find all the information that the Adit platform has about one of your patients. Because the Patient Card links together many of Adit’s other modules, it’s a convenient place to perform some of your most common tasks.

Accessing the Patient Card is easy! Start typing your patient’s name into the Patient Search box, which you can find at the top of any page within the Adit platform. Select the patient from the list of suggested matches, and their Patient Card will open on the right-hand side of your screen.
There are three main sections to the Patient Card: the top, Activity, and Patient Info.

The top section of the Patient Card contains the patient’s name, ID, location, gender, age, and date of birth. There are also icons to Call, Text, or Email the patient, and a notation of the patient’s last scheduled and next scheduled appointments.
Note: Calling is only available if you have Adit Voice enabled on your account.
The next section is for Activity related to the patient:
- Patient Forms
- Hygiene Status
- EHR Balance Due
- Adit Pay Balance
- Remaining Benefits
- Unscheduled Production
- Unscheduled Family Members
If you have Patient Forms enabled on your account, you can assign a Patient Form to a patient, or send them a reminder about a pending form.
If you have Adit Pay enabled on your account, you can see the patient’s balance and send a payment request.
If you have Practice Analytics enabled on your account, you can see their Hygiene Status, Remaining Benefits, and Unscheduled Production, as well as Follow Ups and Notes.

Follow Ups are also stored in this section, and you can create, edit, and log an attempt right from the Patient Card. Any notes logged regarding this patient, either manually or automatically by a Follow Up task, appears in the Notes section at the bottom.
The Patient Info section contains details about the patient that have synced over from your EHR software, including:
- Contact information (phone number, email, and address)
- Treatment due dates
- Preferred language
- Insurance information
- Balance due
- Permissions to email and text
The Family File lists all of the patient’s linked family members and highlights if they need an appointment scheduled soon.

articles.title: What is CRM?

blocks.x: CRM (Customer Relationship Management) is the upgraded version of the Patients Module in Adit.

CRM is designed to help practices organize and manage everyone who interacts with the practice - not just patients. Instead of storing all records as Patients, CRM automatically categorizes contacts into different record types and allows practices to track their journey through various stages.
This makes it easier to manage patient relationships, track prospective patients, organize communications, and improve conversion rates.
CRM Record Types
CRM organizes records into four categories:
Patients
Patients are individuals who have an existing relationship with your practice, including:
Existing patients
New patients who have booked an appointment
How Patients are Created
Automatically when a new patient appointment is booked
Manually by practice staff in Adit
Synced from your EHR/PMS
Patient Stages
Patient records progress through the following stages:
No Appointment History - No history of past and future appointments
Scheduled - No completed appointments, but have an appointment scheduled for the future
Never Showed - No completed appointments, but have an appointment in that past that did not complete
Completed - Have one completed appointment, but no history of payment
Won - Have completed one appointment with payment done OR have completed more than one appointment
These stages help you understand where each patient is in their treatment journey.
EHR Synchronization
Patient records are fully synchronized between Adit and your EHR/PMS.
Any patient created in Adit is synced to the EHR, and any patient created in the EHR is synced to Adit. Patient counts and details remain consistent across both systems.
Detailed Explanation
You can read more about patient records in CRM here
Leads
Leads are prospective patients who contacted your practice but have not yet booked an appointment.
How Leads are Created
Automatically through Call Intelligence
Automatically through AI Agent interactions
Manually by practice staff
Lead Stages
Lead records can move through the following stages:
Open
Not Relevant
Lost
When a Lead books an appointment, the record is automatically converted into a Patient, and their journey continues through the Patient stages.
EHR Synchronization
Lead records exist only in Adit and are not synced to the EHR.
Detailed Explanation
You can read more about Lead records in CRM here
Contacts
Contacts are individuals or organizations that interact with your practice but are not patients or prospective patients.
Examples include:
Vendors
Insurance companies
Referral partners
Employee family members
Other business contacts
How Contacts are Created
Contacts must be manually created or tagged by practice staff.
EHR Synchronization
Contact records exist only in Adit and are not synced to the EHR.
Detailed Explanation
You can read more about Contact records in CRM here
Unrecognized Contacts
Unrecognized Contacts are records that cannot automatically be classified as Patients, Leads, or Contacts.
Examples include:
Spam calls
Unknown phone numbers
Unrecognized SMS conversations
How Unrecognized Contacts are Created
These records are automatically created by Adit when interactions occur with unknown or unclassified contacts.
They cannot be created manually.
EHR Synchronization
Unrecognized Contact records exist only in Adit and are not synced to the EHR.
Detailed Explanation
You can read more about Unrecognized Contact records in CRM here
What Changed Compared to the Old Patients Module?
Previously, all records were stored as patients, regardless of whether they were actual patients, prospective patients, vendors, or spam callers.
This created several challenges:
No way to track prospective patients (Leads)
No way to separate patients from vendors or other business contacts
Spam calls created patient records
Patient lists contained significant noise and clutter
Difficult to identify true patient records without filtering
Quick Actions displayed mixed record types
No visibility into where a patient or lead was in their journey
No ability to create targeted campaigns for Leads
Limited visibility into communication history and follow-up activities
Benefits of CRM
CRM addresses these challenges by:
Separating Patients, Leads, Contacts, and Unrecognized Contacts
Tracking the lifecycle of Leads and Patients through stages
Providing cleaner and more accurate patient data
Enabling targeted text and email campaigns
Improving follow-up workflows
Centralizing communication history
Helping practices track and improve conversion rates
By organizing records and tracking every stage of the patient journey, CRM helps practices build stronger relationships, improve operational efficiency, and increase revenue.

articles.title: CRM - Leads

blocks.x: Leads are prospective patients who have shown interest in your practice but have not yet booked an appointment.
Unlike Patients, Lead records exist only within Adit and are not synced to your EHR/PMS.
When a Lead books an appointment and becomes a patient, the Lead record is automatically converted into a Patient record. The patient's journey is then tracked using Patient stages.
How Are Lead Records Created?
Lead records can be created automatically or manually from multiple areas within Adit.
Automatic Record Creation
Lead records can be automatically created from:

Call Intelligence - When a prospective patient contacts the practice to book an appointment but does not complete the booking. This applies to calls handled by both Front Desk staff and AI Front Desk.
EHR Visitor Appointments - When a visitor appointment is created in an EHR that supports visitor scheduling without creating a patient record.
Manual Record Creation
Lead records may also be manually created by practice staff through:
CRM - Create Leads individually or import Leads in bulk using a CSV file. Lead can also be created by converting an existing Contact or Unrecognized Contact
Call Tracking - Review calls and manually create Leads from prospective patient conversations.
Quick Actions - Create a Lead while using quick action against someone who is not an existing patient or existing contact.
Engage - Create a Lead when an SMS is sent directly from Engage for new number
Pozative - Create a Lead when a review request is sent directly from Pozative
Lead Fields
In addition to PII like name, phone number, DOB and email, Lead records will have the below fields
Stage
The Stage field helps track where a Lead is in the conversion journey.
Open
The default stage assigned to all newly created Leads.
Open Leads are prospects who may still convert into patients.
Not Relevant
Used when the contact is not a legitimate patient opportunity and should not be tracked as a Lead.
Lost
Used when the Lead is a legitimate prospective patient, but the practice was unable to convert them into a patient.
All Lead stages are manually managed by the practice. When a Lead books an appointment, the Lead is automatically converted into a Patient record and is no longer managed through Lead stages.
Follow-Up Date
The Follow-Up Date field identifies the next scheduled follow-up date for the Lead.
This field is manually maintained by the practice and helps organize outreach activities.
Temperature
The Temperature field indicates the likelihood that a Lead will convert into a patient.
Hot - High likelihood of conversion.
Warm - Moderate likelihood of conversion.
Cold - Low likelihood of conversion.
Temperature is manually maintained by the practice and can be used to prioritize follow-up efforts.
Notes
The Notes field allows staff to record follow-up summaries, conversation details, and other relevant information about the Lead.
Notes are editable directly from the Leads list for quick updates.
Lead Owner
The Lead Owner field identifies the user responsible for following up with the Lead.
Any user within the practice can be assigned as the Lead Owner.
This field helps establish accountability and ownership of lead follow-up activities.
Lead Source
The Lead Source field identifies the marketing source that generated the Lead.
Examples include:
Google Ads
Google Organic Search
Facebook Ads
Direct Calls
Other marketing channels
This field helps practices measure marketing performance and lead acquisition sources.
Profile Created As
The Profile Created As field identifies the record type when the profile was first created.
Possible values include:
Lead
Patient
Contact
Unrecognized Contact
This field helps practices understand how records move through the CRM and measure conversion rates between categories.
Profile Created By
The Profile Created By field shows who originally created the record.
Possible values include:
Adit
A practice user
Profile Created From
The Profile Created From field identifies the Adit module or system that originally created the Lead record.
Examples include:
Call Intelligence
CRM
Quick Actions
Call Tracking
EHR Visitor Appointment
Profile Created Date
The Profile Created Date field shows when the profile was originally created, regardless of any future changes to the record type.
Not Relevant Reason
When a Lead is moved to the Not Relevant stage, a reason can be selected to explain why the contact is not a valid patient opportunity.
Sales Call - The contact was attempting to sell a product or service to the practice.
Vendor / Supplier - The contact represents a company that provides products or services used by the practice.
Insurance Company - The contact is associated with an insurance provider and is not seeking treatment.
Pharmacy - The contact is a pharmacy representative or pharmacy-related inquiry.
Other Practice / Doctor - The contact is another healthcare provider, specialist, or medical practice.
Lab Technician - The contact is associated with a laboratory or diagnostic service.
Wrong Number - The contact reached the practice by mistake.
Other - Any reason that does not fit the categories above.
Lost Reason
When a Lead is moved to the Lost stage, a Lost Reason can be selected to help understand why the opportunity did not convert.
Preferred Financing Not Accepted - The patient's preferred payment or financing option is not available.
Preferred Slot Not Available - The requested appointment date or time is unavailable.
Preferred Service Not Available - The requested treatment or service is not offered by the practice.
Preferred Location Not Available - The requested practice location is unavailable.
Preferred Provider Not Available - The patient wanted to see a specific provider who was unavailable.
Medicaid Not Accepted - The practice does not accept Medicaid.
Medicare Not Accepted - The practice does not accept Medicare.
Insurance Not Accepted - The patient's insurance plan is not accepted by the practice.
Cash Patients Not Accepted - The practice does not accept cash-pay patients for the requested service.
Language Barrier - The patient's preferred language is not supported.
Price Inquiry - The patient contacted the practice to inquire about pricing but did not book an appointment.
Availability Inquiry - The patient contacted the practice to inquire about appointment availability but did not book.
Left Voicemail - The patient left a voicemail requesting an appointment, but the practice was unable to reconnect with them.
Other - Any reason that does not fit the categories above.
Total Touchpoints

Last Touchpoint
The date and time of the most recent communication between the Lead and the practice.
Last Incoming
The date and time of the most recent communication initiated by the Lead.
Last Outgoing
The date and time of the most recent communication initiated by the practice.

blocks.x: Advanced Online Scheduling allows your patient to book specific services at specific times, directly into your EHR schedule. This helps streamline your scheduling and saves your staff time by allowing patients to book on their own.
To learn how to set up online scheduling please follow this guide:
How to Set Up Your Receptionist Email
Navigate to the Online Scheduling module.
In the top navigation menu, select Scheduling.
If you don’t see this option in the menu, click the three dots
to view the rest of the menu options.
Click the Editicon for the location you would like to update.
In the Receptionist Email(s), add all email addresses which should receive a copy of each appointment request. Separate emails with a comma (no space).
Click Save to save your changes.
How to Enable Advanced Online Scheduling
Scroll down to Online Scheduling?
Toggle the switch on or off as needed and click Confirm when prompted.
How to Enable Appointments to Be Written into the EHR
Scroll down to this field: Write Appointments into EHR/PMS?
Toggle the switch on
How to Manage Service Rules

Defining your services will allow patients to book with a particular provider in a particular operatory at a particular time, ensuring your schedule is seamless and saving your office staff time. Make sure the services are clearly defined and easy for your patients to understand the schedule.
Scroll down to Reasons for Visit.
Click + Create Service and fill out the required fields:
Name of Service: Choose a name that patients will understand, as this will display on the booking form.
Patient Type: Is this service for New or Returning patients?
Service Duration in Minutes: Choose the amount of time to block in your schedule for this service.
Appointment Type: Select the type from the dropdown menu (if applicable)
Operatories: Select all operatories where this appointment can be booked.
Click the Add button to save the service.
Click the toggle switch to turn the service on or off.
If the switch is gray with the button to the left, it is off.
If the switch is orange with the button to the right, it is on.
How to Manage Provider Rules
Scroll down to Providers-Service Rules. Click on the toggles to enable the necessary providers.
Update the matrix grid by checking the boxes that are necessary to match services to providers.
Click Save to save your changes.
How to Manage Operatory Rules
Scroll down to Operatories-Service Rules. Click on the toggles to enable the necessary operatories.
Update the matrix grid by checking the boxes that are necessary to match services to operatories.
Click Save to save your changes.
Scroll down to Operatory-Provider Rules, if providers are enabled.
Update the matrix grid by checking the boxes that are necessary to match providers to operatories.
Click Save to save your changes.
How to Set Your Office Hours
Scroll down to Business Hours.
Click the Edit button.
Select the days and times your office is open.
Click Apply to save your changes.
How to Define the Earliest Time a Patient can Book Their Appointment
Scroll down to the Calendar Buffer.

Enter how many hours in advance you require patients to schedule. For example: if your practice does not offer same-day appointments, enter at least 24 in the Calendar Buffer field. If you would like online bookings to be restricted to two days or further out, enter 48 hours.
How to Require Patients to fill out their Payment Preference
Scroll down to Ask for Payment Preference?
Toggle the switch On
If you want to make this field mandatory to be filled out, select Payment Option is Required
Now when patients fill out the form, there will be a field asking them to select how they will be paying for their services.

articles.title: Understanding Adit's Formula for Calculating Availability
articles.module: Scheduling: Adit Scheduler and Online Scheduling

blocks.x:
Click Here To Watch A Video
Adit can automatically calculate your practice’s real-time availability using the following settings:
Availabilities configured in Adit
Operatories and Providers synced from your EHR
Adit App Business Hours
This article explains what each of these settings means and how to configure them to ensure your online scheduling works seamlessly for your practice.
What is an Availability?

Availability is a feature in Adit that is used to set up designated time periods on the schedule where you would like to accept certain types of appointments. Availabilities are associated with providers, operatories, and appointments.
Click Here to learn how to create an availability in Adit.
What are Operatory/Provider Hours?
Operatory and Provider Hours are the working hours configured in your EHR. These determine when each provider and operatory (treatment room) is available for appointments.
When syncing with your EHR, Adit typically pulls the following scheduling data:
Provider working hours
Operatory working hours
Holidays
These function similarly to Availabilities in Adit, but originate from your EHR instead.
Alert: Not all EHRs offer "Availabilities", and the name may vary depending on your system.
In RevolutionEHR, these are called Appointment Slots
In Crystal PM, these are called Schedule Templates
What are Adit App Business Hours?
Adit App Business hours refer to when your practice will be open or closed.
Alert: Adit does not sync business hours from your EHR. If you want Adit to factor your business hours into real-time appointment availability, you’ll need to set them up directly within Adit.
Click Hereto learn how to configure your business hours.
How Does the Formula Work for Real-Time Availability?
In your Online Scheduling settings, you can configure Adit to calculate availability using a combination of the three main data points described above.
To Set the formula: Navigate to the Online Scheduling Module
Go to the Scheduling Page In the Formula For Availabilit y section, you will see three checkboxes select the data points you want Adit to use.
Different Configurations:
1. When only one checkbox is selected, this means Adit will ONLY use that data point to calculate your real-time availability.

2. When Availabilities and Operatory/Provider Hours from your EHR are selected, Adit determines available times using an “OR” formula . This means that any time that is open in either Adit’s availability OR your EHR schedule or will be shown as available for booking.

Example Scenario: In your EHR , Dr. Tim Smiles is scheduled to work on: Monday, Oct 15 from 10 AM to 12 PM and 1 PM to 5 PM In Adit , Dr. Tim Smiles has availabilities set for: Monday, Oct 15 from 8 AM to 1 PM Result: Patients will see Dr. Tim Smiles as available on: Monday, Oct 15 from 8 AM to 5 PM

3. When Availabilities and Business Hours are selected, Adit calculates available times using an “ OR ” formula . This means that any time that is open in either Adit’s availability OR your Adit App Business hours will be shown as available for booking. king.
Example Scenario:
In Adit, Dr. Tim Smiles has availabilities set:
Monday, Oct 15 from 8 AM to 1 PM.
In Adit, your practice’s business hours are set to be open:
Mondays from 9 AM to 4 PM.
Result:
Patients will see Dr. Tim Smiles as available:
Monday, Oct 15 from 8 AM to 5 PM

4. When Provider/Operatory Hours from EHR and Business Hours are selected, Adit calculates available times using an “ AND ” formula . This means only the hours that overlap between a provider’s availability and the practice’s business hours will be shown as available for booking
Example Scenario:
In your EHR, Dr. Tim Smiles is scheduled to work on:
Monday, Oct 15 from 10 AM to 12 PM and 1 PM to 5 PM
In Adit, your practice’s business hours are set to be open:
Mondays from 9 AM to 4 PM
Result:
Patients will see Dr. Tim Smiles as available:
Monday, Oct 15 from 10 AM to 12 PM and 1 PM to 4 PM
5. When Availabilities, Provider/Operatory Hours from EHR, and Business Hours are selected, Adit calculates available times based on this formula:
(Availabilities in Adit) OR (Provider Hours AND Business Hours)
Example Scenario:
First, Adit will look at availabilities:

Availabilities: Monday, Oct 15, 8 AM to 1 PM Second, Adit will look at the overlapping times between the Provider/Operatory hours and Adit App Business Hours EHR Provider Hours: Monday, Oct 15 10 AM to 12 PM & 1PM to 5 PM Business Hours: Mondays 9 AM to 4 PM Result: Available Time Shown : Monday, Oct 15, 8 AM to 4 PM

articles.title: How to Enable Maximize Lead Capture on Custom Booking Links
articles.module: Scheduling: Adit Scheduler and Online Scheduling

blocks.x: Until now, a patient who started a booking and never finished it was simply lost. Maximize Lead Capture asks for their details before the booking begins, so the opportunity becomes a lead instead of disappearing.

Maximize Lead Capture is a toggle on a Custom Booking Link, available across all practice verticals. It adds a new first page that collects the patient's name, phone number and email. What they enter there is kept whether or not they go on to book.
What changes
Toggle off
How it worked before
Patient opens the booking link
Chooses an appointment type and a time
Enters their details at the end
Leaves partway through
If they do not finish
Nothing. You never knew they were there.
Toggle on
How it works now
Patient opens the booking link
Enters their details on a new first page
Chooses an appointment type and a time
Leaves partway through
If they do not finish
A Lead appears under CRM, Leads, with their name, phone and email.

Moving the details to the front is the whole idea. A patient who completes the booking sees no difference worth noticing, because what they typed on the first page is pre-populated in the later steps. A patient who drops out leaves behind somebody you can call.
It does add a step
Everyone opening the link now answers four questions before seeing your availability. That is the trade. Worth watching your booking numbers for a week after you switch it on.
How it works
Three steps sit in front of the booking. The third is the one that matters, because it is the point at which anything is captured at all.
Step 1
Opens your link
They land on a short information page carrying your practice branding, instead of the calendar.
Step 2
Enters their details
Name, phone and email, all required. On a multi location link they choose a location here too.
Step 3
Selects Next
The details reach Adit. From here the booking carries on as normal.
Nothing is captured before this point.
Turning it on
Go to Online Scheduling in Adit.
Select Booking Link, then select the booking link for your location.
Set Maximize Lead Capture? to Yes.

It applies to the link straight away, and it is set per link, so you can run it on one and leave it off on another. The URL itself does not change, so anywhere you have already shared it keeps working.
What the patient sees

The link opens on the information page rather than the calendar, asking for First Name, Last Name, Phone Number and Email. All four are required. Once they select Next, the rest of the booking runs exactly as it always did.
The patient has to select Next

The lead is created when they move past the information page, not when they start typing. If somebody fills the form in and closes the tab without selecting Next, nothing is captured and no lead appears. This is the most common reason a lead you expected is not there.
From form to lead The Next button. Nothing is captured until it is selected. · The resulting lead under CRM, Leads.
The Next button. Nothing is captured until it is selected.
The resulting lead under CRM, Leads.
Practices with more than one location

If multiple locations are enabled on the booking link, the first page also asks which location the patient is booking for, before anything else. That answer is what creates the lead profile in the right location. Without it a lead from an abandoned booking would arrive with no location attached and could sit with the wrong team.
Testing a booking link
For support teams

Opening a live booking link to check something behaves exactly like a real patient abandoning a booking, so it creates a lead in that practice's CRM. Add ?booking_from=adit to the end of the URL to skip the first page and avoid it.
The same booking link, with and without the parameter. The highlighted part is the only difference:
Lead capture runs
https://booking.adit.com/62236964-cac0-42d8-9a38-ed7111859cc9
The information page appears. An abandoned booking creates a lead.
Lead capture skipped
https://booking.adit.com/62236964-cac0-42d8-9a38-ed7111859cc9?booking_from=adit
Straight to the booking. Nothing is captured.
What each one opens Without the parameter. The information page appears first. · With the parameter. Straight to the booking.
Without the parameter. The information page appears first.
With the parameter. Straight to the booking.
FAQs
Someone filled the form in but no lead was created. Why?
The lead is created when the patient selects Next and moves past the first page. If they closed the tab while still on it, nothing was submitted and nothing was captured.
Do I need to reshare the booking link after turning this on?
No. The link itself does not change, so anywhere you have already shared it keeps working.
What happens to captured leads if I turn the toggle off?
Leads already in CRM stay there. Turning it off only stops the first page appearing on new visits.
Can I use it on some booking links but not others?
Yes. It is a per link toggle, so you can capture leads on a campaign link and leave your general link alone.

blocks.x: The ASAP List in Adit allows patients to request earlier appointment times if a slot becomes available. This feature helps practices fill last-minute cancellations quickly while keeping patients happy with faster access to care.
What is the ASAP List?

The ASAP List is a queue of patients who have opted in to be notified if an earlier time opens up. Once a cancellation occurs, staff can see which patients are waiting and contact them to fill the spot.
How Patients Can Add Themselves to the ASAP List
Patients have the opportunity to add themselves to the ASAP List via the confirmation page after booking an appointment
1. Book an Appointment
The patient books their appointment online.
Once the booking is confirmed, the Thank You Page is displayed.
2. Select “Join ASAP List”
On the Thank You Page, patients see an option: “Want an earlier appointment? Join the ASAP List.”
Patients click the checkbox or button to confirm.
3. Confirmation of ASAP Enrollment
A confirmation message appears, confirming that the patient has been added to the ASAP List for the service, provider, and location they booked.
The appointment remains scheduled at the original time until staff manually reassign the patient to a new slot.
Notifications & Staff Visibility

When a patient adds themselves to the ASAP List from the confirmation page, the appointment will not be automatically rebooked.Instead, your team gains visibility into this request inside Adit’s Engage > ASAP List dashboard.
From here, staff can:
See a list of all patients who requested to be seen sooner.
Review patient details such as provider, appointment type, and preferences.
Reach out to patients directly (call, text, or reassign) when earlier slots become available.
