articles.title: Setting Fields as Pre-Fill Fields in Patient Forms

blocks.x: Overview

Pre-Fill Fields let your staff populate specific fields on a form before it is sent to the patient. The patient then receives the form with that information already locked in - they can see it, but they cannot change it. This is ideal for details the office controls and the patient shouldn't edit, such as the appointment date, the treating provider's name, or an internal reference number.
This article covers the supported field types, the limitations to be aware of, how to configure a Pre-Fill field on a form, and the two ways staff can enter pre-fill information when sending forms.
Who Is This Article For?
Practice administrators who build forms, and front-office staff who send forms via Quick Text or the Patient Card and need to complete pre-fill information before sending.
Benefits
Reduces patient data entry - Patients aren't asked to fill in details the office already knows.
Ensures critical information is included - Key details like appointment dates and provider names are guaranteed to be on the form, entered accurately by staff.
Supports internal workflow requirements - Office-use-only information can travel with the form without relying on the patient to supply it.
Supported Field Types
Pre-Fill can be enabled on the following field types:
Single Line Text
Date Fields
Multi-choice checkboxes
Important Limitations
Pre-Fill fields cannot be marked as Required. The Required toggle is not compatible with Pre-Fill, since the patient is not the one completing the field.
Patients cannot edit Pre-Fill fields. The information staff enters is read-only on the patient side.
Empty Pre-Fill fields remain blank after submission. If staff skip a pre-fill field before sending, the patient cannot fill it in - it will simply come back empty.
Part 1: Setting Up a Pre-Fill Field on a Form
Step 1: Open Form Manager
Navigate to the Patient Forms module in Adit.
In the left navigation menu, click Form Manager.
Edit the desired form by clicking the Form Name or the Edit icon.
Step 2: Enable Pre-Fill on the Field
Select an existing Single Line Text or Date field on the form (or add a new one from the toolbar). The field properties panel opens on the right.
Enable the Pre-Fill Field toggle in the properties panel.
Click Save in the top navigation.
The field is now configured for pre-fill functionality and will be presented to staff for completion whenever this form is assigned.
Part 2: Entering Pre-Fill Information Before Sending
Once a form contains Pre-Fill fields, staff complete them at the time the form is assigned. Pre-Fill entry is available when assigning forms through:
Quick Text
Patient Card → Assign Form
Understanding the Pre-Fill Status Indicators
Adit shows a colored status icon so staff can see at a glance whether the pre-fill information has been completed before the form goes out:

rows: One or more Pre-Fill fields are still incomplete.
Click the icon and complete the outstanding fields before sending.
All Pre-Fill fields have been completed.
None - the form is ready to send.

blocks.x: Option 1: Individual Entry
Best when assigning a single form to a patient.
Click the Pre-Fill icon on the form assignment.
Enter the required information into each Pre-Fill field.
Click Save.
Send the form to the patient.
Option 2: Bulk Entry
Recommended when assigning multiple forms at once - outstanding pre-fill fields across all forms are completed from a single review screen.
Click Send or Assign.
On the review screen, complete all outstanding Pre-Fill fields across the assigned forms.
Submit the forms.
Key Reminders
Only staff can edit Pre-Fill fields - patients cannot modify pre-filled information in any way.
If a Pre-Fill field is left empty when the form is sent, it remains blank after the patient submits - the patient cannot complete it on your behalf.
Pre-Fill fields cannot be designated as Required.
Watch the status icon: send only when it turns green if you need every pre-fill value populated.
Common Use Cases
Appointment dates - confirm the visit date on consent or pre-visit paperwork.
Provider names - identify the treating provider on treatment-specific forms.
Internal reference numbers - case, claim, or chart numbers used by your office.
Office-use-only information - any detail your workflow requires on the document that the patient should not supply or alter.
Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why can't I make my Pre-Fill field Required?
By design, Pre-Fill fields cannot be marked as Required. The patient is not the one completing the field, so a Required validation on their side would not make sense.

Q: We sent a form and the pre-fill field came back empty. What happened?
The field was likely not completed by staff before sending. Empty Pre-Fill fields remain blank after submission - patients cannot fill them in. Check for the orange status icon before sending next time.

Q: Can patients at least see the pre-filled information?
Yes - the information is visible to the patient on the form, but it is read-only and cannot be edited.

Q: Which sending methods support pre-fill entry?
Pre-Fill fields can be completed when assigning forms through Quick Text or via Patient Card → Assign Form.

articles.title: Toggling Auto-Import ON or OFF for Patient Forms

blocks.x: Overview

Auto-Import is the feature that automatically transfers completed Patient Forms into your connected EHR/PMS. When Auto-Import is enabled for a form, two things happen automatically after the form is completed and approved:
The completed form PDF is uploaded into the patient's record in the EHR (in the folder you've configured - see the related article on EHR Folder selection).
All mapped fields are updated in the patient's chart with the responses from the form.

With Auto-Import turned OFF, completed forms remain in Adit and must be reviewed and imported manually by your team. This article explains when Auto-Import applies, when it does not, and the two ways to enable or disable it.
Who Is This Article For?
Practice administrators and team members who manage form workflows in the Patient Forms module and decide how completed forms should flow into the EHR.
Benefits of Auto-Import
Eliminates manual importing - Completed forms flow into the EHR without a staff member having to push each one across.
Reduces administrative workload - Front-office teams spend less time on repetitive import tasks, especially on high-volume forms like new patient intake.
Speeds up record updates - Patient charts reflect the latest information shortly after approval instead of waiting in a manual queue.
When Auto-Import Works (Eligibility Requirements)
Auto-Import can only run when Adit knows exactly which patient the form belongs to. For that reason, it is available only when the form is sent through one of the following patient-specific channels:

rows: A specific patient is selected when the form is sent.
The request is tied to a specific patient record.
Rules assign forms to identified patients automatically.
Anyone can complete a public link, so Adit cannot confirm which patient record the submission belongs to.

blocks.x: Important: Forms completed through a public URL cannot be auto-imported. These submissions must be manually matched to the correct patient and then imported by your team. If your practice relies heavily on public form links, plan a manual review workflow for those submissions.
Option 1: Toggle Auto-Import from Form Manager
Use this method to quickly change the setting for one or more forms without opening each one.
Navigate to the Patient Forms module in Adit.
In the left navigation menu, click Form Manager.
Locate the form in the Form Manager list.
Find the Auto-Import column for that form and switch the toggle ON (enabled) or OFF (disabled). The change takes effect immediately.
Option 2: Toggle Auto-Import Within the Form
Use this method when you are already editing a form and want to adjust the setting at the same time.
Open the form for editing from Form Manager.
Locate the Auto-Import setting in the form's configuration options.
Enable or disable the feature.
Click Save to apply your changes.
How to Decide: ON or OFF?

Turn Auto-Import ON for routine, high-volume forms sent to known patients (new patient intake, medical history updates, consent forms sent via Form Requests) where you want charts updated with minimal staff effort.

Keep Auto-Import OFF for forms where your team prefers to review every submission before anything reaches the EHR, or for forms primarily distributed via public URL (where Auto-Import would not apply anyway).
Note: The Auto-Import feature is not available within forms where Multi-Sign is enabled. Frequently Asked Questions

Q: A patient completed a form from our website link, but nothing imported. Why?
Forms completed through a public URL are not eligible for Auto-Import because no specific patient was selected when the form was sent. Locate the submission in Adit, manually match it to the correct patient, and import it.

Q: Does Auto-Import also update the mapped fields, or only upload the PDF?
Both. When Auto-Import runs, Adit uploads the completed PDF to the patient's PMS record and updates every mapped field with the patient's responses.

Q: Is Auto-Import a global setting or per form?
Per form. You can enable it for some forms and leave it off for others, depending on your workflow.

articles.title: How to Use Adit Patient Forms Library

articles.title: View a Patient Form

blocks.x: The Patient Forms dashboard allows you to see forms that have been requested, submitted, and approved, each in an easy, filterable list.
To view a patient form:
Navigate to the Patient Forms module.
In the navigation menu, click on Submission.
Choose which list view you’d like to access:
All - shows all form requests and submissions
Requested - shows forms that your staff requested from patients, but are incomplete. This will also show forms which were sent to patients via Auto-Assign.
Submitted - shows forms that patients submitted, regardless of completion.
Imported - shows forms that your staff approved and pushed to your EHR.
Archived - shows forms that your staff archived from your Patient Forms dashboard.

To approve a patient form:
Navigate to the Patient Forms module.
In the navigation menu, click on Submission.
Click the Submitted tab.
Locate the form you want to approve.
Click the Approve button.
Select existing patient by typing in their name or create a new patient profile.
Click Approve.

articles.title: How To: View and modify a patient's form history

blocks.x: When you assign a form through Adit's Patient Forms module, we automatically track which form was assigned and when. When the patient submits a form through Adit's Patient Forms, we log that information as well. You can view all of this data for each patient in their Form History.
Adit uses the Form History to automate assigning forms to patients on a recurring basis. This is useful for things like asking patients to update their medical history every 12 months.
To view a patient's Form History, open their Patient Card and click on the Patient Forms tile.

The top section shows forms that are currently assigned to the patient but still pending. You can archive these requests by clicking the Archive iconbeside the form name. If you would like to assign an additional form to this patient, click the Assign Form button.

The bottom section of the form history shows all of the forms that this patient has submitted through Adit's Patient Forms feature and the date of each submission. You also have the option to manually log a form by clicking the Add Completed Form button. This allows you to log the date that a form was submitted outside of Adit's Patient Forms system (such as a paper copy) and ensures the Form History remains intact to accurately assign recurring forms.

articles.title: Getting Started, Set Up Treatment Plans (Dental)

blocks.x: The Get Started wizard walks you through the whole module in order: practice details, your treatments, your first template, a test send, then live. Work through it once and treatment plans are ready to use.
Set up the Treatment Plans module, for dental practices
The guided walkthrough covers every stage in order, on the real screens. This article is the written version for when you would rather read it.
Open the interactive walkthrough →
An interactive walkthrough for this topic is available in the online version of this article.

Treatment Plans has a guided setup built into the module. It takes you through every setting in the right order, so nothing is missed and nothing needs revisiting later. This article is the written version of that flow.
Open Treatment Plans from the left navigation menu. Scroll down to see what the module offers, then select Get Started.
Settings are per location

Practice details and branding are stored per location, while treatments and templates are shared across the whole organization. If you run several locations, work through the General Information stage for each of them.
Stage 1: General Information
This is where the core settings for your plans live.
Enter the practice name you want displayed on treatment plans.
Add your practice logo with Choose File. Upload the image, crop it as needed, then select Save.
Set the theme color for your plans. Pick your color, then select Apply.
Enter the email address that will receive submitted treatment plans, then select Save.
Enter the email address that will receive patient replies to a treatment plan request, then select Save.

Set the Auto-Attach toggle. Select Yes to have Adit attach the completed treatment plan PDF to the patient profile in your EHR. You can then choose the destination folder and the format of the PDF file name.
Select Next.
Worth getting right the first time
The PDF folder and naming format decide how every completed plan is filed in your EHR from then on. It is much easier to set now than to reorganize later.
Stage 2: Treatments
Treatments are what eventually go onto your templates and plans. As a dental practice you start with a head start here.
Already there
Adit pulls your existing treatment codes from your EHR and displays them on this page.
Cannot be deleted
Codes from your EHR stay. You can still edit them to attach images or video with the edit icon.
Shared across locations
A treatment created in Adit at one location appears in all of them.
To add something your EHR has no code for, select the create button. Treatments created here live in Adit only and are never written back to your EHR.
Creating a treatment
Enter the treatment code.
Enter the Proc Abbreviation.
Enter the Description, a short label of up to 50 characters.
Enter the Long Description, up to 600 characters, if you want one.
Enter the price.
Select Next.
Add images by selecting the upload area or dragging files in. Paste a YouTube link to attach a video.
Select Create. The next screen shows how the treatment will appear on a patient's plan in Product View.
Once all your treatments are in, select Next.
Stage 3: Templates
A template is a saved plan layout, and you can create as many as you need. Templates built at one location can be used at the others, so one standardized template can serve the whole organization.
Select the create button, name your template, then select Continue.
What appears on the plan
The first section decides what the patient sees at the top. Use the checkboxes to show or hide:
Practice logo
Practice display name
Phone number
Treatment plan name
Patient's insurance information
You can also add a banner. Upload an image, choose which area of it is displayed, and select Save. Banner content, the text that sits with it, can be added below.
Choosing a view
Dental plans can be presented two ways.

rows: A chart of treatments, with phases, tooth numbers, surfaces and insurance coverage
A card per treatment with its images and video
Clinical plans where the detail matters
Work a patient understands by looking at it

blocks.x: Building the plan in Table View
Enable the tooth chart checkbox if you want one on the plan, then pick from the four available charts in the dropdown.
Select Add Treatment(s), search for the codes you want, tick each one and select Add.
The treatments appear in the table with the details you set up earlier already filled in. Every column is editable here.
Use the phases control to break the plan into phases, and drag treatments between them.
Use + Add Option(s) to create a second tab called Option 2, then build its treatments separately.
Use Table Settings to choose which columns show. You can also drag to reorder them, or pin a column to keep it in place.

In Product View, each card shows the treatment code, price and short description, with the longer description below. Both the description and the images can be edited on the plan, and the cards can be dragged into order.
Estimate and discounts
Insurance coverage and discounts can be applied per treatment in the table. To apply them as a flat total for the whole plan, use the estimate section instead.
Manage Discounts applies a discount to the plan total. Name each one and enter a percentage or a dollar value, then save.
Add Insurance Coverage applies insurance. This is mainly for a specific patient's plan, since a template has no patient insurance to reference.
A checkbox displays the ESTIMATE stamp on the plan.
Payment options
Tick the checkbox to enable payment options on the plan.
Choose the payment methods to offer. Credit Card, Convenience Fees and Bank/ACH are only available if you have Adit Pay enabled.
Tick the payment plan checkbox to let patients set up a payment plan.
To reward paying in full, enter a percentage or dollar discount for upfront payment.
To let the patient shape their own schedule, enable the customize option. They then see a Customize button and a slider for the down payment and recurring amount.
Enter a minimum down payment. The patient cannot slide below this.
Set the payment frequency.
Use the two arrows to decide how the plan is calculated. The up arrow sets the total number of payments. The down arrow sets the monthly payment amount instead.
Which arrow to use
For a 24 month plan, use the up arrow and enter 24. For payments of $300 a month until the balance clears, use the down arrow and enter 300.
Consent and forms

Tick the consent checkbox to collect any of the following: a patient signature, patient consent forms, a doctor signature, or agreement to your terms and conditions. Tick the terms checkbox to require agreement, and customize the message shown. Separate checkboxes require the patient signature and the doctor signature.
To require forms once a patient accepts, attach them with the patient forms button.
Multiple locations
If this template will be used across several locations, select the form for each location. Forms are stored per location, and the patient only sees the one belonging to the location treating them.
Finish the template
Preview the template to see how it looks, then select Save Template. Once all your templates are built, move on.
Stage 4: Test it
Before going live, send a plan to yourself and check it end to end.
Pull up a test patient profile.
Select the Patient Info tab.
Scroll to the treatment plan section and select + Add.
Fill in the required information and select Continue.
Customize the plan as you want it, then select Save & Send.
Send the request by text message, email, or both.
Check your email and text messages and review the plan as the patient sees it.
Check the plan in the Adit forms app.
Check the treatment plan PDF in your EHR.
Stage 5: Go Live
The last screen summarizes everything you set up. Use the edit icon to revise anything that is not right. When it all looks good, select Go Live and you can start sending treatment plans.
FAQs
Do I have to complete the wizard in one sitting?
No. The stages are ordered so each one builds on the last, but you can leave and come back. The summary screen at the end shows what is configured and lets you revise any stage.
Do I need to run this for every location?
Practice details and branding are per location, so those need setting for each one. Treatments and templates are shared across the whole organization, so you only build those once.
Which payment methods need Adit Pay?
Credit Card, Bank/ACH and Convenience Fees all require Adit Pay, as do payment plans. Cash and Check work without it, with the payment settled in person.
Can I apply insurance while building a template?
Not meaningfully. A template has no patient attached, so there is no insurance to reference. Add Insurance Coverage is used when customizing a specific patient's plan.
What is the difference between the two arrows in the payment plan section?

They decide how the schedule is calculated. The up arrow sets the total number of payments, for example 24 months. The down arrow sets the monthly amount instead, for example $300 a month until the balance clears.

articles.title: Guide to Treatment Plans

blocks.x: Adit provides practices with the tools to compile treatment plans, send treatment plans to patients to sign, and set up payments and payment plans for treatment plans.
Treatment Plans live within the Patient Forms module in Adit’s platform.
The typical process to create, send, and approve a treatment plan through Adit looks like this:
Practice creates or imports the treatment plan, including available treatment options, payment options, and discounts.
Practice sends the treatment plan.
Patient receives a text and/or email with a link to their treatment plan.

Patient reviews the treatment plan and selects from the provided options for treatment and payment, then signs the plan and any attached forms, completes any required payment, and submits the treatment plan.
Practice receives a notification that the treatment plan has been accepted.
If required, the practice can countersign the treatment plan before pushing it to the patient file in the EHR/PMS software.
Treatment Plan Status
There are several statuses used over the life of a Treatment Plan:
Draft - a Treatment Plan that has been created and saved, but not yet sent to a patient.
Requested - a Treatment Plan that has been sent to a patient and is waiting for their approval.
Pending Sign - a Treatment Plan that has been completed by the patient and is awaiting signature from the practice.
Accepted - a Treatment Plan that has been completed by the patient and signed by the practice (if required).
Canceled - a Treatment Plan that has been canceled.
Archived - an accepted Treatment Plan that has been archived.
Navigate Treatment Plans

To reach the Treatment Plans dashboard, navigate to the Patient Forms module, then select Treatment Plans from the top navigation menu. From this page, you can view the Overview of Treatment Plans for all of your locations, or select a specific location from the left navigation menu to see only the Treatment Plans for that location.
Each location page (including the Overview) has six tabs at the top to choose from, which allow you to narrow down what Treatment Plans appear in the list.
All
Draft
Requested
Submitted
Canceled
Archived
You can also search for Treatment Plans using the Search box at the top right corner of the Treatment Plans dashboard. You can search by Treatment Plan Name or by Patient Name.
For more information on how to create, manage, and customize Treatment Plans, please see our How To articles!

articles.title: Understanding Treatment Plans (Dental)

blocks.x: Treatment Plans is now its own module, included in Adit Core. Insurance now breaks down on every treatment row, templates have their own page, and patients can shape their own payment plan.
What is new in Treatment Plans, for dental practices
Click through the real screens at your own pace. Most people find the walkthrough faster than reading this page, and this article is here for the detail afterwards.
Open the interactive walkthrough →
An interactive walkthrough for this topic is available in the online version of this article.
This guide covers where the module lives, what each page does, and how a plan is built from the first treatment through to the patient signing it.
For dental practices

This article describes the dental build. Orthodontic, chiropractic and optometry practices have a different build, with no tooth chart, phases or table view. Use the version of this article written for those specialties instead.
Where to find Treatment Plans
Open Treatment Plans from the left navigation menu. Four tabs run across the top, each with a distinct job.
Tx Plans
Create, send, review and track plans for individual patients. The list shows the location and current status of each plan.
Templates
Reusable plan layouts, so a new plan opens with the treatments, columns, payment options, forms and consent you want.
Treatments
The practice master list, with pricing, descriptions, images and video.
Preferences
Branding, coordinator emails, signing rules, delivery settings and default consent text.
What has changed

If you have built treatment plans in Adit before, most of the workflow will feel familiar. The one change practices notice first is the insurance breakdown. Coverage now sits on the treatment rather than on the plan total, so when a patient asks what happens if they defer the surgery and just do the extractions, the figures update as soon as you remove a row. No more working it out on a calculator while the patient waits.
The full list of changes 13 differences from the previous build

rows: A single page inside the Forms module
A dedicated module with four pages
One preset layout, configured in Preferences
As many templates as you need, on their own page
One coverage total for the whole plan
Primary coverage, secondary coverage and patient pay on every treatment row
Up to five, each a percentage or a dollar amount
A fixed set you could show or hide
Columns you can show, hide, reorder and pin
Only the codes synced from your EHR
Synced codes plus treatments you create yourself
Four numbering systems, including primary teeth
A single tooth, a range, letters, or a bridge quadrant
A surface column on each treatment
Table View or Product View, with images and video
Phases are preserved, and Dentrix is now supported
The practice set what the patient received
The patient can adjust the plan within limits you set

blocks.x: What lives where
Treatments and Templates are shared across the organization. Preferences and Treatment Plans are specific to each location. This one distinction explains most of the behavior you will run into.

rows: One treatment table serves every location. Codes synced from your EHR carry the location they came from.
A template built in one location is available in all the others.
Branding, display name and default text are set per location.
A plan belongs to the patient's location, and payment posts there.

blocks.x: Worth knowing

If a patient is seen at one location but will pay at another, create the plan under the location that will collect the payment. The plan and its payment follow the patient record, not the appointment location.
Treatments
The Treatments page is the master list of everything the practice can put on a plan. Treatments get there in two ways.
Treatments synced from your EHR

Adit pulls the treatment codes from the master list in your EHR, across every location. For each one it brings the code, the description and the procedure abbreviation. It does not bring the price, so that is yours to set in Adit.
Because the same code normally exists at each location, you will see it listed once per location with the location named on the row. That Location label only appears on codes that came from the EHR.
Treatments you create in Adit
You can also add treatments of your own, with your own code, description, price, images and video. Anything created in Adit stays in Adit and is never written back to your EHR.
This is a real change from the old workflow. A plan used to be limited to whatever the sync returned, so anything your EHR had no code for could not be presented at all. Now it can.
Full instructions are in How to Create Treatments, for dental practices.
Templates

A template is a saved plan layout. You set it up once and pick it when you create a plan, rather than rebuilding the same thing each time. This is where the old preset settings from Preferences have gone, and you are no longer limited to one.

Go to Templates and add a template, give it a name, then either start from scratch or pick an existing template to copy. Copying creates a new template prefilled with everything from the one you chose, which you can then edit freely.
Templates across locations

Templates are organization level, so the treatment list and the form list inside a template show entries from every location, each labeled with the location it belongs to. When you create a plan for a patient, Adit filters both lists down to that patient's location.

So if a template will be used across several locations, add the treatment and the form for each of those locations when you build it. Selecting only the version belonging to one location leaves the template with nothing to offer patients at the others.
Preferences
Preferences holds practice settings only, since the preset plan layout has moved to Templates. These settings are per location, so check them for every location you operate.
Branding. The display name shown on every plan, your logo, a theme color and a banner template image.
Email settings. The address that receives submitted plans, and a separate address for replies to a plan request. Each has its own Save.
Plan settings. Auto attach, e-sign and who may sign. See below.
Consent message. The default terms and conditions text displayed on a plan.
Thank you page. The message a patient sees after completing their plan.
Request messaging. The text message and email templates sent when a plan goes out.
Three settings worth pausing on
Auto Attach
Puts the completed plan PDF on the patient profile in your EHR. Switch it on and you also choose the destination folder and the file naming format.
E-sign
Set to Yes, the patient enters their name, phone number and email alongside their signature. Set to No, they simply sign.
Signers allowed
Controls which users at your practice may sign a plan. Only these users can complete the doctor signature field.
Previewing a template

Branding is per location, so a template previewed with All Locations selected at the top of Adit shows no logo and no practice name. Switch to a specific location to see the plan as that location's patients will.
Interactive walkthrough Treatment Plan Preferences (Dental) , click through it here
Open the interactive walkthrough →
An interactive walkthrough for this topic is available in the online version of this article.
Open it full screen if you would rather have the room.
The plan builder

The builder is where a plan comes together. It uses the same layout as Booking Links in Online Scheduling: configure on the left, watch a live preview of the patient view on the right. Everything below appears in both the template builder and the plan builder, so anything you set up in advance can still be adjusted for one patient.
The top of the plan

Whatever you name the plan appears at the top of the patient view. You choose whether to show your logo, the practice display name and the practice phone number, all of which come from Preferences for that location. If no phone number is set, the line simply comes through empty, so check Preferences before switching it on.

Below that sit the patient name and date of birth, added for you. You can also show a benefits section that pulls the patient's insurance from your EHR and displays the carrier, deductible and remaining benefit. If the patient has nothing on file the section stays hidden even when it is switched on, so there is no empty block on the page. A few EHRs do not return the deductible and remaining figures, in which case Adit shows what it does receive.

There is also space for a banner image and banner text. New accounts have no default banner, so nothing appears until you add one. If you were already using treatment plans and had a banner stored, that banner carries over untouched.
The tooth chart
The chart can be shown or hidden on any plan, and four numbering systems are available so it can match both the convention your practice follows and the patient in the chair.
The four numbering systems

rows: Permanent teeth in the FDI two digit notation
Primary teeth lettered A to T
Primary teeth in the FDI two digit notation

blocks.x: The primary teeth charts are new. Practices working with children previously had no chart that fit.
Enter a tooth number on a treatment row and that tooth lights up on the chart. The field takes more than a single number:
a single tooth, such as 5
a range, such as 1-3, for a treatment covering several teeth at once
letters, when you are on a child chart
a bridge quadrant, entered as UR, UL, LL or LR, which the field reads as upper right, upper left, lower left and lower right
Next to the tooth, a Surface column records which surface the treatment applies to, so a cavity on the inner side of a tooth is documented on the treatment itself instead of in a note somewhere.
Adult chart, with a treatment applied.
Child chart, with a treatment applied.
Adding treatments to a plan
Select Add Treatment to bring treatments onto the plan. There are two sources.
ALL TREATMENTS
Unplanned Treatments
Everything available in Adit: codes migrated from your EHR plus treatments you created
In a template, treatments from every location are available
In a patient plan, the list filters to that patient's location
FROM THE EHR
Planned Treatments
Treatments already on the patient's plan in your EHR
Unscheduled: planned but not yet attached to an appointment
Scheduled: attached to an appointment but not completed
Not available in templates, since a template has no patient
Search by code, description or surface, add what you need, then drag the rows into the order that best fits the conversation.
Importing a plan the patient already has

If a treatment plan already exists in your EHR there is no need to rebuild it. When you create a plan, choose to use the existing plan rather than starting from scratch, and Adit brings the treatments across. Phases are preserved, where previously everything landed in Phase 1 and had to be reorganized by hand.

Dentrix works differently, because Adit cannot read the plan directly. Export the patient's treatment plan from Dentrix as a PDF and upload it. Adit reads the file and builds the plan from it, including the treatments, the phases and the primary and secondary insurance.
Dentrix only
The PDF upload path is offered on Dentrix. Every other supported EHR imports the plan directly.
The Dentrix PDF upload.
The imported plan in the builder.
The treatments table

Table View lays the plan out one treatment per row and is the default for dental. Use Table Settings to choose which columns appear, drag them into the order your team already reads in, and pin a column to keep it in place while you scroll.
Column reference all 11 columns

rows: The treatment priority on the plan.
A tooth number, a range, a letter, or a bridge quadrant.
The surface the treatment applies to.
The treatment description, editable on the plan.
From your EHR for synced codes, or from the price you set.
What the primary insurance is expected to cover.
What the secondary insurance is expected to cover.
Any discount applied to that treatment.
What the patient owes, calculated for you.

blocks.x: Where the amounts come from
For treatments imported from your EHR, the fee and the expected primary and secondary coverage are populated when the patient has insurance on file.
For treatments created in Adit there is no insurance information to reference. The fee comes from the treatment price, and coverage starts at zero for you to enter.
In both cases Patient Pay is calculated from the fee, the coverage and any discount. Every figure can be overridden directly on the plan without changing the master treatment or anything in your EHR.
Phases

Phases group treatments into the stages care actually happens in. An implant is the obvious example: the tooth comes out, the area heals for a few weeks, and only then does the implant go in. Those belong in separate phases rather than as three lines on one list.
Add a phase, then drag treatments into it. Phases are available in Table View only.
Table View and Product View

Dental plans can be presented either way. Table View is the default and carries the clinical detail. Product View shows each treatment as a card with its images and any video after them, which suits work a patient understands better by looking at it: aligners, whitening, cosmetic treatment, or retail items such as night guards.

In Product View each card shows the treatment code, price and short description, with the longer description below. That description can be edited and further images added directly on the plan, without going back to the Treatments page.

rows: A card per treatment with images and video

blocks.x: Table View.
The same plan in Product View.
Presenting more than one option

A plan can carry up to five options, each holding its own set of treatments. Select + Add Option(s) and a new tab appears on the plan, which you then build the same way. The patient sees the options grouped and clearly labeled.

Use options to present a choice rather than a decision already made: comprehensive treatment against a phased approach, or a premium material against a standard one. It saves sending two or three separate plans.
The Estimate

The Estimate section summarizes the plan. Select Add Insurance Coverage to open a window showing the patient's insurance policies from the EHR, then set what the primary and secondary policies should cover. Coverage starts at $0 rather than arriving as a lump sum, so each amount reflects what you intend.
Select Manage Discounts to apply up to five discounts, each named and entered as either a percentage or a dollar amount. A percentage is calculated from what the patient owes.
The Fee Structure then gives the whole picture: total fee, insurance coverage, discounts and final patient responsibility. There is also a checkbox to display the ESTIMATE stamp on the plan.

Because coverage and discounts are applied at treatment level, removing a treatment updates the totals immediately. That makes it easy to compare what the patient owes for half the treatment this year and the rest next year, without leaving the screen.
How the patient pays
Payment sits at the bottom of the plan and runs through Adit Pay. Nothing is enabled by default, so each plan starts with payment switched off until you turn it on.
Payment method

Turn on the requirement to collect payment, then choose the methods. Cash and Check let the patient accept the plan and settle in person with nothing processed in Adit, and these work whether or not Adit Pay is set up. Credit Card and Bank/ACH, where enabled, run through Adit Pay. If Adit Pay is not set up for that location the online section is disabled and the plan tells you Adit Pay is required.
A Convenience Fee, where you have one configured in Adit Pay, applies to one time payments only, and the option stays unavailable until Credit Card is selected.
Payment options
Payment options become available once payment is required. From there you decide whether the patient pays in full, over time, or gets the choice of both.
One time payment
The patient settles the full amount. You can offer a discount for paying in full, entered as a percentage or a dollar amount.
Payment in installments
Set the frequency, the amount due today and either a recurring amount or a total number of payments. Adit builds the schedule.
Nothing is prefilled

The frequency and the number of payments both need entering before a plan can be sent. Installments also need at least one online method, Credit Card or Bank/ACH, since there is nothing to charge against otherwise. Leave payment options switched off entirely and the patient simply sees the payment method section and pays the full amount.
Letting the patient set their own payment plan

You can go one step further and let the patient build the schedule themselves. Switch this on and they see a Customize option, with a slider between what they put down today and what they pay each period. A bigger deposit brings the recurring amount down, a smaller one pushes it up, and a Reset button returns them to the figures you set.
You still hold the terms. The practice chooses the frequency and can set a minimum down payment, so the patient cannot slide below what you are prepared to accept.
Forms and consent

Attach any forms the patient needs to complete when they accept the plan, such as a consent form, a financial agreement or post operative instructions. Forms are stored by location, so the list shows every form across your locations with the location named beside it, and the patient sees only the form belonging to the location treating them.

Consent is a separate section. Switch it on to require a patient or guardian signature, a doctor signature, or both, and choose whether the full consent text is displayed. The text comes from your default consent message in Preferences.
Previewing, saving and sending
Preview, at the top of the builder, shows the plan exactly as the patient will see it. Worth using before anything goes out, particularly the first few times.

A plan can be saved at any point, including before any treatments are on it, so you can set one up and come back to it. Once a treatment is added its details need completing, and a plan cannot be sent without at least one treatment on it.
To send one from a saved template, go to Tx Plans, select New Plan, fill in the patient details and choose your template. The plan loads prefilled and is ready to go.
What the patient receives
The patient gets a link by text, email or both, depending on your Preferences. Opening it on a phone or computer shows the plan exactly as it appeared in your preview.
At the top they see your logo, practice name and phone number, followed by the plan name and their own name and date of birth. A Download button lets them keep a copy.
What appears, section by section
Treatments and fees
The treatments appear next, grouped by option where options were used. Each one shows its code, price, description and any attached images or video. The Fee Structure and total follow below.
Payment

Where payment is required, the patient chooses between a one time payment and installments. The installment side shows the amount due today, the remaining balance, the payment frequency, the number of payments, the recurring amount and a link to view the full schedule.
The payment methods you enabled appear below. Where a Convenience Fee applies, the patient sees the actual fee amount rather than how it is calculated.
Consent, forms and submission

The final sections hold the consent text, the terms checkbox and the signature fields, followed by any forms you attached, each with its own Start button. Nothing is submitted until the patient selects Submit at the end.

Once submitted, the plan goes to your treatment coordinator email address and, where auto attach is on, the completed PDF is attached to the patient's file in your EHR. Card payments show as taken, bank payments show as processing while they clear. Any payment plan the patient accepted is created in Adit Pay and managed from there.
The patient view, top of the plan.
The patient view, payment section.
The patient view, consent, forms and submit.
FAQs
Do I still need Practice Analytics to use treatment plans?
No. Treatment Plans is part of Adit Core, so it is available without Practice Analytics.
Why is the same treatment code listed several times?
Because it exists at more than one location, and Adit migrated each one. The Location column on the row tells you which is which. That column only appears on codes that came from your EHR.
Will editing a treatment code in Adit change it in my EHR?

No. Nothing in Adit is written back to your EHR. Be aware of the reverse, though: the code, description and abbreviation belong to your EHR, so if that record changes there, the next sync overwrites what you typed in Adit. Change those fields in your EHR and use Adit for the price and the media.
Can I use one template across all of my locations?

Yes, templates are organization level. Treatment codes and patient forms are stored per location though, so add the treatment and the form for each location the template will serve. When you create the plan, Adit filters both lists down to the patient's location.
Why does my template preview show no logo or practice name?
Because All Locations is selected at the top of Adit. Branding lives in Preferences, which is per location. Switch to a specific location and the preview fills in.
Can a patient pay by cash or check if we do not have Adit Pay?
Yes. Cash and Check work whether or not Adit Pay is set up. Credit Card, Bank/ACH and payment plans all require Adit Pay, and the online section stays disabled without it.
Does the convenience fee apply to payment plans?
No. A convenience fee applies to one time payments only, and the option stays unavailable until Credit Card is selected as a payment method.
Can I show a patient more than one treatment option?
Yes, up to five. Select + Add Option(s) to create a new tab on the plan and build its treatments separately. The patient sees each option grouped and labeled.
Why can I not send a plan I just built?

A plan needs at least one treatment before it can be sent, and any treatment you added needs its details completed. You can still save an empty plan and come back to it. If you offered installments, the frequency and the number of payments also need entering, since neither is prefilled.

blocks.x: Treatment plans are new to your specialty. Send a patient a branded page showing what you recommend, what it costs, what insurance covers and how they can pay, and let them sign it from their phone.
Set up and use Treatment Plans, for ortho, chiro and opto
Click through the real screens at your own pace. Most people find the walkthrough faster than reading this page, and this article is here for the detail afterwards.
Open the interactive walkthrough →
An interactive walkthrough for this topic is available in the online version of this article.
Until this release, treatment plans were available to dental practices only. They are now available to orthodontic, chiropractic and optometry practices as part of Adit Core.

A treatment plan is a page you send to a patient showing the care you are recommending, the cost, what their insurance covers and how they can pay. They open it on a phone or computer, choose how to pay, complete any forms and sign. The finished plan comes back to your coordinator inbox and attaches to their patient file as a PDF.
A separate article covers dental
The dental build is different, with a tooth chart, phases and a table layout that do not apply here. Use this article for orthodontic, chiropractic and optometry practices.
What is different in your build
The dental build carries clinical machinery that does not apply outside dentistry. Rather than leave unused controls on the screen, those parts are simply not present for you.
What is not in your build, and why 8 differences from the dental build

rows: There is no master procedure code list to pull from in your systems
Treatments are presented as cards with images rather than as clinical rows
Your treatments have a name instead, and the code is there if you use one
Pulled where your system provides it
Carrier, deductible and remaining benefit are shown when available

blocks.x: Everything else works the same as it does for dental: templates, branding, payments through Adit Pay, attached forms, consent and the patient view.
Where to find Treatment Plans
Open Treatment Plans from the left navigation menu. Four tabs run across the top.
Tx Plans
Create, send, review and track plans for individual patients. The list shows the location and current status of each plan.
Templates
Reusable plan layouts, so a new plan opens with the treatments, payment options, forms and consent you want.
Treatments
Your list of what the practice offers, with pricing, descriptions, images and video.
Preferences
Branding, coordinator emails, signing rules, delivery settings and default consent text.
Start with your treatments
Your Treatments page starts empty, because nothing is pulled in from your system. Before you can build a plan you need a list of what you offer.

This is a smaller job than it sounds. Most practices in your specialty work from somewhere between fifteen and thirty treatments, not the hundreds of codes a dental practice carries, so an afternoon usually covers it and you never have to do it again.
Orthodontic
Metal braces, ceramic braces, aligners, retainers, consultations.
Chiropractic
Adjustments, rehabilitation sessions, supplements, supports.
Optometry
Eye exams, contact lens fittings, frames, lens options.
Because plans are presented as cards rather than a table, images are worth adding. A patient choosing between frame styles or aligner options is making a visual decision.
Full instructions are in How to Create Treatments, for ortho, chiro and opto practices.
What lives where
Three scopes are at work, and knowing which is which explains most of what you will see.

rows: Create a treatment once and it is available in every location.
A template built in one location is available in all of them.
Branding, display name and default text are set per location.
A plan belongs to the patient's location, and payment posts there.

blocks.x: Worth knowing

If a patient consults at one location and is treated and pays at another, create the plan under the location that will collect the payment. The plan and its payment follow the patient record, not the appointment.
Templates

A template is a saved plan layout. You set it up once and use it when creating a plan, rather than rebuilding the same thing each time. This is where templates earn their keep in your specialty, because you tend to present the same few packages repeatedly.

An orthodontic practice might keep a template for comprehensive treatment, one for aligners and one for retention. An optometry practice might separate eye exams, contact lenses and glasses. A chiropractic practice might keep a template per care package.
Go to Templates, add one, give it a name and select Continue. Start from scratch, or pick an existing template to copy, which creates a new template prefilled with everything from the one you chose.
Templates across locations
Templates are organization level, and so are your treatments. A treatment added to a template is available everywhere the template is used, with no extra setup.

Forms are the exception. They are stored at location level, so the form list in a template shows every form across your locations with the location named beside each one. If a template will be used in more than one place, add the form for each. The patient then sees only the form belonging to the location treating them.
Preferences
Preferences holds your practice settings, and they are set per location.
Branding. The display name shown on every plan, your logo, a theme color and a banner template image.
Email settings. The address that receives submitted plans, and a separate address for replies to a plan request. Each has its own Save.
Plan settings. Auto attach, e-sign and who may sign. See below.
Consent message. The default terms and conditions text displayed on a plan.
Thank you page. The message a patient sees after completing their plan.
Request messaging. The text message and email templates sent when a plan goes out.
Three settings worth pausing on
Auto Attach
Puts the completed plan PDF on the patient profile. Switch it on and you also choose the destination folder and the file naming format.
E-sign
Set to Yes, the patient enters their name, phone number and email alongside their signature. Set to No, they simply sign.
Signers allowed
Controls which users at your practice may sign a plan. Only these users can complete the doctor signature field.
Previewing a template

Branding is per location, so a template previewed with All Locations selected at the top of Adit shows no logo and no practice name. Switch to a specific location to see the plan as that location's patients will.
Building a plan

You configure the plan on one side and can preview what the patient will receive at any point. Everything below appears in both the template builder and the plan builder, so anything you set up in advance can still be changed for one patient.
The top of the plan

Whatever you name the plan appears at the top. You choose whether to show your logo, the practice display name and the practice phone number, all of which come from Preferences for that location. If no phone number is set, the line comes through empty, so check Preferences before switching it on.
There is also space for a banner image and banner text. Nothing is added by default, so the banner stays empty until you put something there.
Adding treatments
Select Add Treatment(s) and choose from your list. You can add several at once, and if something is missing you can create it from this window without leaving the plan.

Each treatment appears as a card carrying its images, its video after them, the price, the short description and the longer description below. You can edit that description or add further images directly on the plan, without going back to the Treatments page. Drag the cards to arrange them in the order that suits the conversation.
Insurance coverage is added here with Add Insurance Coverage. Where your system provides it, Adit shows the carrier, the deductible and the remaining benefit.
Discounts are added with Manage Discounts.
Presenting more than one option

A plan can carry up to five options, each holding its own set of treatments. Select + Add Option(s) and a new tab appears on the plan, which you then build separately. The patient sees them grouped and labeled, so you can lay out alternatives on a single plan instead of sending two or three.

This is worth knowing about in your specialty, because a first consultation is usually a conversation about choices. An orthodontic practice can put metal braces against ceramic against aligners. An optometry practice can show a basic lens package beside a premium one. A chiropractic practice can offer a short course of care beside a longer one.
The estimate

The estimate totals the plan. Add Insurance Coverage opens a window showing the patient's insurance, where you set what the primary and secondary policies should cover. These start at zero, so what you enter is deliberate.

You can also apply up to five discounts, each named and entered as a percentage or a dollar amount, where a percentage is taken from what the patient owes. The Fee Structure then shows the total fee, the coverage, the discounts and the final patient figure. There is also a checkbox to display the ESTIMATE stamp on the plan.
How the patient pays
Payment sits at the bottom of the plan and runs through Adit Pay. Nothing is switched on by default, so every plan starts with payment off until you decide otherwise.
Payment method

Turn on the requirement to collect payment, then choose the methods. Cash and Check let the patient accept the plan and settle in person with nothing processed in Adit, and these work whether or not Adit Pay is set up. Credit Card and Bank/ACH, where enabled, run through Adit Pay. If Adit Pay is not set up for that location the online section is disabled and the plan tells you Adit Pay is required.
A Convenience Fee, where you have one configured in Adit Pay, applies to one time payments only and stays unavailable until Credit Card is selected.
Payment options
Payment options become available once payment is required.

One time payment. The patient settles the full amount. You can offer a discount for paying in full, entered as a percentage or a dollar amount, which exists only while payment options are switched on.
Payment in installments. You set the payment frequency, the amount due today and either a recurring amount or a total number of payments, and Adit builds the schedule.
Nothing is prefilled

The frequency and the number of payments both need entering before a plan can be sent. Installments also need at least one online method, Credit Card or Bank/ACH. Leave payment options off and the patient simply sees the payment method section and pays the full amount.
Letting the patient set their own payment plan

You can let the patient build their own schedule. Turn this on and they see a Customize option, with a slider between what they pay today and what they pay each period. A larger deposit lowers the recurring amount, a smaller one raises it, and Reset brings the schedule back to your original figures.
You still control the terms. Set the payment frequency and a minimum down payment, so the patient cannot adjust the schedule below what you are willing to accept.

This one was built with orthodontics in mind. The first consultation is often when a patient decides whether to move forward, so letting them find a payment amount that works while they are already looking at the plan can remove the need for a call back to the office.
Forms and consent

Attach any forms the patient needs to complete when they accept the plan, such as a financial agreement or a care agreement. Forms are stored per location, so each form in the list is labeled with its location and the patient sees only the one belonging to the location treating them.

Consent is separate. Turn it on to require a signature from the patient or guardian, the doctor, or both, and choose whether to display the full consent text. The text comes from your default consent message in Preferences.
Previewing, saving and sending
Preview, at the top of the builder, shows the plan exactly as the patient will see it. Worth using before anything goes out, particularly the first few times.
A plan can be saved at any point, even before any treatments are added. Once a treatment is added its details need completing, and a plan cannot be sent without at least one treatment on it.
To send one from a saved template, go to Tx Plans, select New Plan, fill in the patient details and choose your template. The plan loads prefilled and is ready to go.
What the patient receives
The patient receives a link by text, email or both, depending on your Preferences, and opens the plan on a phone or computer exactly as it appeared in your preview.

At the top they see your logo, practice name and phone number, followed by the plan name and their own name and date of birth. A Download button lets them keep a copy. Their treatments follow as cards, grouped by option where options were used, each showing the price, the description and any images or video. The fee structure and total appear below.
What appears, section by section

Where payment is required, they choose between a one time payment and installments. The installment side shows the amount due today, the remaining balance, the frequency, the number of payments and the recurring amount, with a link to view the full schedule. The payment methods you enabled appear below, and a convenience fee is shown as its actual amount rather than as a rule.

Last come the consent text, the terms checkbox and the signature fields, followed by any forms you attached, each with its own Start button. Nothing is submitted until the patient selects Submit at the end.

After submission the plan is sent to your coordinator email address and attached to the patient's file as a PDF. Card payments show as collected, bank payments show as processing while they clear. Any payment plan the patient accepts is created in Adit Pay and managed from there.

FAQs
Can Adit pull my treatments in automatically?

No. Treatment codes are migrated for dental practices only, because dental systems carry a standard master code list. In your specialty you build the list in Adit, which usually means fifteen to thirty treatments.
Why is there no tooth chart or table view in my account?

Both are dental features. Your plans are presented in product view, which shows each treatment as a card with its images and video. Phases, tooth numbers and the per treatment insurance columns are dental only as well.
Do I have to create each treatment for every location?
No. Treatments are created once for the whole organization and are available everywhere. Patient forms are the exception, since those are stored per location.
Can I use one template across all of my locations?
Yes. Templates are organization level, as are your treatments. Add the appropriate patient form for each location the template will serve, since forms are per location.
Why does my template preview show no logo or practice name?
Because All Locations is selected at the top of Adit. Branding lives in Preferences, which is per location. Switch to a specific location and the preview fills in.
Will insurance information show on my plans?

Where your system provides it. Adit displays the carrier and, where available, the deductible and remaining benefit. If the patient has nothing on file the section stays hidden, so there is no empty block on the page.
Can a patient pay by cash or check if we do not have Adit Pay?
Yes. Cash and Check work whether or not Adit Pay is set up. Credit Card, Bank/ACH and payment plans all require Adit Pay.
Can I show a patient more than one treatment option?

Yes, up to five. Select + Add Option(s) to create a new tab on the plan and build its treatments separately. This is the usual way to present braces against aligners, or a basic package beside a premium one.

articles.title: How to Create Treatments (Dental)

blocks.x: Your treatment codes arrive from your EHR on their own. What they do not arrive with is a price, and your EHR has no code for the elective work you want to present. This is how you fill both gaps.
How to create treatments, for dental practices
Two minutes, clicking through the real screens. Come back here for the field reference and the answers to the usual questions.
Open the interactive walkthrough →
An interactive walkthrough for this topic is available in the online version of this article.
Treatments are the building blocks of every treatment plan. Before you can present a plan to a patient, Adit needs to know what you offer and what it costs.

As a dental practice you start ahead, because your treatment codes come across from your EHR. This guide covers what arrives on its own, what you need to add, and how to create a treatment of your own when your EHR has no code for it.
What arrives from your EHR
Adit migrates the master treatment code list from your EHR for every location. For each code it brings across three things:
Treatment code
The code itself, which doubles as the name of the treatment in dental.
Description
The description held against the code in your EHR.
Procedure abbreviation
The short form your team already uses.
It does not bring the price. Fees are set in Adit, so a newly migrated code arrives without one until you add it.

Because the same code normally exists at each location, you will see it listed once per location with the location named on the row. That label only appears on codes that came from the EHR, never on ones you create yourself.
Setting a price on a migrated code
Open the treatment from the Actions column, enter the price, and save. You can add images and video at the same time.
Prices you set in Adit stay in Adit. Nothing on this page is ever written back to your EHR.
One thing to watch

The code, description and abbreviation belong to your EHR. If that record changes there, the next sync brings the change into Adit and overwrites what you typed in those fields. Change them in your EHR rather than here, and use Adit for the price and the media.
Creating your own treatment

Create a treatment in Adit when your EHR has no code for something you want to present. Elective and retail items are the usual case: whitening, night guards, cosmetic work, anything sold rather than coded.
1. Open the Treatments page
Go to Tx Plans in the left navigation menu, then the Treatments tab.
2. Start a new treatment
Select + Add Treatment. The Create Treatment window opens on the first of two steps.
3. Fill in the details
Five fields, in this order. Only the treatment code is required.

rows: The treatment code. In dental this doubles as the name of the treatment, so use something your team recognizes.
The short form your team uses for the procedure.
A brief label, up to 50 characters. This is the line that appears beside the code and price on a plan.
A fuller explanation for the patient, up to 600 characters. This is the paragraph that sits under the treatment, and it can be customized on any individual plan.
The default fee. You can override it on any individual plan.

blocks.x: Select Next to move on.
4. Add images or video
The second step is optional, but worth doing for any treatment a patient understands better when they can see it.
SUPPORTED
Images
Drag files into the upload area, or browse to select them
Only .jpeg and .png files
Up to 10 MB each
No limit on how many you add
YOUTUBE ONLY
Video
Paste a YouTube URL and select Add
YouTube links only, no file uploads
One video per treatment
Adit tells you if the link is not valid

Anything you add here appears when the treatment is used on a plan presented in Product View, with images first and the video after them. Table View shows the treatment details instead, so media is most useful for elective work you want to present visually.
5. Create it
Select Create. The window closes with your treatment in the list, ready to add to a plan. Back returns you to the details if something needs changing first.
Finding your way around the list
The list shows the treatment title, the code, the location for migrated codes, how many images or videos are attached, the description, the price and the actions available.

By default it is sorted by what was updated most recently, and you can sort by treatment code instead. Search by code or description to find something quickly, which is the fastest route when the same code repeats across several locations.
Editing and deleting
Both actions live in the Actions column on each row.
Use the edit iconto change the price, description or media at any time.
Treatments you created in Adit can be removed with the trash can icon.
Codes imported from your EHR cannot be deleted, because your EHR owns them. Retire the code in your EHR instead and the change follows through on the next sync.
Deleting is safe for work already done
A treatment you remove from this list stays on any treatment plan or template that already uses it, so a plan a patient is still looking at will not change underneath them.
Worth knowing
There is one treatment table for the whole organization. Treatments you create are available in every location without being recreated.
Creating, editing or deleting a treatment in Adit changes nothing on the EHR side.
A plan can override anything. Description, fee, coverage and discounts are all editable on an individual plan without touching the master treatment.
Set a price even where it varies. A default saves time on every plan, and you can still adjust per patient.
FAQs
My codes are already listed. Do I need to create anything?
Prices, in most cases. Create a treatment when you want to present something your EHR has no code for, such as whitening or a night guard.
Why is the same code showing several times?
Because it exists at more than one location, and Adit migrated each one. The location on the row tells you which is which.
Why can I not delete one of these?
It came from your EHR, and your EHR owns it. Retire the code there instead, and the change reaches Adit on the next sync.
Does Adit pull the price from my EHR?
No. Only the code, description and procedure abbreviation are migrated. The price is set in Adit.
Can I upload a video file?
No. Video needs to be hosted on YouTube and added as a URL, one per treatment.
Does the price include insurance?
No. The price is the full fee. Coverage and discounts are applied on the plan itself, where Adit calculates what the patient owes.
Will my images show on every treatment plan?
They show in Product View, which presents each treatment as a card. Table View, the default for dental, shows the treatment details in a row instead.

articles.title: How to Create Treatments (Ortho Chiro Opto)

blocks.x: Your Treatments page starts empty, and that is the point. You build the list once, for the whole organization, and it is there in every location from then on.
How to create treatments, for ortho, chiro and opto
Two minutes, clicking through the real screens. Come back here for the field reference and the answers to the usual questions.
Open the interactive walkthrough →
An interactive walkthrough for this topic is available in the online version of this article.
Treatments are the building blocks of every treatment plan. Before you can send a plan to a patient, Adit needs to know what you offer and what it costs.

Nothing is pulled in from your system, so the list is yours to build. That is a smaller job than it sounds. Most practices in your specialty work from somewhere between fifteen and thirty treatments, so an afternoon usually covers it, and you never have to do it again.
Before you start
You will need access to the Treatment Plans module.
It helps to write your list out first. Focus on what you actually present to a patient rather than everything the practice could conceivably do.
Orthodontic
Metal braces, ceramic braces, aligners, retainers, consultations.
Chiropractic
Adjustments, rehabilitation sessions, supplements, supports.
Optometry
Eye exams, contact lens fittings, frames, lens options.

Gather your images at the same time. Plans in your build are presented as cards rather than a table, so a good image does a lot of the work. Images must be .jpeg or .png files of up to 10 MB each, and video must be hosted on YouTube.
Adding a treatment
1. Open the Treatments page
Go to Treatment Plans in the left navigation menu, then the Treatments tab. The first time you arrive you will see a prompt to create your first treatment.
2. Start a new treatment
Select + Add Treatment. The Create Treatment window opens on the first of two steps.
Already created it elsewhere?
Treatments created in Adit are shared across the whole organization, so anything added at another location already appears in this list. Check before creating a duplicate.
3. Fill in the details
The name matters most here. It is what the patient reads on their plan, so write it the way you would say it to them.

rows: The name as the patient should see it, for example Clear Aligners or Annual Eye Exam. Up to 50 characters.
A code, if your practice uses one. Leave it blank if you do not.
A brief label, up to 50 characters. This is the line that appears beside the price on the plan.
A fuller explanation for the patient, up to 600 characters. This is the paragraph that sits under the treatment, and it can be customized on any individual plan.
The default fee. You can override it on any individual plan.

blocks.x: Select Next to move on.
4. Add images or video
This step is optional in principle and close to essential in practice, because your plans are presented visually.
SUPPORTED
Images
Drag files into the upload area, or browse to select them
Only .jpeg and .png files
Up to 10 MB each
Add as many as you need
YOUTUBE ONLY
Video
Paste a YouTube URL and select Add
A preview of the attached video appears
YouTube links only, no file uploads
One video per treatment

On the plan, images appear first and the video after them, beneath the treatment name and description. When a patient is choosing between frame options or aligner types, these are what they are looking at while they decide.
5. Create it
Select Create. The window closes with your treatment in the list, ready to add to a plan. Back returns you to the details if something needs changing first.
You only do this once
Treatments belong to the whole organization, not to a location. Create Clear Aligners once and it is there in every location you operate.
Finding your way around the list
The list shows each treatment's name, its code where you added one, how many images and videos are attached, the description, the price and the available actions.
By default it is sorted by what was updated most recently, and you can sort by treatment code instead. Use the search field to find a treatment by name or description.
Editing and deleting
Use the edit action to change the name, price, description or media at any time.
The delete action removes a treatment from the list. It stays on any treatment plan or template that already uses it, so a plan a patient is still looking at will not change underneath them.
Worth knowing
Anything you sell can be a treatment. Supplements, supports, frames, retainers and equipment all work the same way as a clinical service.
A plan can override anything. Price, description, coverage and discounts are all editable on an individual plan without touching the master treatment.
Set a price even where it varies. A default saves time on every plan, and you can still adjust per patient.
Write for the patient, not for your team. The description is read by someone deciding whether to go ahead.
FAQs
Can I pull my treatments in from my system automatically?
No. Treatment codes are migrated for dental practices only, because dental systems carry a standard master code list. In your specialty the list is built in Adit.
Do I have to create each treatment for every location?
No. Treatments are created once for the whole organization and are available everywhere.
Do I have to enter a treatment code?
No. The code is optional in your build. Use it if your practice works with codes, and leave it blank otherwise. The treatment name is the required field.
Can I upload a video file?
No. Video needs to be hosted on YouTube and added as a URL, one per treatment. A preview appears once you select Add.
Does the price include insurance?
No. The price is the full fee. Coverage and discounts are applied on the plan itself, where Adit calculates what the patient owes.
What happens to plans that already use a treatment I delete?
Nothing. The treatment stays on any plan or template that already uses it, so a plan a patient is still reviewing will not change underneath them.
