articles.title: Attach a Patient Form to a Treatment Plan

blocks.x: Many practices like to attach consent forms or informational handouts to a treatment plan for the patient to sign off on.

Note: In your Adit platform, you will need to add the consent form or handout to your Patient Forms module before you can attach it to a Treatment Plan. For help adding a form to your Patients Form module, see our article on how to Create a Patient Form.
To attach a patient form or consent form to a treatment plan:
Create the Treatment Plan. For more detailed instructions, see how to Create a Treatment Plan.
Scroll down to the Consent Forms section at the bottom of the plan builder.
Click the button to Attach Consent Form from Adit’s Patient Forms.
In the pop-up box, click the drop-down menu to see a list of your active forms from your Patient Forms module.
Check the box beside each form you would like to attach to this Treatment Plan. You can select up to 5 forms.
Click the Done button.
Finish building the Treatment Plan and send it to your patient.
Note: If you have already sent a Treatment Plan to a patient, you can edit the plan to attach forms up until the patient submits the Treatment Plan.

When the patient receives the Treatment Plan, they will not be able to complete or accept the plan until they complete all the attached Patient Forms. To complete a form, click on the Start or Complete button beside each attached form and follow the provided instructions. The page will redirect back to the Treatment Plan, where the patient can then click on the next form and repeat until they have completed all of the attached Patient Forms. Only when all attached Patient Forms are completed will the Submit button at the bottom of the Treatment Plan be available to click, which completes their Treatment Plan.
Note: Attached Patient Forms are not submitted to the practice until the patient submits the entire Treatment Plan.

articles.title: Attach a Treatment Plan to a Patient File in your EHR

blocks.x: When a Treatment Plan is imported into your EHR/PMS software, it attaches to the Patient File in the Treatment Plans folder. There are two ways to import a Treatment Plan into your EHR/PMS software - manual and automatic.
Manual Approval of Treatment Plans
To manually approve a Treatment Plan:
Navigate to the Treatment Plans dashboard.
Locate the desired Treatment Plan on the All or Submitted page.
Click the Approve button in the Import Status column.
Check the box beside which documents you would like to import.
Click the Approve button.
Automatic Approval of Treatment Plans

For practices who do not wish to manually review and approve each completed Treatment Plan, we offer the ability to automatically import the plan to your EHR/PMS software. If the Treatment Plan requires a practice/doctor’s signature, it will auto-import as soon as the practice signs the plan. If the Treatment Plan does not require a practice signature, it will auto-import as soon as the patient completes and submits the plan.
You can enable automatic approval by navigating to the Patient Forms module, then Preferences > Treatment Plans. Scroll down to the Plan Settings section and toggle the Auto-attach option to Yes.

articles.title: Complete and Approve a Treatment Plan

blocks.x: Treatment Plans are completed by the patient and approved by the practice.
Complete a Treatment Plan

The patient must click on the link they received in the email or text message to open their Treatment Plan. They can then click through the Treatment Plan to review the treatment options, select from the available payment options, accept the terms and conditions, and complete any attached Patient Forms.
Once they are satisfied with the Treatment Plan, the patient clicks the Submit button at the bottom of the page to complete the Treatment Plan.

The practice then receives a notification that the plan is complete and can access the completed plan on the Treatment Plans dashboard (it will appear on the All and Submitted pages). From here, you can countersign the Treatment Plan (if needed), view the payment plan or payment receipt in Adit Pay, and Approve (import) the Treatment Plan into your EHR/PMS software. You can also Download, Archive, or Cancel the Treatment Plan using the icons in the far right column.
Sign a Treatment Plan

When creating a Treatment Plan, one of the options you can include is a practice or doctor’s signature. If this is required on a Treatment Plan, the plan will show a status of Pending Sign once the patient submits the completed plan.
To sign a completed Treatment Plan:
Locate the Treatment Plan on the All or Submitted pages of the Treatment Plans dashboard. You can search by Treatment Plan Name or by Patient Name near the top-right corner of the page.
Click on the name of the Treatment Plan to open it.
Click the Sign button near the top of the page.
Fill out the signee information and click the Accept & Sign button at the bottom right.
Draw, Type, or Upload a signature image, then click the Accept & Sign button at the bottom right.
Approve a Treatment Plan

Once a Treatment Plan is completed and signed (if required), it needs to be Approved. You can set your preferences to automatically approve and import Treatment Plans, or you can approve each one manually. For more information on importing Treatment Plans to your EHR/PMS software, please see our article on how to Attach a Treatment Plan to a Patient File in your EHR.

Note: Once a Treatment Plan is completed by the patient, any associated Payment Plans can be found in the Adit Pay module. Each Treatment Plan will contain a link that will take you to the Payment Plan details in Adit Pay.

articles.title: Create a Treatment Plan

blocks.x: Adit's Treatment Plans allow practices to easily create and send a plan to a patient for signature, payment, and approval.
To create a Treatment Plan:
Navigate to the Patient Forms module.
In the top navigation menu, select Treatment Plans. If you don’t see this option in the menu, click the three dots to view the rest of the menu options.
Click the New Plan button near the top right corner of the page.

In the form that pops up, enter the Patient Name. The system will suggest matches based on the patients who have synced to Adit from your EHR/PMS software. You must select one of the suggested matches.
Enter a Treatment Plan Name that allows you to differentiate this plan from others for the same or different patients.
Click Start.

This will open the Treatment Plan builder. The left side of the page allows you to set up the specifics of this Treatment Plan. The right side of the page is a preview of what the plan will look like to the patient. Most of the information for the plan, such as Custom Settings, Payment Options, and the Consent statement, automatically populate based on the preferences you have set within the Patient Forms module. Other information, such as Procedures and Insurance Benefits, pull from the patient record in your EHR/PMS software.
Custom Settings

The Custom Settings section contains options that will add or remove elements from the current treatment plan. You can customize the default values for these settings under Preferences. For more information on these custom settings, please see our article on how to Customize Default Treatment Plan Options.
Options

Options allow you to present different treatment, coverage, and payment choices to the patient when needed. A treatment plan must include at least one Option; each Option must include at least one Procedure. To add another treatment option, click Add Option above the Procedures section.
You can also split Procedures into Phases. To add a Phase, click the Add Phase option on the right side of the Procedures box.

Note: You can drag and drop Procedures to reorder them within their Phase, or to move them to a different Phase in the same Option. Click on the dots to the left of the procedure and hold while you drag it to your desired position.
Procedures

To add a Procedure to the Treatment Plan, click the Add Procedure option on the right side of the Procedures box. Next, you’ll be provided with options for Planned Tx and Unplanned Tx. Check the box beside the procedures you would like to add to the current Treatment Plan Option, then click Add.

Planned Tx are treatments that have already been associated to this patient in your EHR/PMS treatment planner. Each treatment will show you the priority assigned to that procedure, the affected tooth number (if applicable), the treatment code, description, and associated fee from your EHR/PMS fee schedule.
Note: You can hide the tooth number and priority columns from the treatment plan using the Custom Settings at the top of the Treatment Plan page.

Unplanned Tx allows you to choose from all available treatments in your EHR/PMS software, including those that are not yet associated to this patient. This allows you to quickly add a treatment to the treatment plan without having to wait for data to sync from your EHR software to Adit.

Note: Unplanned treatments will not have a priority or tooth notation available. The fee provided for unplanned treatments will be the default based on the fee schedule for the patient’s insurance and may not reflect the actual amount you plan to charge this patient.
Unplanned treatments added to a Treatment Plan will not update the treatments associated with the patient in your EHR/PMS software.
Once a Procedure is added, you can edit any of the information about that treatment as it applies to this specific patient, including the priority, tooth, code, description, and fee.
Insurance Coverage

This section will automatically pull the patient’s insurance benefit information from your EHR/PMS software. Update the dollar amount to be applied to this treatment plan for each insurance (Primary Coverage and Secondary Coverage); this amount will be deducted from the Total Fee to calculate the Patient Pay amount in the preview on the right side of the page.
Apply Discount

If you wish to apply a discount to the total fee of this treatment plan, you can designate it in this section as a percentage or as a dollar amount. If you do not wish to apply a discount to the total fee, uncheck the Apply Discount box.
Note: The discount displays in green in the Total Fee section of the Treatment Plan with the word “Save” beside it.
Payment Options

In this section you will define the payment options available for this patient. You can choose to allow a one-time payment, allow a payment plan, or you can offer both for the patient to choose which they prefer. You can also choose which payment methods you will accept - Credit Card, Check, or Cash.

Note: Payment Plans and Credit Card payments are only available if you have Adit Pay set up on your Adit account and enabled in the Preferences for Treatment Plans. If you do not have Adit Pay, these options will be greyed out and unavailable for your practice.

Allow One-Time Payment - select this option to allow the patient to make a one-time payment. You can also specify an additional discount if they pay all at once, either as a percentage or as a dollar amount.

Allow Payment Plan - select this option to allow the patient to select a payment plan. You will define the terms of the plan, including the Frequency (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Yearly), any Upfront Payment Amount, and either the Number of Payments or the Recurring Payment amount.

Note: If you enter the Number of Payments, the Recurring Payment Amount will calculate automatically. If you enter the Recurring Payment amount, the Number of Payments will calculate automatically. Click the double-arrow icon between these two fields to switch which one auto-calculates.
Consent

The text box in this section allows you to provide the terms and conditions that will display on the Treatment Plan. The patient must check a box that says “I accept the following terms and conditions” before they can accept the plan.
Note: If you leave the text box blank, the checkbox to accept the terms will not display on the Treatment Plan. You can set a default value for this text block under Preferences.
Consent Forms

This section allows you to attach consent forms or other documents from your Adit Patient Forms module to the Treatment Plan. For more information on this feature, please see our article on how to Attach a Patient Form to a Treatment Plan.
Save, Discard, and Send

At any time during the creation of your Treatment Plan, you can click the Save button at the bottom of the plan builder to save your progress. This will allow you to return to this plan later without having to start over.

You can also discard the changes made to the current Treatment Plan since your last save by clicking the Discard button at the bottom of the plan builder. If you have not saved your Treatment Plan yet, the Discard button will delete the plan you have in progress and return you to the Treatment Plans page.
When you are ready to send the Treatment Plan to the patient, click the Save & Send button at the bottom of the plan builder.

articles.title: Customize Default Treatment Plan Options

blocks.x: Treatment Plans are highly customizable and can be configured in unique ways to suit your practice. We know that practices generally set their Treatment Plans up similarly every time, so we’ve provided a robust set of preferences where you can configure the default values for your Treatment Plans and only make minor adjustments when needed. This allows you to create and send Treatment Plans quickly and easily throughout the day.

To customize the default options for Treatment Plans, navigate to the Patient Forms module. In the top navigation menu, hover over Preferences and then select Treatment Plans. Select your location from the left navigation menu.
Treatment Plan Branding Options

In this section, you can upload a logo and a banner image and select a theme color that matches your practice’s branding. You can also edit the name of the practice/organization that will show on the treatment plan. These options customize the appearance of the Treatment Plan, but do not affect any functionality.
If you have multiple locations set in Adit, the Treatment Plan Display Name will default to the name given at the organization level.
Email Settings

The Treatment Coordinator Email allows you to specify which email address should receive the Treatment Plans as patients submit them. This is a required field; if you leave it blank, you will not be able to send Treatment Plan requests via email.

If a patient replies to the Treatment Plan Request email, the Reply-to Email lets you specify where that message should go. If left blank, your practice will not receive these messages, and patients will get frustrated with the lack of response from your office.
Plan Settings

Auto-attach allows you to skip the manual Approval step for each individual Treatment Plan. Once a patient submits their completed Treatment Plan and it is countersigned by your practice (if needed), the form will be automatically imported into your EHR/PMS software and attached to the patient file in the treatment plans folder.
Toggle Enable Adit Pay to Yes if you would like to allow patients to make credit card payments or Payment Plans for their Treatment Plan.
Treatment Plan Request Default Text

This section allows you to customize the default values for the Treatment Plan Request text message and email. For more information on how this information is used, please see our article on how to Send a Treatment Plan.
Treatment Plan Default Custom Settings
This section allows you to set the default values for your practice for all the Custom Settings available on Treatment Plans.
Treatment Plan Templates customizes if specific elements appear on the Treatment Plan.
Teeth Numbering System selects options between FDI or universal tooth numbering systems.
Show Benefits displays or removes the Your Benefits section at the top of the treatment plan.
Show Tooth Diagram displays or removes the tooth diagram at the top of the treatment plan.
Show Tooth Column displays or removes the “tooth” number in the Procedures section of the treatment plan.
Show Priority displays or removes the “priority” column in the Procedures section of the treatment plan.
Show Estimate Stamp displays or removes the “ESTIMATE ONLY” stamp effect from the Total Fee section of the treatment plan.
Show Insurance Payout displays or removes the Primary Insurance Coverage and Secondary Insurance Coverage lines from the Total Fee section of the treatment plan.
Require Patient Sign displays or removes the patient signature field from the bottom of the treatment plan.
Require Doctor Sign displays or removes the doctor signature field from the bottom of the treatment plan.
Apply Discount allows you to configure a default discount amount.

Payment Plan and Payment Method allow you to set up the default payment options you would like to have available on all Treatment Plans; these can be further edited on each specific plan in the plan builder.

Consent Message and Thank You Page Message allow you to fill in the text that you would like to display for your terms and conditions on the Treatment Plan and your thank you message after the patient submits their Treatment Plan.

articles.title: How to Import Treatment Plans

blocks.x: Using Adit, you can import existing treatment plans to present and send directly to patients for approval and payment if desired. You can also import additional treatment plans when providing multiple options for patients.
Importing A Treatment Plan
Importing while creating a new plan:
1. Navigate to TX Plans within the Patient Forms module and select New Plan.
2. Choose Use Existing Plan then search for the patient, add the treatment plan name, and select which treatment plan you'd like to import.
Importing into an existing plan (Providing Additional Options)
1. Select the existing plan under TX Plans within the Patient Forms module.
2. Select the Import Option button within the treatment plan
3. Select which treatment plan you'd like to add as a new option within the existing treatment plan.
The new option should appear next to the current options.

articles.title: Manage Existing Treatment Plans

blocks.x: There are several actions that you can take on an existing Treatment Plan, but they are limited based on the current status of the Treatment Plan. These actions can be found in the far right column of the Treatment Plans list.
Send - a right-facing arrow; available to plans in Draft status. Brings up a window where you can send the plan to the patient.
Remind - a circular arrow that looks like a clock; available to plans in Requested status. Brings up a window where you can send the plan to the patient again.
Cancel - a circle with an x in it; available to plans in any status but Accepted, Archived. Cancels the request; canceled requests are automatically deleted after 90 days.
Download - an arrow pointing down at a line; available to plans in Accepted or Pending Sign status. Downloads a PDF of the Treatment Plan.
Archive - an arrow pointing down inside a box; available to plans in Accepted status. Moves the plan from Submitted to Archived view so that it is out of your way.
Unarchive - an arrow pointing up inside a box; available to plans in Archived status. Un-archives the plan so it returns to its previous Accepted status.
Edit a Treatment Plan

You can edit a Treatment Plan up until the point that the patient submits the completed plan to the practice. To edit a Treatment Plan, click on the Treatment Plan Name. If the plan is in Draft or Requested status, it will open the plan builder so that you can make changes, then re-send the plan to the patient. If the plan is in any other status, the patient has already submitted it and it can no longer be edited. You will need to cancel the plan and create a new one.

articles.title: Send a Treatment Plan

blocks.x: There are two ways to send a Treatment Plan once it is ready: from the plan builder page, or from the Treatment Plans dashboard.
If you are building a Treatment Plan, there is a button at the very bottom of the plan builder to Save & Send.
From the Treatment Plans dashboard, you can send a plan from the All or Draft pages. Click the Send arrow icon in the far-right column.

When you click either of those options, a box pops up where you can specify how to send the Treatment Plan to the patient. You can Select a method, either directly to the patient via SMS (text message) via Email or both. Here you also have the option to Select Push to Device. Select which device to Push the form to and press Send. This will allow you to view the treatment plan and share with the patient on your office tablet using the Adit Patient Forms Application. If you choose to send the plan via SMS (text message), via Email, or both Check the box for the methods you would like to use, then use the Message Priority dropdown to determine which should take priority.
The remaining fields in this pop-up allow you to customize the contents of the text message or email that we will send to this patient.
When you’re ready, click the Send button at the bottom of the screen to send the Treatment Plan to the patient.

articles.title: Adit Pay

blocks.x: Adit Pay is Adit's integrated payments module for collecting patient payments online and in the office. Practices can send text-to-pay requests, charge cards on file, take card-present payments on the Wise BBPOS E terminal, accept Bank/ACH payments, and set up payment plans and subscription (membership) plans.

This module covers setup and business details, terminals (purchase, registration, order status and connection troubleshooting), requests, refunds, cancellations, receipts, automatic payment reminders, disputes, payouts, posting payments to the EHR ledger, convenience fees versus surcharges, and the Adit Pay FAQ.

articles.title: Guide to Adit Pay's Payment Plans

blocks.x: Navigating the Payment Plan Dashboard
In the top navigation bar, select Payment Plans
You will be redirected to the dashboard where you can see all of your current payment plans.
At the top of the dashboard, each tab represents a different plan status. Clicking on that tab will filter out and only show those plans within that status.
Understanding Plan Statuses
Draft - These are plans that are still in draft stage and have yet to be activated or sent out for a card.
Sent - These are plans that have been initiated and are waiting for the patient to add a card on file.
Active - These are plans that are active and have a card on file.
Payment Issue - These are active plans that have an unpaid payment request.
Inactive - These are plans that have been paused. No future charges will occur.
Completed -
These are plans that are completely paid off.
If it is a payment plan, that means there is no remaining balance.
If it is a subscription plan, that means the plan has expired and is paid off.
Archived
Inactive or completed plans that are now archived.
** Please note that active plans cannot be archived.
The columns used in the dashboard are:
Plan Name - clicking on this will open up the payment plan detail page
Patient - clicking on this will open up the patient card
Patient ID - this is pulled from the EHR
Plan Amount - this is the total amount of the payment plan
Frequency - this is how often the billing will run
Start Date - this is the date the payment plan starts
Next Payment Date - this is the next scheduled payment
# of Payments - this is how many installments
Recurring Payment - this is the amount that is charged each installment
Overdue Balance - this is the total amount of payment requests that did not receive a successful payment
Remaining Balance - this is how much is owed left on the payment plan
Status - these are the different status of the plan (refer to point 3A above)
Action Icons
Edit - this will redirect the user to either the payment plan detail page if the plan is active, or set up page if the plan is in draft stage
Archive - this will move the plan into archived status

articles.title: What Is ACH, and How Does It Work in Adit Pay?

blocks.x: Patients verify their bank account in seconds by securely logging in with their bank, the same way you might connect an account in a budgeting app.

When a patient pays by Bank/ACH in Adit Pay, whether for a payment plan, a subscription, or a one-time payment, their bank account has to be verified before it can be charged. Verification confirms the patient actually owns the account, and helps prevent failed payments and fraud.
This guide explains how that verification works today, and where Bank/ACH can be used.
What is ACH, and why does Adit offer it?

ACH (Automated Clearing House) is the electronic network US banks use to move money directly between bank accounts, the same system behind direct deposit paychecks and automatic bill payments. When a patient pays by ACH, the funds are withdrawn from their checking or savings account and processed through the ACH network. After the payment clears (typically within 1 to 4 business days), the funds are received by the payment processor. They are then transferred to the practice's bank account according to the practice's configured payout schedule, without using a card network like Visa or Mastercard.
Adit offers it as a payment option for three reasons:
Cheaper on larger balances
0.5% + $1.75, so the cost barely moves as the amount goes up
Built for recurring
The same rail that already runs direct deposit and autopay
No fee for the patient
A bank payment never carries a Convenience Fee, so the patient pays the exact balance
What it costs, and when it is worth using

The ACH cost of 0.5% + $1.75 is charged to the practice and is never shown to the patient. Because the fixed part is larger than a card's and the percentage is much smaller, ACH is the cheaper option on bigger balances and the more expensive one on small ones. The turning point is around $60 against an online or Text to Pay card payment, and around $90 against a card taken on the terminal.
This is why Bank/ACH matters most on treatment plans and large balances, and why it is worth offering even to patients who would otherwise reach for a card.
Where Bank/ACH is available
Bank/ACH has expanded beyond its original scope, so it is worth knowing both what it covers and where it does not reach.
AVAILABLE
Where patients can pay by bank
Payment plans and subscriptions, the original and most common use
One-time payments as well, through Quick Text, Collect Payment, and the Text-to-pay link
NOT AVAILABLE
Where it does not reach
Practices located in Canada, regardless of any other setting
Patients without online banking, or whose bank is not supported for verification. There is no manual fallback today
Recent Update

Manually entering a routing and account number is no longer available as a verification method. Secure bank login now covers more than 97% of US bank accounts, so this is the only way a patient adds a bank account today. If a patient's bank is not supported, they can pay by card instead.
How verification works
Three steps, completed in seconds:
1. Select your bank
The patient picks their bank from a list on the payment page
2. Log in securely
Through a bank-hosted window, powered by Stripe Financial Connections. Adit never sees the credentials
3. Verified instantly
The account is confirmed right away, and the payment can be submitted immediately

This method works with any bank supported by Stripe Financial Connections, which covers more than 97% of US bank accounts, and requires the patient to have online banking access with a supported bank. Verification is instant, but the payment itself still settles over the ACH network, typically within 1 to 4 business days.
No Fee at Setup

Adding and verifying a bank account is always free. The ACH transaction cost of 0.5% + $1.75 applies only when an actual payment is processed, never at setup, and it is charged to the practice rather than the patient.
If a patient's bank is not supported

Secure bank login covers more than 97% of US bank accounts, but if a patient's specific bank is not supported, or they would rather not link it this way, there is no manual fallback today. In that case, the patient can pay by card instead, and a Convenience Fee may apply depending on your Preferences settings.
FAQs
Which payments can be made via Bank/ACH?
Payment plans and subscriptions, plus one-time payments sent through Quick Text, Collect Payment, or a Text-to-pay link. Bank/ACH is available for US practices only.
Do convenience fees apply to bank payments?
No. Convenience fees never apply to Bank/ACH payments, regardless of the location's settings. The patient pays the exact balance, and the practice absorbs the ACH processing cost.

This is one of the ways a patient can avoid a Convenience Fee, alongside cash and check. A card payment carries the fee wherever it is taken, including on a terminal in the office. See How are convenience fees different from surcharges.
Is the patient's banking login shared with my practice or Adit?
No. The login happens inside a secure, bank-hosted window powered by Stripe Financial Connections. Neither your practice nor Adit ever sees the patient's banking credentials.
How many bank accounts can a patient save?
One bank account at a time. To add a different one, the patient (or practice) needs to remove the existing account first.
What if my patient's bank is not supported for verification?
There is no manual fallback today. The patient can pay by card instead, and a Convenience Fee may apply depending on your Preferences settings.
Is there a fee to add or verify a bank account?
No. Adding and verifying is always free. The 0.5% + $1.75 transaction cost only applies once an actual payment is processed, and it is charged to the practice.
Is Bank/ACH always cheaper than a card?

No. Because ACH has a larger fixed component, a card is cheaper on small balances. The turning point is around $60 against an online card payment and around $90 against a card taken on the terminal. Above that, ACH is cheaper and the gap widens quickly: a $1,000 balance costs $6.75 by bank against $29.30 by card online.
Is Bank/ACH available outside the US?
Not currently. Bank/ACH is available for US practices only; a Canadian location will never see the Bank option, regardless of settings.

articles.title: Adit Pay - Troubleshooting Terminal Connection Issues

blocks.x: Overview:

This article explains the standard troubleshooting steps to resolve terminal connection or payment issues on the Adit platform. These issues are commonly reported after a Chrome update or following an Adit app outage.
Common Symptoms:
Terminal is disconnected or unresponsive
Payment does not display on the terminal
Error appears during in-office payment processing
Step 1: Check Network Connection
Ensure that both the client’s computer and the payment terminal are connected to the same network. If they are not, reconnect both devices to the same network.
Step 2: Update Chrome Browser
Open Google Chrome.
Go to Settings → About Chrome.
Check if Chrome is up to date.
If an update is available, install it and realunch the browser.
Step 3: Enable Local Network Access
Open the Adit web app in Chrome.
Click the lock icon in the address bar.
Select Site Settings.
Locate “Local Network Access” (or “Live Network Access”) and set it to “Allow”.
Reload the page after enabling this option.
Note: Sometimes this option appears directly in the small pop-up after clicking the lock icon. You can enable it from there and reload immediately.
Step 4: Test Terminal Functionality
In the Adit app, click on Quick Text.
Enter the patient’s name.
Select “In-Office Payment” and click “Confirm”.
If the amount appears on the terminal, the connection is successful.
Step 5: Change DNS Settings (if issue persists)
In Chrome, go to Settings → Privacy and Security → Use Secure DNS.
Change the provider to Cloudflare (1.1.1.1).
Relaunch Chrome and test the payment again.
Important: Use only Cloudflare (1.1.1.1). Do not use Google or other DNS providers. If the DNS option is grayed out, do not make any changes and Please contact your Local IT Team/Person.
Step 6: Optional Technical Check (Adit Pay Support Only)
If the issue continues after performing all steps above:
Retrieve the terminal’s IP address from Stripe.
Ping the IP address using the Command Prompt on the client’s computer.
If the IP is not reachable, the client’s local IT should inspect the network configuration.
Summary: Most terminal issues are resolved by the following:
Both computer and terminal are on the same Wi-Fi network.
Chrome is updated and Local Network Access is allowed.
DNS is changed to Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) if Step 3 is Failed.
If the issue still persists after performing all steps, advise the client to contact your local IT to review network settings.

articles.title: Convenience Fees vs. Surcharges: What’s the Difference and Why This Isn’t a Surcharge

blocks.x: Pass Adit's processing fees through to patients on one-time card payments, applied uniformly across every card type, disclosed before the patient pays, and always avoidable by paying another way.

Adit Pay's Convenience Fees setting (labeled "Pass Through Adit Fees to Patient" in Preferences) lets your practice pass processing costs on to the patient automatically, without having to calculate anything by hand.

Because the words "convenience fee" and "surcharge" are often used interchangeably, this guide explains the difference, and why Adit Pay's implementation is a convenience fee, not a surcharge, under card network (Visa/Mastercard) rules.
How Adit Pay applies the fee
Four principles keep the fee compliant and patient-friendly:
All card types
Applies equally to credit, debit, Apple Pay & Google Pay
Fee-free alternatives
Cash, check, or Bank/ACH where the practice offers it
Disclosed up front
Shown as its own line item before the patient pays
Never on recurring
Payment plans & subscriptions are always excluded
Where the fee applies

When the setting is enabled, the fee is added to one-time card payments wherever the card is taken. That includes payments collected in the office on an Adit terminal, as well as online payments, Text to Pay, and payment requests. The rate depends on how the card is presented:
Card present
Card tapped, inserted, or swiped on an Adit terminal in your office.
Card not present
Online payment page, Text to Pay, payment request, or a card saved on file.
The fee is always shown on its own line and is never folded into the treatment amount. For example:

rows: Card on the terminal, in office
Card via Text to Pay or online
Card via Text to Pay or online

blocks.x: On card payments your practice receives the full service amount it billed, because the fee covers the processing cost. On Bank/ACH the patient is never charged a convenience fee and the practice pays the ACH processing cost instead.
What is never charged the fee: payment plans and subscriptions, CareCredit, HSA and FSA cards, Bank/ACH payments, and cash or check recorded as offline payments.
Best Practice · Recurring Payments
Convenience fees never apply to payment plans or subscriptions, per card network rules. Enable Bank/ACH payments so patients on recurring plans have a low-cost way to pay.
Surcharge vs. Convenience Fee

The two answer different questions. A surcharge penalizes the patient for choosing a credit card. A convenience fee recovers the cost of processing the payment, applies the same way to every card, and can be avoided entirely by paying another way.
SURCHARGE
A penalty on the card type
Applies only to credit cards; never legal on debit or prepaid cards
Requires registration with the card networks before use
Capped at the merchant's actual cost of acceptance
Prohibited or restricted in several states
CONVENIENCE FEE · ADIT PAY
A fee for processing the payment
Applies uniformly to every card, credit and debit alike, never to one card type
Set at Adit's own processing cost, not marked up
Patient always has a fee-free way to pay: cash, check, or Bank/ACH
Disclosed as a separate line item before payment
Fee Rates · What the Fee Covers

When enabled, Adit passes its processing fees through to the patient: 2.25% + $0.20 for card-present transactions and 2.9% + $0.30 for card-not-present transactions. Your practice receives the full service amount.
Why Adit Pay's fee is NOT a surcharge
It applies to both credit and debit cards equally. A surcharge legally cannot touch debit cards; Adit Pay's fee applies uniformly to every card payment: credit, debit, Apple Pay, and Google Pay.

Patients have a genuine way to avoid it. Cash and check are never charged the fee, and Bank/ACH carries no fee for the patient where the practice offers it. The fee reflects the cost of processing a card payment, not a penalty for choosing a card.
It's fully disclosed before payment. The patient sees the fee as its own line item on the payment page and receipt before completing payment.
It never applies to recurring payments. Per card network rules, convenience fees are for one-time payments only, so Adit Pay automatically excludes payment plans and subscriptions.
FAQs
Where are convenience fees not available?
Convenience fees are not available in Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, or Canada due to regulations and state rules.

Eligibility is determined by your practice location's address (the address on your connected Stripe account), not the patient's billing address. In multi-location organizations, each location is evaluated separately, so a Texas location may offer convenience fees while a Massachusetts location cannot.
Which payments do convenience fees apply to?
When toggled ON, the fee applies to all one-time card payments, card present or not present, including credit, debit, Apple Pay, and Google Pay.
It does not apply to recurring payments (payment plans and subscriptions), CareCredit, HSA/FSA cards, or ACH/bank payments.
Does the fee apply to payments taken in the office on a terminal?

Yes. If Convenience Fees are enabled, a card payment taken on an Adit terminal carries the fee at the card-present rate of 2.25% + $0.20. A $100.00 balance becomes $102.51 for the patient, and your practice still receives $100.00.
Paying in person does not by itself avoid the fee. What avoids it is the payment method: cash, check, or Bank/ACH.
Do convenience fees post to the patient's ledger?

No. Only the service amount posts to your EHR/ledger. The patient's ledger tracks outstanding payments and the actual medical services provided, so keeping convenience fees off the ledger keeps your billing records accurately matched to those services.
How do refunds work when a convenience fee was charged?
You may refund the entire amount the patient paid, including the convenience fee.
Only the refund amount up to the original payment request posts to the ledger. Example: for a $1,000 request with a $30.18 fee, refunding the full $1,030.18 posts $1,000 to the ledger.
What happens to payment requests sent before I turned convenience fees on (or after I turn them off)?
Requests that were already sent and are still unpaid remain fee-free. The fee setting is stored on each request when it's created, so patients never see an unexpected charge.
You can open an unpaid request and add the convenience fee to it, then re-send. If you later disable convenience fees globally, applied fees on open requests are removed.
Can I accept partial payments with convenience fees enabled?
No. Partial payments are automatically disabled while convenience fees are on, so the fee always corresponds to one complete transaction.
How can a patient avoid the fee?
By paying with something other than a card. Cash and check are never charged a convenience fee, and Bank/ACH payments (where enabled) carry no fee for the patient.
Card payments carry the fee wherever they are taken, including on a terminal in your office.
Related Articles
How Bank Account Verification Works in Adit Pay How To: Set Up Adit Pay Guide to Adit Pay Payment Plans & Subscriptions

articles.title: How to Create a Manual Payment in a Payment Plan

blocks.x: You can manually create a payment towards a patient’s payment plan.

Creating manual payments is only available for payment plans and not subscriptions

To create a manual payment:
Click on the plan name on the payment plan dashboard.

In the dropdown select Create Payment
In the pop up you will see the following:
Remaining Balance
This is the total plan amount minus what has already been paid
Outstanding Balance
This is the amount of payment that have failed and are now overdue
Amount to Charge
This is the amount that you want to manually create
Once you enter in the amount, select Next
Select Confirm
This will then manually create a payment with the patient’s card on file. The plan balance will automatically recalculate.
Please note that depending on the current situation of the payment plan, the flow will be slightly different.:
Example 1:
The total Plan amount is $5,000, with 10 installments
Recurring Monthly Amount is $500
Installment 1 - Paid $500
Installment 2 - Paid $500
Installment 3 - Paid $500
Now you want to create a manual payment of $2000
We will take $5000 minus the $1,500 previously paid minus the $2000 manual payment, which leaves $1,500 of a remaining balance.
There are still 7 remaining installments, so $1,500 divided by 7 equals $214.29 of a recurring payment.
New Recurring Monthly Amount = $214.29
Installment 1 - Paid $500
Installment 2 - Paid $500
Installment 3 - Paid $500
Installment 4 - $214.29 Scheduled
Example 2:
The total Plan amount is $5,000, with 10 installments
Recurring Monthly Amount is $500
Installment 1 - Paid $500
Installment 2 - Paid $500
Installment 3 - $500 UNPAID
Now you want to create a manual payment of $2,000.
There will be a pop up that shows up
This means that there is an existing overdue balance of $500. However, since you are creating a $2,000 charge to the patient, this will then void that open request.
Select Confirm
Now everything willl recalculate by taking the total plan amount $5,000 minus $1000 already paid minus the $2,000 manual payment.
The remaining balance of $2,000 divided by 7 remaining installments equals to $285.71 of a recurring payment.
Installment 1 - Paid $500
Installment 2 - Paid $500
Installment 3 - $500 VOID
Installment 4 - Paid $2,000
Installment 5 - $285.71 scheduled
Example 3:
The total Plan amount is $5,000, with 10 installments
Recurring Monthly Amount is $500
Installment 1 - Paid $500
Installment 2 - Paid $500
Installment 3 - $500 UNPAID
Now you want to create a manual payment of $100.
There will be a pop up that shows up
This means that there is an unpaid request of $500. Since you are trying to make a manual charge to the patient that is only $100, it is best to just collect that $100 under that existing request.
This will help keep the data clean and avoid having to void any requests or recalculating the payment plan/installments.
To collect a payment, go to the unpaid request and click on the blue Checkmark icon
To learn more about how to collect payments, click here.
Now the plan will show like this:
Installment 1 - Paid $500
Installment 2 - Paid $500
Installment 3 - $100 out of $500 Paid. ($400 still overdue)

Example 3:
Start Date is Sep 1
Recurring Monthly Amount is $500
On Sep 15, the start date is changed from Sep 1 to Sep 10
In this scenario, the first installment has already executed on Sep 1, and the next date that payment will run on is Oct 10.
This is because the plan is updated on Sep 15, which is after the Sep 10 date. So the payment would run on the next billing date instead.
Installment 1 - Sep 1 $500 Paid
Installment 2 - Oct 10 $500 Scheduled
Installment 3 - Nov 10 $500 Scheduled
Example 4:
Start Date is Sep 1
Recurring Monthly Amount is $500
On Sep 15, an attempt is made to change the start date from Sep 1 to Aug 15.
This would not be possible, because Aug 15 is before the initial start date of Sep 1 and is in the past.
If a subscription plan has any outstanding payment requests, even if you edit the subscription plan, these unpaid requests will be unaffected.

There are numerous ways in which you can add or update a payment card:
From the Practice Side:
You can manually update the card from the payment or subscription plan page

Email

CVV

Delete Card

If there are no cards on file yet:
The patient will have to enter in their card details
At the bottom of the page, they will have the option to select the checkbox Save This Card on File

articles.title: Manage Payment Disputes

blocks.x: A dispute (also known as a chargeback) occurs when the cardholder questions your payment. If a patient disputes a charge that you collected through Adit Pay, you will be notified via email notification, an internal notification in your Adit platform, and the dispute will be displayed in your Adit Pay dashboard. Once a dispute is created, the original payment amount, along with a separate $15 USD dispute fee is deducted from your account balance. At this point, you will have 7-21 days (depending on the card network) to respond to the dispute. You can choose to accept the dispute, which refunds the patient, or you can fight the dispute and supply evidence to the credit card company. If you do not make a decision or submit your evidence within that timeframe, the dispute is automatically accepted and your funds are permanently reversed.
To Submit Evidence for a Payment Dispute: Watch This Video Here
Navigate to the Adit Pay module.
In the top navigation menu, select Disputes. If you don’t see this option in the menu, click the three dotsto view the rest of the menu options.
Click on the patient’s name who has submitted the dispute.
Click Submit Evidence.
Enter the details of the services that you provided to the patient.
Upload any documents that will help support your case.
Type in any additional information you want to provide.
Click the Submit Evidence button.

Once submitted, the evidence is sent to the cardholder's bank and will take around 60-75 days to get resolved. As soon as the decision is made, we will update the status in your dashboard and send an email.
If the status is updated as Won: Your funds will be returned to your account along with the initial $15 dispute fee.
If the status is updated as Lost: Your funds and the $15 dispute fee will not be returned
If you would like to accept the dispute because the payment was charged in error, you can choose to do so.
To Accept a Payment Dispute:
Navigate to the Adit Pay module.
In the top navigation menu, select Disputes. If you don’t see this option in the menu, click the three dotsto view the rest of the menu options.
Click on the patient’s name who has submitted the dispute.
Click Accept Dispute.
Confirm your choice by clicking Accept.

What is Adit Pay?

Adit Pay is a payment processing solution that lets your practice manage payments within one platform. Send a quick link for patients to pay their balance online, or process credit cards in person with a terminal.

articles.title: Guide to Adit's Revenue Cycle Management (RCM)

blocks.x: Automated + professionally managed eligibility verification for Dental, Orthodontic, Optometry, and Chiropractic practices, built to cut claim denials before they happen.

Adit’s Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) - Insurance Verification solution enables healthcare practices to automate and standardize insurance eligibility checks. This helps reduce claim denials, protect revenue, and streamline front-office operations.

Unlike manual workflows or basic EDI-only tools, Adit’s RCM combines automated eligibility verification with optional manual verification, delivered through clearly defined tiers aligned to clinical complexity and cost transparency.

Designed as a cross-specialty solution for Dental, Orthodontic, Optometry, and Chiropractic practices, Adit’s Insurance Verification eliminates the operational burden of manual carrier calls while improving accuracy and consistency.

By integrating real-time automated verification with professionally managed manual verification, Adit delivers a scalable, enterprise-ready solution for practices of all sizes, from single-location clinics to large, multi-specialty DSOs.
What we confirm, in real time
Every check is tailored to your specialty’s unique needs:
Status
Is the patient’s insurance active?
Financials
Deductibles, co-pays, and out-of-pocket limits
Specialty Limits
Multi-phase (Ortho) or vision-specific (Optometry) coverage
Benefit Dates
Plan effective dates and renewal cycles
We support both Basic and Advanced eligibility checks and can retrieve procedure-level benefit details for enhanced accuracy.
Best Practice · 48-72 Hours
Verify eligibility 48-72 hours before every appointment. Insurance details can change at any time; early verification reduces claim denials and billing surprises.
Basic vs. Advanced Eligibility Verification
Verification moves through three stages of depth: each one adding a layer of review and detail.
STAGE 1
Basic
Automated check performed via EDI. Standard eligibility data with limited benefit breakdowns.
Up to 40 preset CDT codes
STAGE 2
Standard Advanced
EDI layer plus a second review by Adit’s RCM team, covering deductibles, co-pays, and plan rules.
Up to 20 CDT codes
STAGE 3
Extensive Advanced
The fullest review: co-insurance, out-of-pocket maximums, and coverage limitations, code by code.
Up to 40 CDT codes
NEW · IV26
Upgrade one appointment at a time. Stay on Basic and pay only for the appointments you choose to upgrade to Advanced. See “Adit’s New IV26 Module” in the FAQs below for details.
FAQs
What is RCM?
RCM stands for Revenue Cycle Management. At Adit, we currently focus on the Insurance Verification step of that cycle.
How do I sign up for Adit’s Insurance Verification service?
Adit’s Insurance Verification is part of our Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) offerings. To get started, please contact our Upgrades team, who will assist you with enrollment and next steps.
How do I set up Adit’s Insurance Verification module?
A member of our team will guide you through the setup process. During configuration, you will define:
The lead time before an appointment when insurance verification should trigger
Whether verification results should be attached to the patient’s record as a PDF, a note, or both
The treatment codes to be validated for Basic and Advanced verifications
Our team may contact your practice to request additional insurance information, if required.
For step-by-step instructions, refer to our article: How To: Set Up Insurance Verification.
What is the difference between Basic Eligibility Verification and Advanced Eligibility Verification?
Basic Eligibility Verification

Basic Verification is an automated eligibility check performed via EDI. It returns the standard eligibility information available through the payer’s EDI response, with limited benefit breakdowns or detailed code-level analysis.
Eligibility and benefits validation for up to 40 preset CDT codes
Advanced Eligibility Verification

Advanced Verification provides a comprehensive eligibility and benefits check. The first layer is performed via EDI, and a second layer of verification is completed by Adit’s RCM team. It includes detailed benefit information such as deductibles, out-of-pocket maximums, co-insurance, co-payments, coverage limitations, and plan-specific rules.
Advanced Verification is further categorized as:
Standard Advanced Verification: Eligibility and benefits validation for up to 20 CDT codes
Extensive Advanced Verification: Eligibility and benefits validation for up to 40 CDT codes
Adit’s New IV26 Module

Adit’s new Insurance Verification (IV26) module gives you the flexibility to upgrade individual appointments to Advanced. In an ideal scenario, you can be a subscriber to our Basic plan and get your appointments verified 72 hours before the appointment date, while upgrading one-off appointments to the paid Advanced tier for detailed verification. You just pay for that appointment.
When do I need to take action on an Insurance Verification?

Adit’s team will manage the majority of insurance verifications on your behalf. Action is required from your side only when a verification fails due to missing or incomplete insurance or demographic information.
In such cases, update the required details in the Adit App so the verification can be retriggered before the patient’s appointment.
If enabled, we can also send reminder notifications to your registered email address prompting you to update the missing information and reinitiate the verification in a timely manner.
How do I change which treatment codes are being verified?

To update the treatment codes used for insurance verification, please contact our support team by emailing support@adit.com. Your request will be automatically logged as a ticket in our ticketing system and routed to the appropriate team for review and action.

Since insurance verification is offered across multiple tiers, including Basic, Advanced (Standard), and Advanced (Extensive), the treatment codes selected may impact your verification tier and pricing.
For more information on how treatment codes align with each tier and how pricing may change based on your selections, refer to our Guide to Insurance Verification Charges.
Will you update the patient file in my PMS/EHR software?
Yes. The patient file can be updated in two ways:
By adding a note
By attaching a PDF
You may choose to enable either option, or both, through your preferences in the RCM module.
How do I check the status of an insurance verification?

You can easily monitor the status of all insurance verifications from a single, centralized view. When you navigate to the RCM module within the Adit platform, you will be directed automatically to the Verifications page.
Review the Verification Status column for color-coded status indicators, and refer to the Actions column for Verification Forms or the History of Verification.
For a detailed explanation of each verification status, refer to our article: How To: Check the Status of an Insurance Verification.
How am I billed for Insurance Verifications?
Read our Guide to Insurance Verification Charges to learn more!

articles.title: How to Set Up Auto Forwarding for OTP Emails in Outlook and Gmail
articles.module: Insurance Verification and Revenue Cycle Management

blocks.x: A one-time mailbox rule that routes portal verification codes directly to Adit’s RCM team.

Many insurance payer portals require two-factor authentication (2FA) at login. When Adit’s RCM team authenticates on your practice’s behalf to run eligibility verifications, the resulting one-time password (OTP) is delivered to the practice’s registered email address rather than to Adit directly. Without a way to relay that code, verification requests stall until someone at the practice retrieves and shares it manually.

Configuring an auto-forwarding rule removes that dependency. Once set up, any OTP email matching the criteria you define is copied automatically to rcmverify@adit.com, your own inbox continues to receive the original message unchanged, and Adit’s team can complete authentication without contacting your front desk. This is a one-time setup per mailbox; instructions for both Outlook and Gmail are provided below.
Before You Begin
You’ll need access to the email account currently used to log in to your insurance portals (the account 2FA codes are sent to).
Administrator rights may be required if the mailbox is managed centrally through Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace.
In Gmail, adding a forwarding address requires a one-time confirmation, approved from the account’s registered mobile device.
Outlook
Gmail
Setting Up Auto Forwarding in Outlook
Sign in to Outlook Web
Go to Outlook Web and sign in with your email credentials.
Access Outlook Rules
Click Settings () in the upper-right corner, then Mail > Rules.
Create a Forwarding Rule
Click on Add new rule.
Give your rule a name (e.g., “Forward OTP Emails”).

Under Add a condition, select Subject includes or From and enter the relevant keyword(s), such as “OTP” or the insurance portal’s sender address. A narrower condition reduces the chance of unrelated mail being forwarded.
Under Add an action, select Forward to and enter rcmverify@adit.com.
Click Save to activate the rule. Forwarding applies only to mail received after the rule is saved.
Test the Forwarding Rule

Log in to the insurance portal and confirm the OTP arrives at rcmverify@adit.com shortly after it reaches your own inbox. If it does not, review the rule’s condition and rule order in the Outlook Rules list, since a broader rule earlier in the list can sometimes intercept the message first.
Setting Up Auto Forwarding in Gmail
Sign in to Gmail
Go to Gmail and sign in with your email credentials.
Enable Email Forwarding
Click on the Settings () icon in the upper-right corner.
Click See all settings.
Navigate to the Forwarding and POP/IMAP tab.
Under Forwarding, click Add a forwarding address.
Enter rcmverify@adit.com and click Next. Gmail treats this as a security-sensitive change, so a confirmation step follows.

Note: Google sends a push notification to the mobile device associated with this account to confirm that the forwarding address was added intentionally. Approve the prompt on that device before continuing; the forwarding address cannot be activated until this confirmation is completed.
Open the verification email sent to rcmverify@adit.com and click the confirmation link.
Create a Gmail Filter for OTP Emails
Adding the forwarding address in Step 2 makes forwarding possible; a filter is what actually applies it to OTP emails specifically, rather than forwarding every message in the mailbox.
Return to Gmail settings and go to the Filters and Blocked Addresses tab.
Click Create a new filter.
In the From field, enter the email address of the insurance provider.
Alternatively, in the Subject field, enter keywords such as “OTP” or “verification code”.
Click Create filter.
Select Forward it to and choose rcmverify@adit.com from the dropdown menu.
Click Create filter to finalize the setup.
Test the Forwarding Rule
Log in to the insurance portal and confirm the OTP arrives at rcmverify@adit.com.
Security & Troubleshooting
Forwarding rules move a copy of sensitive authentication data outside your primary mailbox, so a few safeguards are worth keeping in mind once the setup above is complete.
Restrict the destination. Only rcmverify@adit.com should receive forwarded OTPs. Confirm the address before saving each rule or filter.
Some portals resist forwarding. Payers that detect forwarded mail or bind OTPs to the originating IP address may reject them; in that case, manual login by the practice remains the fallback.
Revisit rules after email changes. Password resets, mailbox migrations, or new IT policies can silently disable forwarding; periodic verification is recommended.
Fully reversible. The rule or filter can be edited or removed at any time from the same settings screen, with no impact on normal mail delivery.
Once configured, OTP delivery to Adit’s RCM team requires no further action from the practice. For assistance with setup or portal-specific issues, contact the Adit Support Team.

blocks.x: An 8-step walkthrough of the RCM setup wizard, from practice information to insurance mapping.

Setting up Adit’s Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) system is the first step toward streamlining and automating your front-office insurance workflows. Leveraging a high-speed EDI infrastructure, along with an optional manual verification fallback (available in Advanced packages), this setup ensures accurate and comprehensive eligibility verification across Dental, Optometry, and Orthodontic practices.
Getting Started
Navigate to the RCM Module
When you first access the RCM module within the Adit platform, you may see a welcome screen introducing the feature and prompting you to schedule a demo.

If this screen appears, it indicates that your account has not yet been upgraded to include the Insurance Verification feature. In this case, please connect with a member of the Adit team to enable access.
The welcome screen shown before the Insurance Verification feature is enabled.
Clicking Get Started will guide you through the setup steps outlined below.
Practice Information
The Practice Information form, including registered name, NPI, Tax ID, and address fields.
Once your account has been successfully upgraded, you will be prompted to complete the Practice Information section. This information is used to process insurance verification requests accurately.
Enter all required details under Enter in the information required for verification and ensure all mandatory fields (marked with *) are completed.
Please Note: Incorrect or missing information may cause verification requests to fail or return inaccurate eligibility results.
After completing the form, click Next to proceed. During the setup process, you can:
Click Back to return to the previous step
Click Cancel to exit the setup at any time
NPI Settings
In the NPI Settings section, select how you want to configure provider NPIs for verification:
Choose One NPI if you want to use a single default NPI for all verifications
Choose Multiple NPI to assign different NPIs based on the provider associated with each patient
Under Set up each Provider’s NPI, click Add Provider to enter provider details. In the Provider Information section, enter the following details exactly as configured in your EHR:
Provider name
NPI
Tax ID
Ensure that all provider details are accurate and match your EHR records.
Please Note: Incorrect or missing information may cause verification requests to fail or return inaccurate eligibility results.
Additionally, configure each provider’s network participation and fee schedule to ensure that benefits retrieved through automation or EDI reflect the correct in-network or out-of-network status.
After completing the setup, click Next to proceed or Back to return to the previous step.
Provider Information under NPI Settings, showing Provider, NPI, and Tax ID fields.
Verification Settings
Trigger Selection, Frequency of Verification, and EHR/PMS Settings including PPO and HMO templates.
Trigger Settings
Under Trigger Selection, choose how many days before the appointment Adit should verify patient benefits. Select your preferred option (e.g., 3 Days Before Appointment or 5 Days Before Appointment).
Verification Settings
Under Frequency Selection, choose how often patients should be verified between appointments. The default setting is 6 Months, but this can be adjusted based on your practice needs.
EHR / PMS Settings
Eligibility Verification PDF Settings
Choose Yes or No for attaching the Eligibility Verification PDF to the patient’s file
If Yes is selected, choose the folder from the dropdown where the PDF should be stored (File Name Format: Verified Date - Patient Name)
Patient Note Settings
Choose Yes or No to add a note to the patient’s file after verification
PPO Template
Provide the preferred format for notes under PPO Template. You can use available fields such as:
Insurance Carrier
Verification Date
Plan Maximum / Plan Remaining
Ortho Maximum / Ortho Remaining
Deductible Met (Ind)
HMO & Other Template
Define the format for notes under HMO & Other Template to ensure consistency in documentation.
Select Tx Codes
Basic and Advanced verification packages share a similar structure, with important functional differences. Each treatment code includes 1 to 4 verification questions, which may include:
Whether the treatment is covered and at what percentage
Age limitations for coverage
Frequency limitations
Patient eligibility and next eligible date, if applicable

Within the settings for Adit’s Insurance Verification feature, you can specify exactly which treatment codes should be included in either an Advanced Eligibility Verification or a Basic Eligibility Verification. The treatment codes you select will be checked every time a patient undergoes that type of verification.
Basic Package
Select up to 40 treatment codes
Verification responses are sourced entirely from EDI
No manual intervention is performed under this package
Advanced Package
Standard: up to 20 codes
Initial verification via EDI, followed by manual verification.
Extensive: up to 40 codes
Initial verification via EDI, followed by manual verification.
Selecting treatment codes to verify under the Basic package.
One-Off Upgrade (Basic → Advanced)
Clients on the Basic package can upgrade individual appointments to Advanced verification using the One-Off Upgrade option.
Standard and Extensive one-off upgrade options for individual appointments.
Upgrade options include:
Standard: Up to 20 codes
Extensive: Ability to select additional codes up to 40 codes
If no additional codes are selected, only the treatment codes defined in Preferences will be verified.
Selecting treatment codes to verify under the Advanced package.
Notification Settings
This setting determines how your practice is notified when a verification request fails.
Enabling email alerts ensures that your team is promptly informed of any failed verifications, allowing timely follow-up and preventing disruptions in patient workflows.

If email notifications are not enabled, failed verifications may go unnoticed. This can result in patients arriving with unverified insurance, leading to potential billing issues and front desk delays.
Configuring email alerts for failed verification requests.
Automation Credentials
In the Automation Credentials section, Adit requires access to your insurance portal login credentials to automatically retrieve eligibility information on your behalf.
Enter the required credentials for each insurance listed to enable automated verification.
Click Connect to securely add or authenticate credentials for a specific insurance
Once connected, the Status will display as Authenticated
Please Note: The credentials provided here are used only for system automation and should not be used for manual login purposes.
Providing accurate and up-to-date credentials ensures seamless and uninterrupted eligibility verification.
Connecting insurance portal credentials for automated verification.
Portal Credentials
In the Portal Credentials section, provide login credentials for insurances that do not support full automation.
These credentials enable Adit to perform manual verification or detailed eligibility audits when automated (EDI) verification is not available.
Enter the required portal Username and Password for each applicable insurance
Ensure credentials are accurate and kept up to date for successful verification
Providing valid portal credentials helps improve verification coverage and ensures more comprehensive benefit details when automation is not supported.
Entering portal username and password for insurances that require manual verification.
Insurance Mapping
Mapping insurance names from your EHR/PMS to Adit's standardized master list.

The final step in the setup process is Insurance Mapping. In this section, you will see a list of insurance names exactly as they appear in your EHR/PMS. Each insurance must be mapped to Adit’s standardized master insurance list using the available dropdown.
This mapping ensures consistent insurance identification and accurate processing across the RCM module.

Example: An insurance listed in your EHR as BCBSTX may correspond to Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas in Adit’s master list. Select the appropriate standardized option from the dropdown to complete the mapping.
Note: Accurate mapping is critical to ensure successful verification and correct eligibility results.
After completing all mappings, click Next to proceed.

articles.title: What is the difference between Basic Eligibility Verification and Advanced Eligibility Verification?
articles.module: Insurance Verification and Revenue Cycle Management

blocks.x: Adit can do two types of Insurance Verification for your practice: Advanced Eligibility Verification and Basic Eligibility Verification.
Advanced Eligibility Verification is the initial check required to verify coverage amounts for:
A patient’s first ever visit to your practice,
A patient’s first visit in a calendar year, or
A patient’s first visit after changing their insurance.
In an Advanced verification, Adit will ask more questions and get more detailed information about the patient’s eligibility, coverage, and limits.

After the initial Advanced verification is complete, that patient will not need to do another Advanced Elilgibility Verification for the rest of the calendar year, or until they change their insurance - whichever comes first. Each of that patient’s subsequent visits on the same insurance in the same calendar year will only need to undergo a Basic Eligibility Verification instead. Basic verifications are simplified and mainly check to see remaining benefits and coverage amounts.

Within the settings for Adit’s Insurance Verification feature, you can specify exactly which treatment codes should be included in either an Advanced Eligibility Verification, a Basic Eligibility Verification, or both. The treatment codes you select will be checked every time a patient undergoes that type of verification.

articles.title: When do I need to take action on an Insurance Verification?
articles.module: Insurance Verification and Revenue Cycle Management

blocks.x: Adit automatically triggers a verification before each appointment by creating a verification record based on the preferences that you set for your practice. Once the verification is triggered, Adit’s team takes over and handles the verification on your behalf, providing you with a detailed report when the verification is complete.

Your practice should check daily to see if there are any verification records that require your attention. These will generally be records with a status of Rejected, Failed, or On Hold, as these require additional information from you or from your patient in order for us to try again. You can also choose to manually verify any patients whose verifications are in Open, Rejected, or Failed status.
Rejected Verifications

Rejected verifications are ones where Adit was unable to pull enough information from your PMS to start the verification process for that patient. Usually this is because the patient has not yet provided their insurance information.

Adit can automatically send a Verification Request text or email to the patient asking them to provide this missing or incomplete information; you can customize this message in your preferences. If you prefer, you can also manually send the Verification Request text or email to the patient through the Quick Text menu.

Whether sent manually or automatically, the Verification Request message will include a form the patient can fill out and submit to provide the information we need to finish the verification. Once the patient submits the form, the verification status will update back to Open and Adit will attempt the verification again. You can also manually verify the patient yourself if desired.
On Hold Verifications

A verification is placed On Hold if Adit is unable to attempt the verification for a reason other than missing patient information. There are various reasons why a verification may be On Hold, and you can see the reasons noted in the Details column on the Verifications page.
You may need to take action in some of these situations, such as updating your provider portal login for a specific insurance company.
Failed Verifications
In the event that someone tries to complete a verification but cannot, the status will show Failed and a reason for the failure. A verification can fail for various reasons, including:
Expired or termed policy
Insurance company is unable to identify the patient
Insurance company is unable or unwilling to share patient info with a third party company like Adit.

If you see a verification with a status of Failed, you should take action by clicking on the Failed status and choosing to either manually verify the patient yourself or to create a new verification record which re-submits that verification to our team to try again.
If you choose to create a new verification record, you’ll need to provide updated patient and insurance information on the next screen before Adit can attempt to verify this patient again.

articles.title: Adit Voice, Phones and eFax

blocks.x: Adit Voice is Adit's VoIP phone system. Practices use supported Grandstream and Yealink desk and cordless phones, the softphone in the Adit app, or the Adit mobile app. The call flow (call tree) controls which phones ring and when, office hours, greetings, voicemail and hold music, and practices can keep multiple call flows or temporarily override them.

This module covers porting numbers and forwarding calls during the port, phone setup and connectivity, call pop settings, patient card pop-ups for incoming calls, blocking callers, whitelisting the practice number against spam labeling, voicemail and greetings, forwarding to an external number, emergency closures and internet outages, international calling, and eFax (getting a fax number, sending, viewing and notifications).

articles.title: Call Forwarding from previous provider to Adit

blocks.x: To ensure you continue receiving incoming calls while your phone numbers are being ported to Adit Voice, you can temporarily forward your existing office phone number(s) to the Adit temporary routing number provided by your Onboarding manager.

This guide includes step-by-step instructions for phone service providers to help you configure network-level call forwarding. Once enabled, your current provider will automatically redirect incoming calls to Adit, allowing your practice to continue receiving calls without interruption while the port is in progress.
Before You Begin
Obtain your Adit temporary routing number from your Adit onboarding manager.
Ensure you have administrator access to your current phone provider's portal (if applicable).
Configure call forwarding before your scheduled port date to avoid any disruption in service.
After enabling call forwarding, place a few test calls from an external number to confirm that calls are reaching your Adit system.

Note: Call forwarding remains active with your current provider until your phone numbers are successfully ported to Adit Voice. Once the port is complete, calls will route directly to Adit, and any temporary forwarding can be removed if it has not already been disabled automatically.
Weave
If you're using the Weave Desktop App, here's how to forward calls:
Open the Weave Desktop App and sign in.
Click on your profile picture/avatar, or the Settings (gear) icon.
Go to Phone or Call Settings (the exact wording may vary slightly depending on your version).
Look for Call Forwarding or Forward Calls.
Turn on call forwarding and Select the phone number you want incoming calls forwarded to, or add a new number by selecting + New Number at the bottom of the pop-up window.
Click Save or Apply.
Don't see the call forwarding option? This can happen if:
Your Weave user account doesn't have permission to set up call forwarding.
Your practice's calls are routed a different way, managed by an administrator.
The setting needs to be turned on from the Weave Admin Portal instead of the desktop app.

Note: These steps are for forwarding all your incoming calls. If you instead want to transfer a call you're currently on to someone else, that's a different process - just let us know and we can walk you through it.
Having trouble? Call Weave Support at 866-519-3684, then press 1, then 2 to speak with a real person.

Tip: Ask Weave support to send a message to their "L2 technician" about a call forwarding issue and inform we need forwarding set up on their backend for both open and closed hours, as a permanent setting.
Spectrum Business/Mobile
Option 1 - Using your office phone:
Pick up the handset and wait for the dial tone.
Dial *72
Wait for the dial tone again.
Dial the 10-digit phone number you were given (include the area code).
You'll hear a short "stutter" tone, then a normal dial tone - this means it worked.
Hang up.
Option 2 - Using the online account:
Sign in to your account online and click the Voice & Services tab.
Under Voice Access, click Manage Forwarding.
Choose your phone line, then click the arrow to see more options.
Turn on the switch for call forwarding, and make sure Prior to Ring is selected.
Click Manage Forwarding Lines, then add a name and the phone number you were given, and click Save.
Use the Forward all calls menu to pick your forwarding number.
Click Save.

You can set up call forwarding either through a web browser or the Xfinity app.

Go to the Xfinity Voice Call Forwarding Settings page and sign in with your Xfinity ID and password.
Option 2 - Using the Xfinity app:
Open the Xfinity app.
Tap the Services tab.
Under Home Phone, select View Xfinity Voice features.
Tap the Settings wheel icon (you may need to sign in again).
Tap Settings, then the menu drop-down.
Select Call Forwarding.

Once you're on the Call Forwarding screen, you'll see options for Basic, Advanced, and Selective Call Forwarding. For most offices, Basic Call Forwarding is what you'll need - this sends all incoming calls to one number.
To turn on Basic Call Forwarding:
Enter the 10-digit phone number you want calls forwarded to.
Click Update.
Need help? Call Comcast at (800) 266-2278 and their team can set it up with you.

Calls will now be forwarded to the specified number.

Place a test call to the AT&T number to confirm it forwards correctly.
Note: The exact feature codes can vary depending on whether the service is AT&T Wireless, AT&T Landline, or AT&T Office/Business service. If the codes above do not work, Call AT&T at 800-331-0500.
