articles.title: Missed Call Overview
articles.module: Call Intelligence, Call Tracking and AI Agent

blocks.x: The Missed Call page gives your practice full visibility into missed patient calls, follow-up activity, and scheduling opportunities. Use this page to identify callers who still need attention, measure callback effectiveness, and understand how missed-call follow-ups influence patient experience and scheduling outcomes.
Unique Missed Calls
What it means

This metric counts the number of unique phone numbers that attempted to call your practice but were not answered during the selected date range. Each phone number is counted once even if the caller tried multiple times.
Why it matters

Unique Missed Calls shows the true volume of different patients your practice missed - not just total call attempts. It helps you distinguish between repeat callers and the number of distinct individuals trying to reach the office.
How practices use it
Understand the scale of missed demand.
Identify staffing or routing issues causing missed callers.
Spot timing patterns (e.g., peaks at lunch or after-hours).
Example
If one patient calls 4 times and another patient calls once, Unique Missed Calls = 2, not 5.
Missed Calls Yet to Be Returned
What it means
These are unique missed callers who have not received any callback attempt from your practice and have not subsequently called again and been answered. In short - they have received no response.
Why it matters
This is the most time-sensitive KPI. It represents callers who are at the highest risk of going to a competitor because they never heard back from the practice.
How practices use it
Prioritize real-time callbacks to reduce lost opportunities.
Assign ownership for monitoring missed calls during business hours.
Identify breakdowns in front-desk workflows or staffing gaps.
Example
A patient calls at 9:00 AM and nobody attempts a callback - the entry remains in this KPI until a callback is made.
Missed Calls Yet to Be Connected
What it means
These are unique missed callers where the practice attempted a callback, but no successful two-way conversation occurred (e.g., the call went to voicemail, patient didn't pick up, invalid number).
Why it matters
This KPI measures follow-up effectiveness, not just activity. A high value can indicate poor timing, insufficient follow-up attempts, screening of unknown numbers, or outdated contact information.
How practices use it
Schedule additional callback attempts (second/third tries).
Adjust calling windows (early morning, lunch, evening) based on connection success.
Try alternate numbers listed on the patient record.
Improve scripts and caller ID handling to reduce screening.
Example
Staff calls twice and reaches voicemail both times - Returned? = Yes, Connected? = No. The entry remains in this KPI until a live conversation occurs.
Scheduling Opportunities Generated
What it means

The number of missed callers who, after being contacted, engaged in a scheduling conversation - even if an appointment was not finalized at that time. This captures interest and intent that could convert into bookings.
Why it matters
Scheduling Opportunities indicate early-funnel demand that would have been lost without the callback. They show how effectively callbacks are creating possible appointments.
How practices use it
Measure how returned calls translate into potential appointments.
Refine callback scripts to better capture booking interest.
Forecast future scheduling needs and production.
Example
A patient asks about available times for a cleaning and says they will check their calendar - this is counted as a Scheduling Opportunity.
Appointments Booked
What it means
The number of confirmed appointments that were scheduled as a direct result of returning missed calls. This is the final conversion metric in the missed-call funnel.
Why it matters
Appointments Booked reflects the real business impact of your callback process - how many missed callers were converted into scheduled patients and potential production.
How practices use it
Track conversion rate from missed calls to booked appointments.
Coach staff on effective booking and confirmation techniques.
Assess how missed-call recovery contributes to monthly production.
Example
A missed caller is contacted and books a crown consultation - Appointments Booked increases by 1.
Missed Call Table (Column Descriptions)
The Missed Call table lists unique missed callers with related metadata. Admins can customize visible columns. Below are the column descriptions presented in user-friendly language.
Caller: Phone number or identified patient associated with the missed call.
Time: Timestamp when the missed call occurred.
Location: Practice location that received the call.
Source: Marketing or tracking source tied to the phone number.
Duration: Ring length before the call was missed.
# Missed Calls: Number of missed calls from this number in the selected range.
Returned?: Yes/No - whether the practice attempted a callback or the patient later called back and was answered.
Returned Time: Timestamp of the most recent callback (if Returned? = Yes).
Previous Returned Time: Timestamp of the prior callback attempt.
# Attempts: Count of outbound callback attempts made to this number.
Connected?: Yes / No / N/A - whether a successful two-way conversation took place after callbacks.
Connected Time: Timestamp when the call was successfully connected (if Connected? = Yes).
Previous Connected Time: Prior successful connection timestamp.
User: Staff member who handled the callback or connected call.
Call Type: System-detected category (e.g., Scheduling, Clinical Question, Billing).
Call Outcome: Result from the analysis (appointment booked, information provided, voicemail, etc.).
Sentiment: Caller sentiment detected during the returned/connected call (Positive/Neutral/Negative).
Reason for Visit: Patient's stated reason for the appointment.
Reason for Not Booking: If no appointment was made, the reason (price, schedule conflict, insurance, etc.).
Revenue Potential: Estimated value band based on Reason for Visit ($, $$, $$$).
Best Practices for Managing Missed Calls
High-level guidance: Combine timely callbacks, prioritized triage, and regular review of analytics to convert more missed callers into appointments.
Return missed calls quickly
Aim to return missed calls within 15-30 minutes where possible. Timely callbacks significantly increase the chance of reaching the patient and converting them into a booking.
Prioritize by Revenue Potential
Use Revenue Potential and Reason for Visit to triage callbacks. High-value callers (e.g., implants, cosmetic treatments, multi-visit plans) should be returned first to maximize production.
Try all patient numbers
If the mobile number doesn't connect, call alternate numbers listed on the patient card (home, work). Trying additional numbers increases the chance of a connection and speeds recovery.
Monitor Returned? and Connected? daily
These columns provide the clearest view of follow-up quality: Returned? = No needs a callback; Returned? = Yes but Connected? = No often needs more attempts or different timing.
Review “Missed Calls Yet to Be Connected” each morning
A persistent high number here signals ineffective callbacks. Adjust staff calling windows, assign follow-up ownership, or explore alternative contact methods (SMS scheduling links, email reminders).
Coach using call analysis fields
Use patterns in Call Type, Call Outcome, Reason for Not Booking, and Sentiment to identify training needs (handling objections, improving scripts, refining pricing conversations).
Track Scheduling Opportunities → Appointments Booked

Monitor the ratio between Scheduling Opportunities and Appointments Booked. A large drop-off indicates a conversion problem - review scheduling flexibility, confirmation processes, and staff booking techniques.
Set clear SLAs and ownership
Define who owns missed-call recovery during shifts and set an SLA (e.g., return all missed calls within 30 minutes during business hours). Track SLA compliance in regular huddles.
Notes & Tips
Voicemail handling: If callbacks reach voicemail, count them as Returned but not Connected. A live conversation is required to mark Connected.
Final status: Once a missed-call entry is successfully Connected, that record represents a completed opportunity and typically remains unchanged.
Tip: Combine weekly reports of missed-call metrics with front-desk scorecards to close the loop on performance.

articles.title: AI Intelligence: Call Handling Summary

blocks.x: The Call Handling section provides AI-powered insights into the quality of patient interactions across your practice. It evaluates call performance using sentiment analysis and scorecard criteria, helping you understand how effectively your team communicates, resolves issues, and delivers a positive patient experience.
This module highlights overall experience trends, individual staff performance, and call-type strengths and weaknesses to support coaching, training, and operational improvement.
Scored Calls
What it means
Total number of calls that have been analyzed and scored by the AI during the selected date range.

Why it matters
This is the sample size underpinning all coaching and quality metrics - larger counts produce more reliable insights.
How practices use it
Ensure enough calls are scored to make reliable conclusions.
Track scoring volume changes after policy, staffing, or routing changes.
Validate coverage for coaching targets (e.g., minimum X scored calls per user/week).

Example
If Scored Calls = 312 this month, the AI scored 312 conversations that feed the coaching and sentiment metrics.
Customer Sentiment
What it means
An aggregated sentiment score derived from call analysis that represents the overall emotional tone (Happy / Neutral / Unhappy) across scored calls.

Why it matters
Sentiment is a quick indicator of patient experience and how calls make customers feel - a drop often precedes churn or increased complaints.
How practices use it
Spot deteriorations in patient experience earlier than complaints or reviews.
Correlate sentiment shifts with staffing, policy, or campaign changes.
Prioritize coaching where sentiment is low.

Example
If Customer Sentiment = 61 (aggregated), this indicates a moderate positive skew but worth investigating if trending down.
Overall Call Score
What it means
The average of all call-quality scores (based on the practice's scorecards) for the selected date range.

Why it matters
Gives a single-number view of call-handling quality across the practice and is useful for tracking improvements from coaching.
How practices use it
Set quality targets (e.g., aim for an average ≥ 75).
Measure the effect of training or script changes.
Compare across locations, teams, or shifts.

Example
If Overall Call Score = 68, that is the mean score of all scored conversations - use it to set coaching priorities.
Unhappy Customers
What it means
The percentage of scored calls where sentiment is negative (unhappy) out of total scored calls in the selected range.

Why it matters
High unhappy percentages indicate patient friction or poor call experiences that can reduce bookings and retention.
How practices use it
Drill into calls with negative sentiment to identify recurring problems.
Provide targeted coaching when a user has a high unhappy rate.
Use it as a KPI to reduce complaint drivers.

Example
If Unhappy Customers = 57%, then 57% of scored calls were categorized as unhappy - investigate causes (wait times, tone, process).
Happy Customers
What it means
The percentage of scored calls where sentiment is positive (happy) out of total scored calls for the selected range.

Why it matters
Measures the share of interactions leaving patients satisfied - a direct indicator of front-desk quality and service experience.
How practices use it
Reinforce behaviors tied to high happy rates in coaching.
Reward staff or teams with consistently high happy percentages.
Track how changes (scripts, staffing) affect satisfaction.

Example
If Happy Customers = 33%, then one-third of scored calls were positive - aim to increase this with coaching.
Customer Sentiment Breakdown
What it means
A chart showing counts (or percentages) of Happy / Neutral / Unhappy calls - a visual decomposition of overall sentiment.

Why it matters
Breakdowns reveal the distribution behind the aggregate sentiment metric, showing whether neutral or strongly negative calls are driving issues.
How practices use it
Prioritize root-cause analysis for large unhappy segments.
Monitor whether neutral calls improve to happy after coaching.
Compare sentiment mix across users or call types.

Example
If the breakdown is 25 Happy / 12 Neutral / 19 Unhappy, focus on reducing the 19 unhappy calls and nudging neutral calls to happy.
Scored Calls by Type
What it means
A chart showing number of scored calls grouped by call type (Scheduling, Billing, Clinical, Insurance, Recare, etc.).

Why it matters
Different call types require different skills; volume by type helps prioritize training for high-volume or low-scoring categories.
How practices use it
Identify which call types produce the most scored calls.
Tailor coaching content to the largest or weakest categories.
Allocate specialists for complex call types (billing/clinical).

Example
If Scheduling and Clinical dominate scored calls, focus coaching resources on those topics first.
Avg Scores by Call Type
What it means
Average call score for each call type - shows which categories have higher or lower quality on average.

Why it matters
Helps identify which call types need the most coaching and which represent strengths.
How practices use it
Run targeted training where avg scores are low (e.g., Billing = 29).
Replicate best practices from high-scoring call types.
Prioritize operational fixes for low-scoring categories.

Example
If Scheduling avg = 89 and Billing avg = 29, launch billing-specific training to raise quality.
Call Score Trend
What it means
A time-series chart showing average call score over the selected period (daily/weekly), highlighting rises or drops in quality.

Why it matters
Trend analysis exposes patterns and timing of quality changes - ideal for measuring impact of interventions.
How practices use it
Spot sudden drops tied to events (staff changes, system issues).
Validate if coaching improved scores over time.
Schedule refresher training when trend weakens.

Example
If the trend dips on Nov 19, check that day’s staffing or call routing to find the cause.
Scored Calls by User
What it means
A chart showing how many scored calls each user handled in the selected time range.

Why it matters
Shows sample sizes per user - necessary context when comparing user-level scores and win/loss metrics.
How practices use it
Ensure statistically meaningful comparisons (avoid judging users with very few scored calls).
Balance scoring assignments so each user has adequate coverage.
Reward users with sustained scoring volume and quality.

Example
If Holly has 93 scored calls and Danny has 12, treat Holly’s metrics as more robust and give Danny more scoring exposure.
Unhappy Customers by User
What it means
A per-user breakdown of unhappy-customer percentages (or counts) relative to their total scored calls.

Why it matters
Identifies which staff members generate the most negative experiences so coaching and remediation can be targeted.
How practices use it
Prioritize one-to-one coaching for users with high unhappy rates.
Compare unhappy rates to avg scores to see alignment.
Use call examples to demonstrate corrective behaviors.

Example
If User A has 59% unhappy calls and User B has 8%, focus coaching on User A’s interactions.
Overall Call Score by User
What it means
Average call score for each user - reflects individual performance against the practice scorecard.

Why it matters
Provides a way to compare user quality and identify who needs training or mentorship.
How practices use it
Create targeted coaching plans per user based on their average score.
Recognize high performers and extract best practices.
Monitor progress by tracking this metric over time after coaching.

Example
If Dr. Grant averages 89 and Dr. Denton averages 20, use Dr. Grant as a model and craft a development plan for Dr. Denton.

articles.title: How to Manage Task Assignment Logic
articles.module: Call Intelligence, Call Tracking and AI Agent

blocks.x: Adit Call Intelligence automatically creates follow-up tasks when a call requires manual action (scheduling, insurance checks, confirmations, billing follow-ups, etc.). The Task Assignment Logic setting determines who receives those tasks, so follow-ups are completed on time.
Where to find this setting
Call Intelligence → Preferences → Task Assignment Logic
Assignment Options - What each option does
1. Assign based on Call User
The task is assigned to the user who handled the call. If the call was answered by a user who has not created a Voice Print, the task may remain unassigned.
2. Round Robin - assign all Call Tasks
Tasks are distributed evenly across a selected pool of users in rotation. Use this when you want a balanced workload across multiple team members.
3. Direct Assign - all Call Tasks to one user
All system-created call tasks are sent to a single designated user (for example, an office manager or central coordinator).
4. Do Not Assign Call Tasks to Anyone
Tasks are created by the system but remain unassigned. The practice will need to assign or pick up tasks manually.
How to configure Task Assignment Logic
Navigate to Call Intelligence → Preferences → Task Assignment Logic.
Choose one of the four assignment options (Call User, Round Robin, Direct Assign, Do Not Assign).
If selecting Round Robin, choose the users to include in the rotation.
If selecting Direct Assign, choose the single user who will receive all tasks.
Click Save (if applicable) to confirm your selection.
Notes & common behaviors
Voice Print dependency: If "Assign based on Call User" is selected but a call is answered by someone without a Voice Print, tasks may remain unassigned.
Round Robin pool: Ensure the selected users are active and expected to handle returned tasks.
Manual reassignment: Tasks can always be reassigned manually from the Call Tasks module if needed.

articles.title: Set up Dynamic Number Placement on your website
articles.module: Call Intelligence, Call Tracking and AI Agent

blocks.x: What is Dynamic Number Placement?

Dynamic Number Placement is a call tracking feature that assigns a unique phone number to each online source and then displays that phone number to visitors who arrive at your website via that specific source.

These sources include organic search, PPC ads, Yelp, or anywhere else your business has a presence online. The data will then feed to your Google Analytics account for you to review once your phone starts ringing. This allows you to pinpoint the exact source of incoming calls.
Why is this tool valuable?

To put it simply, it’s the core of call tracking. In order to accurately track phone calls, you need to install dynamic number placement. Secondly, dynamic number placement allows you to understand who your customer is. If you know where your customer hangs out online - or, more importantly, which sources drive the most phone calls - you can focus your time and ad spend on optimizing channels that drive conversions. Think about it: By knowing where all your calls are coming from, you can better optimize pretty much every aspect of your business - your marketing strategy, advertising campaigns, and even your products and services.

If you’re not tracking your phone calls, then you’re not getting an accurate representation of how leads become patients. After all, you’re probably tracking your online traffic - but what about all those leads that get lost when someone takes an offline action like picking up the phone?
How Does Dynamic Number Placement Work?

Installing Adit’s dynamic number placement on your website is as simple as installing a line of JavaScript code. This code will detect your user’s source and place a cookie on their browser that tells your website to display a specific phone number. This also allows the same number to always appear for that particular user, even if they leave your website and come back later.
To set this up please follow these steps:
Go to Settings
Click on Dynamic Number Placement
Select the location you want to set up

Adit will provide a Code Snippet. You can choose to give this code to your webmaster. Insert this code snippet immediately before the tag on every page of your website. It must be included on every landing page, and every page containing a phone number. You can install this script on both HTTP and HTTPS pages.
Please note, if you have one website for than one location, you will need to install each code for each location.
Once you have installed Dynamic Number Placement on your website, you will need to start setting up your Tracking Numbers. You can do that by reading the following articles:
How to purchase a tracking number
How to set up a tracking number

Step 4 - Set Up Dynamic Number Placement (Call Swapping)
What Is Dynamic Number Placement?
Dynamic Number Placement (DNP), also called Call Swapping, automatically changes the phone number displayed on your website based on a visitor’s traffic source.
Example:
A visitor from Google Ads → sees the “Google Ads” number
A visitor from Facebook Ads → sees the “Facebook” number
A visitor from Organic Search → sees the “Organic” number
This allows accurate tracking of which marketing channels generate the most calls, visible in Adit App Reports.
How It Works

Adit’s DNP uses a small JavaScript snippet on your website. It automatically shows different phone numbers based on how visitors arrived, helping you understand which channels generate the most valuable leads.

Confirm that each source in Adit has the correct tracking number assigned.

articles.title: How to setup a Voice Print
articles.module: Call Intelligence, Call Tracking and AI Agent

blocks.x: What Is a Voice Print?
A Voice Print is a secure voice sample of a staff member that allows Adit Call Intelligence to recognize who spoke during a phone call.
Every person’s voice is unique. Voice Print captures key vocal characteristics so Adit can confidently distinguish staff voices from patient voices, even when names are not spoken during the call.
Once a Voice Print is created, Adit uses it to:
Tag calls to the correct team member
Improve reporting accuracy
Assign follow-up tasks to the right user
Power coaching, analytics, and performance insights
Why Is Voice Print Needed?
Voice Print improves the accuracy of:
Speaker identification (staff vs patient)
Call analytics and performance reporting
Task assignment based on who handled the call

Note:
Call Intelligence continues to work even without Voice Print.
However, Voice Print adds an extra layer of reliability, especially in calls where staff names are not clearly mentioned.
How Does Voice Print Work?
Voice Print follows a simple three-stage process:

One-Time Setup
Each staff member records a short voice sample.

Background Learning
The AI learns the voice over time while calls continue to work normally.
(There is no loss in functionality or accuracy during this phase.)

Fully Active
Once training is complete, Voice Print automatically helps identify speakers on all future calls.
Voice Print Statuses
You may see one of the following statuses under Preferences → Voice Print:

Failed
Voice Print was not submitted, or the upload did not meet minimum requirements.

Processing
Voice Print was submitted successfully and the AI is learning the voice.

Success
Voice Print is fully trained and actively being used for speaker identification.
While Voice Print is in Processing, speaker identification continues to work using call transcripts.
Set Up Your Voice Print - Web / Desktop
Prerequisites
Computer with a working microphone
Browser access (allow microphone permissions)
Access to Call Intelligence
Steps
Go to Call Intelligence → Preferences → Voice Print
Select Use Microphone in your Computer
When prompted by Chrome, click Allow this time
Click Record Me and read the passage shown on screen
Click Stop Recording
Use Play to review the recording
Click Save to upload the Voice Print
If needed, click Discard to re-record.
Verify or Update Your Voice Print
Go to Preferences → Voice Print
Check the status - Success, Processing, or Failed
If the status is Failed, re-record using the steps above
Even if status is Success, you may re-record if needed
Set Up Your Voice Print - Mobile App
This method is recommended if:
Your computer does not have a microphone, or
You want staff to record using a mobile device
Steps
Open the Adit Mobile App
Go to Settings → Voice Print
Tap the + icon (top-right)
Select the user and tap Done
Hand the phone to the user
Tap the microphone icon to start recording
Read the displayed passage clearly
Tap Stop, then Save
Optionally tap Play to review the recording.
Create Voice Prints Without Call Intelligence Access
Yes - this is possible using the Mobile App.
A user who has access to the mobile app can:
Log in on their phone
Hand the device to other staff members
Record Voice Prints on their behalf
This allows practices to create Voice Prints for users without granting them access to Call Intelligence, while still enabling accurate speaker identification.
Common Issues & Troubleshooting
Unable to record using microphone
The system may not have a microphone, or
Browser permission was not granted
Check Browser microphone settings and select Allow.
Voice Print shows “Failed” after upload
Recording may not meet minimum length or clarity requirements
Re-record and submit again
If failures occur across multiple users or practices, this may indicate a backend issue and should be escalated.
Where to Find This Feature

Navigation Path:
Call Intelligence → Preferences → Voice Print

Flow A is a simple, straightforward text with a short message and a link to leave a review.

Flow B has a more personalized feel and includes a series of text messages that the patient has to interact with in order to complete the review process. The first message asks them to rate your practice from 1-5. Depending on what number the patient replies with, they will receive another message asking them to leave a review or an opportunity to give you direct feedback without a review.

While Flow B is more personal, it does require the patient to actively participate in multiple steps, so it is less likely to get them to actually leave you a review in a useful place, such as your Google Business page.
You can change between flow A and B at any time.
To change your Pozative request flow:
Navigate to the Pozative module.
In the left navigation menu, select Preferences.
Navigate to the Review Request Flow
You can play the preview of each version to see what the patient experiences in each flow.
Change the toggle to your desired Flow (A or B).
Your changes will save automatically.

articles.title: Attempt a Follow Up

blocks.x: We call every try to handle a Follow Up task an Attempt. Each Attempt is recorded with its result (successful or not) so that there is a clear record of your team’s efforts to complete a particular task, such as collecting a payment or scheduling an appointment.
To attempt a follow up:
1. Locate the Follow Up task in the Follow Ups dashboard or the Patient Card.

2. Click the appropriate icon to call, text, or email the patient.
The Phoneicon will call the patient directly through Adit Voice, if you have it enabled.
The Text message icon will open an Engage quick-text box, if you have Engage enabled.
The Emailicon will open your device’s email program so you can email the patient.
3. Communicate with the patient as normal.
4. Click the checkmarkicon to log your attempt and its result.

5. Select the result of your attempt:
Contacted (andcompleted) - you spoke with the patient or their guardian and were able to complete the desired task.
Contacted (and not completed) - you spoke with the patient or their guardian but were not able to complete the desired task.
Did Not Reach Decision Maker - you did not speak with the patient or their guardian.
The wording for each of the results will vary slightly based on the nature of a task - for example, scheduling an appointment vs. collecting a payment.
6. If you selected the completed option, click the Save button. You’re all done with this task!
7. If you selected the not completed or Did Not Reach Decision maker options, click the Next button.

8. Update the fields for your next attempt at contacting this patient - you can Assign to another member of your team, Choose a follow up date for the task to be due, and Leave a note with any relevant information, such as who you spoke with or what message you left.
9. Click the Reschedule button.

10. If you do not wish to continue following up on this task, click Don’t Reschedule My Follow Up at the bottom of the window. The Follow Up task is marked as completed with a note that specifies that it was intentionally not rescheduled.

articles.title: Growth Report

blocks.x: The growth report allows you to track your patient loss or gain over time.
Go to Practice Analytics > Reports > Growth. Choose the timeframe you would like to view in the top right.
By tracking New patients, Recaptured patients, and Lost patients we can show your Net Growth number in any timeframe you choose.
The calculation is New Patients + Recaptured Patients - Lost Patients = Net Growth.
Instead of only tracking new patients added to your practice, with the growth report you can get the full scope of your practice growth.
New Patients are any patients completing their first appointment in your EHR.
Recaptured Patients are any patients who were considered Lost and then were added back for an appointment.
Lost Patients are divided into two categories in Adit.

1. Lost (inactivity) - Patients who have not completed an appointment within 18 months. (this is an adjustable timeframe within Practice Analytics > Preferences. There you can change the timeframe either to 12 months or 24 months if you prefer)
2. Lost (status change) - Patients who have been marked as inactive in your EHR.
A few things to consider
If you have recently mass inactivated patients from your EHR it will affect your data. It may be better to choose a larger timeframe in this case to get the most accurate reading for Net Growth.
If you like the growth report check out Dashboards > Growth. The second data field on that page allows you to see 12 months, 24 months or 36 months at a time for growth data.

articles.title: How A Patient's Recall Due Date is Calculated in Adit Using Tracker

blocks.x: Practices using Tracker as their EHR can manage their patient recalls by setting “Pending Appointments”. Pending appointments are appointments that need to be scheduled for a patient, and are set on a calendar to serve as reminders for the practice to bring that patient in.
In order to determine the recall due date in Adit’s patient card:
Adit will first check that patient’s next pending appointment in Tracker.
If there is a pending appointment scheduled, then we will use the original appointment due date listed.

Important Note: Every time a pending appointment is rescheduled, Adit will not be able to find the updated date because Tracker will only provide the original appointment date. Because of this, we recommend to delete the current pending appointment in Tracker and enter a new pending appointment with the updated date instead. This will then correctly update the due date in the patient card.
Adit will first check the patient’s next scheduled pending appointment in Tracker and look up the original date on that appointment.

If there isn’t a pending appointment found for that patient, then Adit will next check the interval set up on the patient tab. If there is an interval set up, then Adit will calculate the due date by adding that number to the patient’s last completed appointment.
If the patient doesn’t have an upcoming pending appointment, or a recall interval set up, then by default Adit will add 6 months to the last completed hygiene appointment.
Define hygiene codes based on CDA

articles.title: Managing Net/Gross Production in Practice Analytics

blocks.x: Practice analytics has two methods of showing you how to calculate production numbers:
The first way is Gross Production, which is the sum of all the production revenue.
The second way is Net Production, which is the sum of all the production revenue minus any adjustments.
All widgets that show production will have a toggle button that will let you select how you want to view these numbers.
If you want to manage which view is shown by default on all of the widgets, you can do the following:
Go to Preferences in the top Navigation bar
Click on the Set Goals Page
In the section called Production Calculations, you will see the field called: What is your preferred method to calculate production?
When the button is toggled to the right and colored orange, Gross Production will be selected.
When the button is toggled to the left and colored grey, Net production will be selected.
If your EHR/PMS is OpenDental, there will also be another field called Would you like Adit to calculate Net Production using the Procedure Date or Payment Date for Write-Offs?
Selecting Payment Date will associate the adjustment based on the date when the payment was made.
Selecting Procedure Date will associate the adjustment based on the date when the procedure was completed.
This field is important to address because it affects which production numbers get adjusted.

In Dentrix, each individual who provides billable treatment to patients is a provider. Providers appear alphabetically according to their IDs, and usually only a provider's ID is displayed and/or printed. Before setting up providers, consider the following information:
- You must assign each provider a unique, four-character, alphanumeric ID. You can use initials or other codes, such as DOC1, DDS1, HYG1, and so on.
- You cannot change a Provider ID once you set it up.
- You cannot delete providers once you create them; however, you can inactivate them.
- You can filter information according to a range of providers in certain reports. Alphabetize your providers so that you can use these ranges effectively for these reports.
- You can create up to 250 providers.
To edit a provider’s information
1. In the Office Manager, click Maintenance, point to Practice Setup, and then click Practice Resource Setup.
The Practice Resource Setup dialog box appears.
Dentrix Practice Resource Setup
2. Select the provider whose information you want to edit from the list, and click Edit.
The Provider Information dialog box appears.
Dentrix Provider Information
3. As appropriate, change one or more of the following:
- Name - Type the provider’s last and first names and middle initial.
- ID - Once you create a provider, you cannot edit the provider’s ID.
- Title - Type the provider’s professional title, such as DDS, DMD, or RDH.
- Specialty - Select the provider’s specialty from the list.
- Address - Type the provider’s business address.
- Phone - Type the provider’s business telephone number and extension.
- Assigned Operatories - Select the operatories that the provider uses most often.
- Class - Select Primary for providers, such as dentists, or Secondary for providers, such as hygienists.
- E-mail - Type the provider’s email address.
- Provider ID - Click to change the provider’s insurance ID.
- Insurance Claim Options - Select Print Provider’s Signature to avoid having to sign each printed insurance claim, and then select "Signature On File" or Provider’s Name.
- Electronic Rx User - Click to allow the provider to write prescriptions electronically.
- Fee Schedule - Click the search button to select a fee schedule different from your practice's usual fee schedule.
- SS # - Type the provider's number.
- State ID # - Type the provider’s state ID number.
- State - Type the two-digit postal code for the state the provider is licensed in.
- State License Expiration - Type the expiration date of the provider’s state license.
- TIN # - Type the provider’s Taxpayer Identification Number.
Note: The provider name, address, Social Security number, TIN, state ID number, and phone number print on insurance claims.
- Medicaid # - Type the provider’s Medicaid number.
- DEA # - Type the provider’s DEA ID number.
- DEA License Expiration - Type the expiration date of the provider’s DEA license.
- DEA Schedule - Select the appropriate schedule.
- NPI - Type the provider’s National Provider Identifier number issued by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS).
- Specialized insurance claim IDs - Select the appropriate option, and then type the appropriate claim ID.
- Provider # - Type the provider’s provider number.
- Office # - Type the provider’s office number.
- Medicare # - Type the provider’s Medicare number.
- Other ID # - Type the provider’s other insurance ID.
- UPIN # - Type the provider’s unique physician identifier number.
- Controlled Substance # - Type the provider’s controlled substance number.
4. Click OK.

blocks.x: Adit Voice makes it super easy to manage and view your missed calls, voicemails, eFaxes, and all of your notifications in one place.
How to Quickly View Your Phone Notifications.
Call Pop. When logged into the homepage of your dashboard, you can check your call logs, missed calls, voicemails, and eFaxes by simply clicking on the Call Pop Icon on the top bar.
In the Call Pop, switch between the different tabs by clicking the icons at the top. They are labeled as follows:
Please note, if you have not set up Adit Voice then the dialpad, directory, and settings icons will not show.
Voicemails. When you check a voicemail in the Call Pop, that voicemail will be marked as READ. You can then choose to ARCHIVE that voicemail by clicking the Archive button.
Faxes. The same settings apply to Faxes. When you view a Fax, it is marked as Read. You can then choose to Archive a Fax.

Call Tracking. The call tracking module can be used to listen to any recorded calls, all historical voicemails, and see all eFaxes. While Call Tracking is a great module to find all of your history and insights, it isn’t made for your daily use. We recommend the Call Pop for checking your phone notifications daily.
How to See Your Notifications When in the App
When logged into the platform, Adit makes it simple for you to constantly see all of your notifications and to-do items in one place. Here is how it works:

The What’s Happening Section. The “What’s Happening” section on your home page shows all of your unread notifications across the app. You can quickly see everything here and quickly mark things as read accordingly. There are two tabs for Practice Notifications and "My Notifications"
Practice Notifications (This is where you'll see the usual notifications for the practice like appts, forms, payments, calls, etc.)
My Notifications (this will only show user specific notifications like internal chat messages and follow ups)

Orange Dots. The orange dot represents if there are any unread items in any of your modules or calls. To view these items, simply click on the module and mark the line item as Read. These items can include:
Unread text messages (Engage module)
Unread voicemails (Call Pop)
Unread faxes (Call Pop)
Missed calls (Call Pop)
Unread form submissions by patients (Patient Forms module)
Unread appointment requests (Online Scheduling module)
Unread contact us submission (Online Scheduling module)
Unread payment received alert (Adit Pay module)
Unread payment disputes alert (Adit Pay module)
Unread Chats (Internal Chat Module)
Follow Up Due Reminders (Practice Analytics Module)
How to Be Alerted of New Notifications
Simply said, there are 4 ways to be alerted of a notification.
Desktop notifications (preferred)
Mobile notifications
Email notifications
Browser notifications (not preferred)
To understand which of these notification options best fits your daily workflows, please read below:

Desktop Notifications. We recommend that your staff set up Desktop Notifications on each of their computers. The benefit to the Desktop Notification App is that your staff can be alerted in real-time of inbound calls, missed calls, appointment requests, and so much more. To set this up, please refer to Set up desktop notifications.

Mobile Notifications. You can receive mobile notifications using Adit’s mobile app on your iPhone or Android device. This usually works well if you aren’t situated at a desk all day and need to be alerted when out of the office. (Example: emergency calls after hours or if you want to stay engaged during your lunch break). To set this up, please refer to Set up mobile notifications.

Email Notifications. You can receive notifications to your email as well from Adit. This usually works best for operations managers and doctors that want to be alerted of specific activities that may happen through the course of a day (ex: Missed Calls). Another use-case for email notifications is if your staff looks at their email inbox all day and wants to be alerted there of any new form submissions or appointment requests. To set this up, please refer to Set up email notifications.

Browser Notifications. Browser notifications are easy to set up but many times can be delayed because of different tabs and processes running on your browser. We do not recommend enabling browser notifications unless notifications are not a time-sensitive need for your daily use-case. Browser notifications are usually used by an off-site staff member that wants to stay engaged but is not responsible for picking up calls. To set up Browser notifications, please refer to Set up browser notifications.

articles.title: Understanding Task Permissions in Adit
articles.module: Tasks, Internal Chat, Notifications and Automations

blocks.x: Task permissions determine who can view, edit, and interact with tasks in the Task Module. Depending on whether a task is private, part of a project, or shared across teams, access levels will differ.
This article explains the different permission types, how private vs. project tasks work, and what happens with subtasks.
Task Accessibility Rules

rows: Task collaborators, project members, and team members
Task collaborators, project members, team members, and organization members

blocks.x: Key Permission Scenarios
Private Tasks
Only collaborators on that task can view or edit it.
If you remove someone as a collaborator, they will immediately lose access.
Tasks in a Project
If a task is added to a project, all project members gain access.
Example : A billing project where all billing team members can see and manage related tasks.
Subtasks and Visibility
If you assign a subtask to someone not added as a collaborator on the parent task, they will:
See only the subtask.
Not see the parent task (it will display as Private Task).
Note: Always add subtask assignees as collaborators on the parent task if you want them to see the full context.
Deleted Users and Task Ownership
If a user is removed from the system, their tasks will automatically be organized in a project

If a user is deleted, a new task will automatically be created with a link to the associated project. This task will be assigned to the staff member who performed the deletion, so they can review the project details and decide how to handle the deleted user’s tasks.
Step-by-Step Instructions: Adjusting Task Permissions
Open the Task you want to review.
Check Collaborators - visible in the task details sidebar.
To add/remove collaborators:
Click the “+ Add Collaborator” button.
Select or remove users as needed.
If the task is in a project, check the project’s privacy settings to confirm who else has access.
For subtasks:
Add the subtask assignee as a collaborator on the main task if visibility of the parent is required.

articles.title: Understanding the Automations Log

blocks.x: The Automations Log is your single source of truth for everything Automations does behind the scenes. It shows every automation run, its outcome, the patient involved, and the exact input and output data - giving your team full visibility, easy auditing, and quick troubleshooting.
This article walks you through how to access the Activity Log, understand the metrics and statuses, filter results, and investigate individual entries.
How to Access the Automations Log
Log in to your Adit Web account
2. Navigate to Settings (top-right corner)
3. Select Automations from the menu.
Click Automations from the left navigation menu
From the secondary menu, select Logs
The Activity Log will load with the All tab selected by default, showing every execution within the selected date range.
Automations Log Overview
The Log is organized into three sections:
Status Tabs - Quick filters by execution outcome
Dashboard Metrics - Visual summary of automation performance
Detailed Log Table - Individual entries for every automation executed
Status Tabs
At the top of the log, you'll see five tabs to filter entries by outcome:
All - Every automation execution within the date range
Success - All configured actions completed successfully
Partial Success - Some actions completed but others failed
Filtered - Patients who matched the automation but were excluded by additional filter rules
Failed - Actions not completed due to an error
Logs can also be filtered using the Search, Date Range and Filters by Automation Type.
The Detailed Log Table
Below the dashboard, you'll find a row-by-row log of every automation execution
Date & Time - Shows when the automation was executed
Automation - Type of Automation
Details - Detailed log of execution when clicked on drop down
Status - Success, Filtered, Failed or Partial Success
Input/Output - To view the underlying data sent into and returned from automation.
Role Based Access
Admin, Owner and Manager users- Can configure the automations
Staff and Read-only users- Can only view the automation.
If an automation has already executed for the day, any updates to its schedule will not apply until the next scheduled run.

articles.title: Understanding the Tasks Home Page
articles.module: Tasks, Internal Chat, Notifications and Automations

blocks.x: The Tasks feature in Adit helps practices organize, track, and complete work more efficiently. Think of it as your team’s digital to-do list - a centralized space where you can create tasks, assign them to team members, set due dates, and monitor progress.
By using the Tasks module, practices can:
Keep daily work organized and visible to the entire team.
Reduce missed follow-ups or incomplete responsibilities.
Collaborate more effectively by assigning tasks and adding comments.
Prioritize urgent items while still keeping track of long-term projects.
My Tasks Page
My Tasks is your personal to-do list. Tasks assigned to you appear here, grouped into default sections so you can triage and prioritize your work..
Default sections (auto-organized)
Recently assigned - New tasks land here first so you can review and sort them.

Do today - Tasks with a due date of today will automatically move into this section. Once a task moves into Do today, it will stay here until you manually move it - even if it becomes overdue. This ensures urgent or missed items remain visible until you take action.

Do later - Everything scheduled further out. Unlike Do today, this section does not have automation. Tasks won’t automatically move here; you will need to manually drag or assign them into this section when you want to keep them out of your immediate queue.
Notes
You can add your own sections and delete sections you created, but default sections cannot be deleted.
Drag tasks between sections, or set a Due date to help prioritization (see: Creating Tasks in Adit).
Add sections / Add tasks (from My Tasks)
+ Add Section: Creates a new list row (e.g., “Billing follow-ups”).
+ Add Task: Opens a task panel where you can name the task, assign it, set due date, link a patient, add to a project, attach files, add subtasks, etc. (see: Creating Tasks in Adit).
My Projects Page

A project is a workspace where related tasks are grouped together. Projects help teams organize work around specific goals, workflows, or initiatives. Instead of keeping everything in a single task list, you can break work into projects to track progress more clearly.
Purpose of Projects:
Organize tasks by theme (e.g., “Insurance Follow-ups,” “Marketing Campaigns,” “Outstanding Claims”).
Provide a dedicated space for collaboration so team members can see all tasks, deadlines, and updates in one place.
Use sections, filters, and custom fields to categorize and prioritize work within the project.
Ensure visibility: everyone added to a project can access the tasks and contribute, making it easier to track ownership and accountability.
Click Projects (left sidebar) to see projects you’re a member of.
What you will see:
+ Add Project (top left) - create a new project.
Search Project (top right) - quickly find an existing project.
Project list - Name and Members for each project.
Inside a project
When you open a project you’ll find:
+ Add Task - create a task within the project.
+ Add Section - group tasks (e.g., “Call today,” “Call next week”).
Customize - add custom fields (dropdowns, text, etc.) to your project table.
Search Tasks, Filter, Table Settings - tools to find and format task lists.
Project actions (three-dot menu):
Edit project details
Set color
Copy project link
Delete project
Search, Filter, Table settings & Column width
Search
Use the Search Tasks bar (top right of the list) to find tasks by name or keywords.
Filter
Click Filter to narrow results. Common filters:
Assignee
Due date range (Today, Next 7 days, etc.)
Project / Section
Custom fields (when available)
You can stack multiple filters and clear them any time.
Table Settings
Click Table Settings to:
Show/hide columns (e.g., Due date, Assignee, Patient, Collaborators, Created By, custom fields).
Reorder columns (drag to position).
Pin columns to keep them sticky while scrolling.
Adjusting column width
Hover the column header edge and drag to resize.
Or open Table Settings and reorder/show/hide columns to create a cleaner layout before resizing.
Step-by-step: Common actions
View your projects
Go to Tasks > Projects.
Use Search Project to find a project, or click + Add Project to create a new one.
Open a project and add work
Click a Project name to open it.
Click + Add Task to create a task inside the project.
Click + Add Section to create a grouping row; it’s added immediately.
(Optional) Click ⋯ (three dots) > Edit project details to rename or update privacy; Set color for quick visual ID; Copy project link to share; or Delete project if needed.
Customize fields (per project)
Inside the project, click Customize.
To edit an existing field: click the field name, update the Field Title and Field Type (e.g., Single-select or Text), and Save.
To add a new field: click + Add Field, choose Field Title and Field Type.
For Single-select fields, click + Add an option, name each option, and (optionally) choose a color. Click Save.
Your new field appears as a column; if you don’t see it, open Table Settings and make sure it’s visible.
Search, filter, and format your view
Use the Search Tasks box to find items quickly.
Click Filter to narrow by assignee, due date, project, section, and custom fields.
Click Table Settings to show/hide or reorder columns.
Drag column edges to resize for readability.
Triage new tasks on My Tasks
Open My Tasks.
Check Recently assigned at the top.
Drag items to Do today, Do next week, or Do later, or set a Due date.
Create custom sections if needed (e.g., “Urgent calls”).
Related articles to link
Creating Tasks in Adit - how to add assignees, due dates, patients, attachments, subtasks, approvals, and mark complete.
Subtasks - how to break work into smaller pieces (and how permissions work when the subtask assignee isn’t a collaborator on the parent task).
Merging Duplicate Tasks - how to merge, what data is preserved, and who gets notified.
Working with Projects - creating/editing projects, privacy, members, and examples (e.g., “Patients to call today/next week,” “Outstanding claims”).

blocks.x:
The Tasks Module in Adit helps practices organize work, assign responsibilities, and track progress in real time. Think of it as your team’s digital to-do list - integrated
with patient and project workflows.

From Within a Task

Merging Duplicate Tasks

Collaborators and Notifications
Add Collaborators (+)

Filters, Search & Table Settings

If a task is private (not in a project), only collaborators can view it.

blocks.x: When a user is removed from your organization in Adit, their assigned tasks don’t get deleted. Instead, Adit reassigns and organizes them to ensure that no important work is lost. This article explains what happens to deleted users’ tasks and how to manage them.
What Happens When a User Is Deleted?
When a user is deleted from your organization in Adit:
● All open tasks previously assigned to that user remain active
● Adit automatically creates a new project titled: "[User Name]’s Previously Assigned Tasks"
● This project helps you to:
○ Quickly access the deleted user’s tasks
○ Review their tasks in one place
○ Reassign or complete them as needed
Note: Tasks in this project are not deleted or completed. They remain open until manually updated.
Where to Find These Tasks
To access a deleted user’s tasks:
Go to the Tasks module from the left navigation panel.
Click on the Projects tab.
Search for the project titled: "[User Name]’s Previously Assigned Tasks"
Open the project to view all tasks that were previously assigned to the deleted user.
Once you have located the project, here’s what you can do to clean it up: complete any finished tasks, or reassign them to other team members for follow-up.
Completing a Task
To mark a task as completed:
Open the task by clicking on it from any list or project view.
Click the checkbox next to the task name or at the top of the task details panel.
The task will be marked as Completed, but it will still remain visible for reference within the project.
Reassigning a Task
To reassign a task to another team member:
Open the task from the “Previously Assigned Tasks” project or task list.
In the task details panel, locate the Assignee field.
Click the current value (which will likely show as “Unassigned”).
Select the new team member from the dropdown list.
Changes are saved automatically.
Deleting a Task
If you want to manually delete a task, follow these steps:
Open the Task Module: Go to the left sidebar and click on Tasks.
Click on My Tasks: Select My Tasks to view your personal task list.
Select the Task to delete: Click on the task you want to delete (e.g., “Test”). Task details will appear on the right-hand side.
Click More options: In the task detail view, click on the More (⋯) icon at the top.
Choose Delete Task: From the dropdown menu, click Delete Task.
Confirm Deletion: A confirmation pop-up will appear. Click Delete Task to permanently delete it.
Best Practices
● Always review the “Previously Assigned Tasks” project after a user is deleted. This ensures tasks are reassigned appropriately.
● Use the Unassigned Tasks filter in the Tasks module to quickly locate and redistribute work.
● Avoid deleting tasks unless they are duplicates or irrelevant, as deleted tasks cannot be recovered.

articles.title: How to Set Up Automations
articles.module: Tasks, Internal Chat, Notifications and Automations

blocks.x: Adit's Automations feature is a smarter way to keep your practice on top of every patient follow-up. Automations automatically create follow-up reminders for your team based on rules you configure per location, so your staff always knows which patients to reach out to and when. Set it up once, and Automations runs quietly in the background every day, surfacing the right follow-ups at the right time.
How Automation Rules Work
Every automation is built from three parts: WHEN it runs, CONDITIONS for who qualifies, and ACTIONS for what happens next.
WHEN (Trigger)
Defines the timing that tells Adit when to evaluate patients against the rule. This is usually time-based, for example:
A set amount of time before or after an appointment (e.g., 48 hours before the scheduled appointment)
A recurring schedule (e.g., every day at 9:00 AM)
The exact trigger options depend on the automation type. See each use case below for specifics.
CONDITIONS (Who Qualifies)
Defines which patients the automation should flag. Common filters include:
Patient status (active, inactive, or both)
Patient type
Procedure codes
Balance thresholds
Appointment conditions
Provider
Please note that the available conditions change depending on the automation type. See each use case below for specifics.
ACTIONS (What Happens)

Once a patient matches the trigger and conditions, choose one or more actions for Adit to take. You can combine multiple actions on a single automation (for example, create a task and send a chat message). These four actions are available across every automation type:
Create a Task
Adit generates a task automatically whenever a patient matches the automation's criteria. No manual entry required.
Task Name
Name the task using free text and dynamic fields.
Example: "Call #PatientName - Unconfirmed Appt"
Assignee
The task is auto-assigned to the staff member you select, so there's no need to manually assign tasks as they're created.
Due Date
Set when the task should be completed by.
Project
Optionally associate the task with an existing project, so it's grouped with related work.
Description
Auto-populate the task with the specific patient's details, so whoever picks it up has everything they need to act right away, without looking up the patient's record.
Create a Follow Up
Adit generates a follow-up entry automatically whenever a patient matches the automation's criteria.
Assignee
Select the staff member the follow-up should be associated with. This is a required field.
Send an Internal Chat
Adit posts a message to an internal group chat automatically whenever a patient matches the automation's criteria.
Group Chat
Select the internal group chat that should receive the notification. The group chat must already exist in Adit; you can search for it by name.
Message
Write the message template with the details your team needs.
Message Preview

The right panel shows a live preview of exactly how the message will appear once sent, with dynamic fields populated with real patient data. Messages are sent from Adit Automations, so your team can easily identify automation-generated notifications in the chat.
Send an Email Notification
Adit sends an email automatically whenever a patient matches the automation's criteria.
Assignee(s)
Select one or more staff members to receive the email. This is a required field.
Subject
Enter the subject line for the email.
Body
Write the email body with the details your team needs.
Email Preview
The right panel shows a live preview of the branded email exactly as staff will receive it, with dynamic fields populated with real patient data.
Note: Follow Ups created through automations appear in the Practice Analytics module.
Navigating Automations
Log in to your Adit Web account.
Navigate to Settings (top-right corner).
Select Automations from the menu.
4. You'll land on the Automations list view, where you can use the All, Active, and Inactive tabs at the top to filter automations by status.

How to Select an Automation to Configure
1. From the Automations page, browse the list of available automations (Unconfirmed Appointment, Incomplete Form, Hygiene Recare, etc.).
2. Use the All / Active / Inactive tabs to filter the view if needed:
All shows every automation available to your location.
Active shows only automations currently turned on.
Inactive shows automations that are turned off or not yet configured.

3. Locate the automation you want to set up (e.g., Unconfirmed Appointment).
4. Click the Edit (pencil) icon on the right side of that automation's card to open its configuration.
5. Click Save to store your configuration, then use the toggle switch on the automation card to activate it. The toggle turns orange when the automation is active.
Note: Only Owner and Manager level users can configure automations. Staff and Read-only users can view but not edit.
Available Automations
Below are the available automation rules
Unconfirmed Appointment
Automatically follow up on patients who haven't confirmed an upcoming appointment, so no one falls through the cracks before their visit.
When: The amount of time prior to the scheduled appointment (e.g., 48 hours)
Conditions: Both active and inactive patients, or filter to just one
Actions: Create a Task, Create Follow Up, Send an Internal Chat, Send an Email Notification (see Actions section above for full details)
Incomplete Form
Automatically follow up on patients with an incomplete form ahead of their appointment, so your team can reach out before they arrive.
When: The amount of time prior to the scheduled appointment (e.g., 24 hours)
Conditions:
Patient type: both active and inactive patients, or filter to just one
Appointment details (optional, add one or more):
Appointment type
Treatment codes on the appointment
Provider on the appointment
Actions: Create a Task, Create Follow Up, Send an Internal Chat, Send an Email Notification (see Actions section above for full details)
Hygiene Recare
Automatically follow up on unscheduled patients who are approaching their hygiene due date, so your team can reach out before the gap in care grows.

When: Set how much time before or after the patient's hygiene due date the automation should trigger. Choose a time frame in days, weeks, or months, and whether it should run before or after the due date.
Conditions: Patient type: both active and inactive patients, or filter to just one
Actions: Create a Task, Create Follow Up, Send an Internal Chat, Send an Email Notification (see Actions section above for full details)
Due Date Recall
Automatically follow up on unscheduled patients who are approaching their recall due date, so your team can reach out before the gap in care grows.
When: Set how much time before or after the patient's due date the automation should trigger. Choose a time frame in days, weeks, or months, and whether it should run before or after the due date.
Conditions: Patient type: both active and inactive patients, or filter to just one
Actions: Create a Task, Create Follow Up, Send an Internal Chat, Send an Email Notification (see Actions section above for full details)
Unscheduled Broken Appointment
Automatically follow up on patients who are unscheduled after breaking an appointment, so they don't fall out of the schedule entirely.
When: Set how much time after the patient's broken appointment the automation should trigger. Choose a time frame in days, weeks, or months.
Conditions: Patient type: both active and inactive patients, or filter to just one
Actions: Create a Task, Create Follow Up, Send an Internal Chat, Send an Email Notification (see Actions section above for full details)
Unscheduled Treatment
Automatically follow up on patients with unscheduled treatment after completing an appointment, so recommended treatment doesn't go unbooked.
When: Set how long after the patient's completed appointment the automation should trigger. Choose a time frame in days, weeks, or months.
Conditions:
Patient type: both active and inactive patients, or filter to just one
Unscheduled treatment dollar amount: trigger only when the unscheduled treatment total is above a set dollar amount
Treatment codes: select which unscheduled treatment codes to consider (multi-select)
Actions: Create a Task, Create Follow Up, Send an Internal Chat, Send an Email Notification (see Actions section above for full details)
Past Due Balance
Automatically follow up on patients with a past due balance, so outstanding balances get worked instead of sitting untouched.
When: Choose one of two trigger types:
Daily: Trigger this automation every day at a specific time you select.
Aging Period: Trigger this automation once a patient's balance reaches a set aging period: 0 to 30 days, 31 to 60 days, or 61 to 90 days.
Conditions:
Patient type: both active and inactive patients, or filter to just one
Patient balance: trigger only when the balance is above a set dollar amount
Appointment status: trigger only when the patient's appointment matches a selected status (only available with the Daily trigger)

Example: A patient has a completed appointment that day and still has an overdue balance above $50. With the Daily trigger set to check for completed appointments and a balance threshold of $50, the automation triggers.
Actions: Create a Task, Create Follow Up, Send an Internal Chat, Send an Email Notification (see Actions section above for full details)
Past Due Claims
Automatically follow up on unpaid claims, so nothing sits past due without your team noticing.
When: Assuming a claim is unpaid, set how long after the submitted date the automation should trigger. Choose a time frame in days, weeks, or months.
Conditions: Patient type: both active and inactive patients, or filter to just one
Actions: Create a Task, Create Follow Up, Send an Internal Chat, Send an Email Notification (see Actions section above for full details)
Note: Hygiene Recare and Past Due Claims are only available on the Analytics Bundle

articles.title: Set up Browser Notifications
articles.module: Tasks, Internal Chat, Notifications and Automations

blocks.x: Browser notifications are easy to set up but many times can be delayed because of different tabs and processes running on your browser.

We do not recommend enabling browser notifications unless notifications are not a time-sensitive need for your daily use-case. Browser notifications are usually used by an off-site staff member that wants to stay engaged but is not responsible for picking up calls.
Here is how to set up browser notifications:
Click on the Bell icon on the top right corner
Toggle on Browser Notifications

Next you will need to ensure that browser notifications are enabled on your browser. To do this, in the address bar of your web browser, click on the toggle icon. A menu will appear, you will see toggle options for notifications and pop ups and redirects. Make sure both are toggled on.
Next you will need to enable notifications on your computer. To do this:
Select the Windows icon on your computer
Search for notifications
Select “Notifications and actions” setting
Scroll down until you find the web browser you use (ex: Google Chrome, Mozilla, Firefox, Microsoft Edge, etc.)
Turn the toggle to “On”

blocks.x: To set up a email notifications:
Click on the Settings gear icon in the top right corner of your Adit platform.
In the My Profile menu, click Notifications
Based on the type of email notification you would like to receive, click on Add Notification in that section.
In the pop up, you can then set the notifications based on your particular preferences.
Below is a list of the type of email notifications you can set up:
Call Tracking
All calls: whenever your practice receives a call
All missed calls: whenever your practice misses a call
Voicemails: whenever you have a voicemail
eFax Delivery Failure: in the event, a fax has gone undelivered
eFax Delivery Success: in the event, a fax was delivered successfully
eFax Failed to Receive: in the event, you did not receive a fax because of an error.

Missed Opportunities: for those who are in Adit’s marketing program, you can set these notifications to alert you when a potential opportunity on an inbound call was not converted. (ex: patient called in to book an emergency appointment, but there was no availability).
Coaching Opportunities: for those who are in Adit’s marketing program, you can set these notifications to be alerted whenever Adit marks a call as a potential coaching opportunity for your staff.
Online Scheduling
Appointment Request: whenever a patient books an appointment
Pozative
Positive Reviews: when your practice receives a new positive review online.
Negative Reviews: when your practice receives a negative review online.
Feedback Review: when a patient has not left a review online but provided feedback through your feedback form.
Engage
Incoming Text Message: whenever your practice receives a text message

articles.title: How to use Internal Chat
articles.module: Tasks, Internal Chat, Notifications and Automations

blocks.x: In this help article, we will show you how to use the Internal Chat module so you can start using it for your team communication.
Here are the features:
Creating a Chat Pop Up
In the top right of the chat thread, click on the chat box button.
This will create a pop up for the chat thread you are one, allowing you to leave the module while still being able to continue chatting.
You can minimize the chat pop up, by clicking on the - icon. This will create a chat bubble in the bottom right corner, where you can click on the bubble to reopen the chat pop up.
If you click on the icon with arrow, it will open the chat thread in a new tab.
Search Feature
You are able to search for users by using the search bar on the left panel.
You are able to search for messages in the chat thread by clicking on the magnifying glass icon.
Marking as Unread
On a message you received, click on the arrow and select Unread from here.
Messages from that point, will now be considered unread and will have the number of unread messages on the left side panel.
Add to Favorites
On the top right of the chat thread, click on the three dots and click on Add to Favorites.
This will create a new section on the left side panel called FAVORITES and these chats will always remain on the top, over the recent chats.
Clearing Chat
On the top right of the chat thread, click on the three dots and click on Clear Chat.
Read the message in the popup, and click on Yes to confirm the removal of all messages in the chat.
Mute Notifications
On the top right of the chat thread, click on the three dots and click on Mute.
Muted chats will have a crossed out speaker icon next to them in the left side panel.
To unmute a chat: On the top right of the chat thread, click on the three dots and click on Unmute.
